In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. And may Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and grant them peace. [Addition from manuscript T.]

Tafsir (exegesis) of Surat al-Isra' [In manuscripts T, F, and A: "Surat Subhan".]

It is Meccan.

Imam al-Hafiz al-Mutqin Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari said: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid say: I heard Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, say concerning Bani Isra'il, al-Kahf, and Maryam: "They are among the first of my old treasures, and they are from my ancient possessions." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4708.]

And Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Marwan, from Abu Lubabah, who said: I heard 'A'ishah say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fast until we would say, 'He does not intend to break his fast,' and he would break his fast until we would say, 'He does not intend to fast.' And he used to recite Bani Isra'il and al-Zumar every night." [Al-Musnad 6/189. Ibn Khuzaymah also narrated it in his Sahih, no. 1163, and said: "If this Abu Lubabah is one whose report may be used as evidence, then I do not know him to be of established integrity, and there is no harm." Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy.]

Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.

* *

He exalts Himself and magnifies His status, because of His power over what no one other than Him can do; there is no god but Him. ﴿Who took His servant by night﴾, meaning Muhammad (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him), ﴿by night﴾, that is, in the dark part of the night, ﴿from the Sacred Mosque﴾, which is the Mosque of Makkah, ﴿to the Farthest Mosque﴾, which is Bayt al-Maqdis, which is Iliya', the source of the prophets from the time of Ibrahim the Friend (of Allah). For this reason they were all gathered for him there, and he led them in prayer in their place and their home. This indicates that he is the greatest Imam and the foremost Leader (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon all of them).

* *

His saying: ﴿The one whom We blessed around it﴾, that is, with crops and fruits. ﴿So that We might show him﴾, that is, Muhammad, ﴿of Our signs﴾, that is, the great ones, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾ [al-Najm: 18].

We will mention some of what the Sunnah has reported of hadiths about this from him (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him).

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, that is, the All-Hearing of the words of His servants, believers and disbelievers, those who affirm and those who deny, the All-Seeing of them, so He gives each what he deserves in this world and the Hereafter.

Mention of the hadiths reported concerning the Isra' (night journey)

Narrated by Anas ibn Malik:

Imam Abu 'Abd Allah al-Bukhari said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, Sulayman, that is, Ibn Bilal, narrated to us, from Sharik ibn 'Abd Allah [In F: "'Abd Allah, meaning Ibn Abi Namir, that he".], who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say on the night the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the journey from the mosque of the Ka'bah: "Three men came to him before revelation came to him, while he was sleeping in the Sacred Mosque. The first of them said, 'Which one is he?' The middle one said, 'He is the best of them.' The last of them said, 'Take the best of them.' That was the night, and he did not see them until they came to him on another night, when his heart saw them, while his eyes were sleeping and his heart was not sleeping; and so it is with the prophets, their eyes sleep but their hearts do not sleep. They did not speak to him until they carried him and placed him by the well of Zamzam. Jibril took charge of him from among them, and Jibril split open what was between his throat and his lower chest until he had emptied his chest and his abdomen. Then he washed it with water from Zamzam, with his own hand, until he had cleansed his inside. Then a golden basin was brought to him, containing a golden vessel filled with faith and wisdom, and he filled his chest and his throat-veins, that is, the veins of his throat, with it, and then he sealed it. Then he ascended with him to the lowest heaven, and he struck one of its gates, and the people of the heaven called out: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' They said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'With me is Muhammad.' They said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'Welcome to him, and he is welcome; the people of the heaven rejoice in him. The people of the heaven do not know what Allah intends for the earth until He informs them.'"

In the lowest heaven he found Adam, and Jibril said to him: "This is your father Adam; greet him." So he greeted him, and Adam returned the greeting and said: "Welcome, my son, what a good son you are!" Then he saw in the lowest heaven two rivers flowing, and he said: "What are these two rivers, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the Nile and the Euphrates, and this is their source." Then he continued with him into the heaven, and there he saw another river upon which was a palace of pearls and emerald. He struck his hand into it and found it to be musk of strong fragrance. He said: "What is this, O Jibril?" He said: "This is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept hidden for you."

Then he ascended to the second heaven, and the angels said to him the same as the first had said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." They said: "And who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent for?" He said: "Yes." They said: "Welcome [In F: "Welcome to him"], and he is welcome and at ease."

Then he ascended with him to the third heaven, and they said to him the same as the first and second had said. Then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, and they said the same. Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, and they said the same. In every heaven there were prophets whom he named; I have memorized from them Idris in the second, Harun in the fourth, another in the fifth whose name I did not retain, Ibrahim in the sixth, and Musa in the seventh, by the preference of Allah's speech. Musa said: "My Lord, I did not think that anyone would be raised above me." Then he rose with him above that, to a place known only to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and the Compeller, the Lord of Might, drew near and descended, until he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer. Then Allah revealed to him what He revealed: fifty prayers upon your nation each day and night. Then he descended with him until he reached Musa, and Musa detained him and said: "O Muhammad, what did your Lord enjoin upon you?" He said: "He enjoined upon me fifty prayers each day and night." He said: "Indeed your nation cannot bear that. Return, and let your Lord lighten it for you and for them." So the Prophet (ﷺ) turned to Jibril, as if seeking his counsel in this, and Jibril gestured to him: Yes, if you wish. So he ascended with him to the Compeller, the Exalted, and he said while in his place: "My Lord, lighten it for us, for my nation cannot bear this." So He removed ten prayers from him. Then he returned to Musa, who detained him, and Musa kept sending him back to his Lord until it became five prayers. Then Musa detained him at the five and said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, I tried with the Children of Israel, my people, for something less than this, and they grew weak and abandoned it. Your nation is weaker in bodies, hearts, bodies, sight and hearing. Return, and let your Lord lighten it for you." Each time the Prophet (ﷺ) turned to Jibril to seek his advice, and Jibril did not dislike that. So he raised him at the fifth and said: "My Lord, my nation is weak in their bodies, their hearts and their hearing [In F, A: "and their hearing, their sight and their bodies"] and their bodies, so lighten it for us." The Compeller said: "O Muhammad." He said: "Here I am at Your service, and at Your pleasure." He said: "Indeed the word is not changed with Me, just as I have enjoined upon you in the Mother of the Book: every good deed is rewarded tenfold, so they are fifty in the Mother of the Book, and they are five for you." So he returned to Musa and said: "How did you fare?" He said: "He lightened it for us; He gave us ten times the reward for every good deed." Musa said: "By Allah, I tried with the Children of Israel for something less than that, and they abandoned it. Return to your Lord, and let Him lighten it for you as well." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Musa, by Allah, I have become shy before my Lord for what I keep going back to Him about." He said: "Then descend in the name of Allah." Then he awoke, and he was in the Sacred Mosque.

This is how al-Bukhari transmitted it in the "Book of Tawhid" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7517]. He also narrated it in "The Description of the Prophet (ﷺ)", from Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from his brother Abu Bakr 'Abd al-Hamid, from Sulayman ibn Bilal [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3570].

Muslim narrated it from Harun ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Wahb, from Sulayman [In F, A: "Sulayman, to him"], who said: "He added and omitted, and advanced and postponed" [Sahih Muslim, no. 162].

And it is as Muslim, may Allah have mercy on him, said, for Sharik ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir was inconsistent in this hadith, his memory was poor, and he did not preserve it accurately, as will be explained in the other hadiths.

Some people regard this as a dream that paved the way for what occurred afterward, and Allah knows best.

[And] [Addition from manuscript T.] al-Bayhaqi said: In the hadith of Sharik there is an addition that he alone narrated, which supports the view of those who claim that he (ﷺ) saw his Lord; that is, his saying: "Then the Compeller, the Lord of Might, drew near and descended, so that he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer." He said: The statements of 'A'ishah, Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Hurayrah, in interpreting these verses as referring to his seeing Jibril, are more authentic [Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi 2/385].

What al-Bayhaqi said is the truth on this question, for Abu Dharr said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you see your Lord?" He said: "There is light; how could I see Him?" And in another narration: "I saw light." Muslim narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him [Sahih Muslim, no. 178].

[The author's words have been abridged due to their great length.]

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned that He had taken His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) on the night journey, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, He followed it with the mention of Musa (Moses), His servant and Kalim (the one who spoke with Allah), peace be upon him. Allah, the Exalted, often links the mention of Musa and Muhammad, peace be upon them, and the mention of the Torah and the Qur'an. For this reason, after mentioning the Night Journey, He said: ﴿And We gave Musa the Book﴾, meaning the Torah, ﴿and We made it﴾, meaning the Book, ﴿a guidance﴾, meaning a guide, ﴿for the Children of Israel, [saying], "Do not take other than Me as a disposer of affairs"﴾, meaning, lest you take other than Me as a protector, a helper, or a deity. This is because Allah, the Exalted, revealed to every prophet He sent that he should worship Him alone, with no partner.

Then He said: ﴿O descendants of those We carried with Nuh﴾. Its implied meaning is: "O descendants of those whom We carried with Nuh." This contains an incitement and a reminder of the favour, meaning: O offspring of those whom We saved and carried with Nuh in the ship. Emulate your father, ﴿for he was a grateful servant﴾. So remember, you, My blessing upon you by sending Muhammad (ﷺ) to you.

It has been narrated in a hadith and in a report from the early generations (al-Salaf, the righteous predecessors) that Nuh, peace be upon him, used to praise Allah, [the Exalted], for his food, his drink, his clothing and all his affairs. For this reason he was called "a grateful servant."

Al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi, who said: Nuh was only called "a grateful servant" because whenever he ate or drank, he praised Allah. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/32)]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Usama narrated to us, Zakariya ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Burda, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel or drinks a sip and then praises Allah for it."

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in this same way, through the chain of Abu Usama. [Al-Musnad (3/117), Sahih Muslim no. (2734), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1816), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (6899)]

Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: He used to praise Allah in every state.

Al-Bukhari also mentioned here the hadith of Abu Zur'a, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the leader of mankind on the Day of Resurrection," and in it: "They will come to Nuh and say: 'O Nuh, you are the first of the Messengers to the people of the earth, and Allah has named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord.'" He mentioned the hadith in full. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4712)]

Allah, the Exalted, says: He decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book, meaning: He informed them in the Scripture He revealed to them that they would cause corruption on the earth twice and would become exceedingly arrogant, meaning they would tyrannize, transgress and commit wrongdoing against people. [In one manuscript: "wa-latu'allunna" ("and you will surely become arrogant").] As Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We decreed to him that matter, that the last trace of these would be cut off by morning﴾ [al-Hijr: 66], meaning: We informed him of it and made him aware of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when the promise of the first of the two came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might﴾, meaning: the first of the two corruptions. ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours of great might﴾, meaning: We gave power over you to an army from Our creation, possessed of great might, that is, strength, equipment and mighty authority. ﴿And they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾, meaning: they took over your lands and passed through the midst of your houses, that is, between them and through their centre, going and coming without fearing anyone.

The exegetes of the early and later generations have differed about who these were that were given power over them. From Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah: it was Goliath (Jalut) of al-Jazar and his army. He was given power over them first, then they were given victory over him afterwards, and Dawud (David) killed Goliath. For this reason He said: ﴿Then We gave back to you the return of victory over them and aided you with wealth and sons and made you greater in manpower﴾.

From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: it was the king of Mosul, Sinjarib, and his army. And also from him, and from others: it was Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), king of Babylon.

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned about him a wondrous story concerning how he rose from one state to another until he became king of the lands, and that he had been a poor, paralysed, weak man who begged people and asked them for food; then his condition led to what it led to, and that he marched to the lands of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and killed a great number of the Children of Israel there.

Ibn Jarir narrated in this place a hadith that he traced back to Hudhayfah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), a lengthy one. It is undoubtedly a fabricated (mawdu') hadith, and no one with even a little knowledge of hadith would doubt it! The utmost wonder is how it passed unnoticed by him, despite his eminence and the greatness of his rank! Our teacher, the memorizer and scholar Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated that it is fabricated and false, and he wrote that on the margin of the book.

Many Israelite reports have been transmitted on this subject, which I have not seen fit to lengthen the book by mentioning; for some of them are fabricated, put forward by some of their heretics, and some of them may possibly be sound, but we are free of them, all praise be to Allah. In what Allah, the Exalted, has related to us in His Book there is sufficiency beyond the rest of the earlier books, and neither Allah nor His Messenger has made us in need of them. Allah, the Exalted, has informed us that when they transgressed and exceeded bounds, Allah gave their enemy power over them, so he violated their sanctuary, passed through the midst of their homes, humiliated and subdued them, as a fitting recompense; and your Lord does not wrong the servants. They had rebelled and killed a number of prophets and scholars.

Ibn Jarir narrated: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: Bukhtnassar prevailed over the Levant, destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis and killed them. Then he came to Damascus and found there blood boiling on a stone (kiba), so he asked them: "What is this blood?" They said: "We found our fathers upon this." Whenever the blood was dominated by the stone, it rose. He said: So he killed seventy thousand, Muslims and others, upon that blood, and it calmed.

This report is sound up to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and this is the well-known account: that he killed their nobles and scholars, until no one remained who could memorize the Torah; he took with him a number of them as captives, including sons of prophets and others, and events occurred whose mention would be lengthy. Had we found something sound or close to it, its writing and transmission would have been permissible. And Allah knows best.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is against yourselves﴾, meaning: then it is against them, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself﴾ [Fussilat: 46].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter came﴾, meaning: the last time, that is, when you corrupted the second time and your enemies came ﴿to disfigure your faces﴾, meaning: to humiliate you and subdue you; ﴿and to enter the masjid﴾, meaning Bayt al-Maqdis, ﴿as they entered it the first time﴾, meaning: as in the time when they went through the homes; ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction﴾, meaning: to ruin and devastate what they had overcome. ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾, meaning: He will turn them away from you. ﴿But if you return [to corruption], We will return [to punishment]﴾, meaning: whenever you return to corruption, ﴿We will return﴾ to giving them power over you in this world, along with what We have stored up for you in the Hereafter of punishment and retribution. For this reason He said: ﴿And We have made Hell a confinement for the disbelievers﴾, meaning: a place of residence, a prison, and an enclosure from which there is no escape for them.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: ﴿Hasiran﴾ means a prison.

Mujahid said: "They will be confined therein." So said others as well.

Al-Hasan said: "A bed and a cushion."

Qatadah said: "The Children of Israel have returned to it, so Allah gave power over them to this group, Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, who take the jizyah from them with humiliation, while they are abased."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us of man's hastiness and of how, at times, he prays against himself, his child, or his property for evil, meaning death, destruction, ruin, a curse, and the like. Had Allah answered him as he asks, he would have been destroyed by his own supplication, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them﴾ [Yunus: 11]. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah interpreted it in the same way. It has already been mentioned in the hadith: "Do not invoke curses upon yourselves, nor upon your children, nor upon your property, lest you coincide with a moment from Allah in which He answers whatever is asked of Him."

What drives the son of Adam to this is his haste and anxiety. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And man has ever been hasty﴾.

Here Salman al-Farisi and Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) mention the story of Adam (peace be upon him), when he tried to stand up before the soul reached his feet. The breath came to him from the direction of his head. When it reached his brain, he sneezed and said, "Al-hamdu lillah" (All praise is for Allah). Allah said, "May your Lord have mercy on you, O Adam." When it reached his eyes, he opened them. When it spread into his limbs and body, he began to look at himself and was pleased with it, so he tried to stand up before the soul reached his feet, but he could not, and he said, "O Lord, hasten [the soul] before the night."

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim*, commentary on Surah 17, verse 12:

God, exalted is He, bestows favour upon His creation through His great signs. Among them is His alternation of night and day, so that they may rest at night and disperse during the day for their livelihoods (*ma'ayish*), crafts (*sina'at*), works, and journeys. Also so that they may know the number of days, weeks (*jumu'*), months, and years, and recognise the passing of the appointed terms (*ajal*) set for debts, acts of worship, transactions, leases, and other matters. For this reason He said: ﴿That you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾, meaning in your livelihoods, your journeys, and the like, ﴿and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾. For if time were one unchanging course and a uniform pattern, none of that would be known. As God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If God made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you light? Will you not then listen?" Say: "Have you considered? If God made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?" But out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [Al-Qasas: 71–73]. He also said: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon, and He it is who made the night and the day succeeding one another, for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾ [Al-Furqan: 61–62]. He said: ﴿And His is the alternation of night and day﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 80]. He said: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term. Is He not the Mighty, the Forgiving?﴾ [Al-Zumar: 5]. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Splitter of the dawn, and He made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿A sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs to its resting place. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 37–38].

Then God made for the night a sign (*aya*), meaning a mark by which it is recognised, namely darkness and the appearance of the moon within it. And for the day He made a mark, namely light and the rising of the bright sun within it. He also differentiated between the light of the moon and the brilliance of the sun, so that one may be distinguished from the other, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. God did not create that except in truth﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Surely in that are signs for a people who fear God﴾ [Yunus: 5–6]. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: "They are times set for people and for the pilgrimage"﴾, and so on [Al-Baqarah: 189].

Ibn Juraij said, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir, concerning His words ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day to give sight﴾: "The darkness of the night and the *sudfah* (the dim, shadowy blend of light and dark) of the day."

Ibn Juraij also said, on the authority of Mujahid: "The sun is the sign of the day and the moon is the sign of the night." Regarding ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾ he said: "It is the blackness that is in the moon, and God created it so."

Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Abbas said: "The moon used to shine as the sun shines, and the moon is the sign of the night and the sun is the sign of the day." Regarding ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾ he said: "It is the blackness that is in the moon."

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) has narrated through multiple sound chains: that Ibn al-Kawwa' asked Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is this smudge that is on the moon?" He said: "Woe to you! Do you not read the Qur'an? ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾. This is its effacement."

Qatadah said concerning His words ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾: "We used to be told that the effacement of the sign of the night is the blackness of the moon that is in it. And ﴿We made the sign of the day to give sight﴾ means luminous. The creation of the sun is brighter than the moon and greater."

Ibn Abi Najih said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾: "The night and the day, as God, mighty and majestic, created them."

The Most High says, after mentioning time and what occurs in it of the deeds of the children of Adam: ﴿And We have fastened to every person's neck his bird [of fortune or misfortune]﴾. His "bird" (ṭā'ir) is what flies away from him of his deeds, as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: good and evil, which he is bound to and for which he is recompensed. ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 99:7–8]. He also said: ﴿[One sits] on the right and on the left, attentive. He utters no word but that there is with him a watchful observer, ready﴾ [Qaf 50:17–18]. He said: ﴿But indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do. Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ [al-Infitar 82:10–14]. He said: ﴿You are only recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Tur 52:16], and He said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:123].

The point is that the deeds of the son of Adam are preserved for him, little and much, and are recorded for him by night and by day, morning and evening.

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, the bird of every person is at his neck." Ibn Lahi'ah said: meaning the omen (ṭayrah) [[Al-Musnad (3/360). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/49): "In it is Ibn Lahi'ah, whose narrations are good but有 some weakness, and the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]].

This statement from Ibn Lahi'ah concerning the interpretation of this hadith is very strange, and Allah knows best.

His saying [Exalted is He] [[Addition from manuscript T.]]: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find laid open﴾, meaning: We will gather for him all his deeds in a record that will be given to him on the Day of Resurrection, either in his right hand if he is among the fortunate, or in his left hand if he is among the wretched. ﴿Laid open﴾ means open, which he and others will read, containing all his deeds from the beginning of his life to its end. ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant﴾ [al-Isra' 17:14]. ﴿It will be said to the human being on that Day what he sent ahead and kept back. Rather, the human being, against himself, will be a witness, even if he presents his excuses﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:13–15]. For this reason He said: ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant﴾, meaning: you know that you were not wronged, and nothing was recorded against you except what you did, because you have recalled all that proceeded from you, and no one forgets anything of what came from him. Every person reads his record, whether literate or illiterate.

* *

His saying [Exalted is He] [[Addition from manuscript T.]]: ﴿We have fastened to his neck his bird﴾. He mentioned the neck only because it is a limb that has no counterpart in the body, and whoever is fastened with something there has no escape from it, as the poet said [[It is Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh, and the verses are in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/500).]]:

"Take it, take it... You have been given it like the collar of the dove..."

Qatadah said, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him [[In manuscript F and A: "with them both".]], from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no contagion and no omen (ṭayrah), and 'We have fastened to every person his bird at his neck.'" This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/39).]].

Imam 'Abd ibn Humayd, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated it in his Musnad with a continuous chain (muttasil), saying: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]], who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The bird of every servant is at his neck" [[Al-Muntakhab of 'Abd ibn Humayd, no. 1053.]].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abd Allah [ibn al-Mubarak] narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Yazid told me that Abu al-Khayr told him that he heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]] narrate from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no deed of a day but it is sealed upon. When the believer falls ill, the angels say: 'O our Lord, your servant so-and-so, have You withheld him?' The Lord, majestic is His majesty, says: 'Seal for him in the likeness of his deed, until he recovers or dies'" [[Al-Musnad (4/146).]].

Its isnad (chain of narration) is good and strong, though they did not record it.

Ma'mar said, from Qatadah: ﴿We have fastened to his neck his bird﴾: he said, "His deed." ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾: he said, "We will bring out that deed." ﴿A record which he will find laid open﴾. Ma'mar said: al-Hasan al-Basri recited ﴿[One sits] on the right and on the left, attentive﴾ [Qaf 50:17] and said: "O son of Adam, I have unfolded for you your scroll, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. As for the one on your right, he guards your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he guards your bad deeds. So do whatever you wish, little or much, until when you die your scroll will be folded and placed on your neck with you in your grave, until you come out on the Day of Resurrection as a record you will find laid open. ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant﴾. By Allah, He has been just to you, the One who made you the reckoner of your own self."

This is from the excellence of al-Hasan's speech, may Allah have mercy on him.

The Most High says, after mentioning time and what occurs in it of the deeds of the children of Adam: ﴿And We have fastened to every person's neck his bird [of fortune or misfortune]﴾. His "bird" (ṭā'ir) is what flies away from him of his deeds, as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: good and evil, which he is bound to and for which he is recompensed. ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah 99:7–8]. He also said: ﴿[One sits] on the right and on the left, attentive. He utters no word but that there is with him a watchful observer, ready﴾ [Qaf 50:17–18]. He said: ﴿But indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do. Indeed, the righteous will be in pleasure, and indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ [al-Infitar 82:10–14]. He said: ﴿You are only recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Tur 52:16], and He said: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:123].

The point is that the deeds of the son of Adam are preserved for him, little and much, and are recorded for him by night and by day, morning and evening.

Imam Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, the bird of every person is at his neck." Ibn Lahi'ah said: meaning the omen (ṭayrah) [[Al-Musnad (3/360). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/49): "In it is Ibn Lahi'ah, whose narrations are good but有 some weakness, and the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]].

This statement from Ibn Lahi'ah concerning the interpretation of this hadith is very strange, and Allah knows best.

* *

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 17, verse 15 (part 1 of 3):

He, exalted is He, informs that whoever is guided, follows the truth, and pursues the traces of prophethood, then he attains the praiseworthy outcome of that for himself [[In F: "al-hamd" (praise).]]. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾, that is, strays from the truth and deviates from the path of right guidance, then he only harms himself, and the burden of that returns upon him alone.

Then He said: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾, that is, no one bears the sin of another, and no wrongdoer commits a crime except against himself, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if one heavily laden calls [another] to its load, nothing of it will be carried﴾ [Fatir: 18].

There is no contradiction between this and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will surely carry their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13], and His saying [exalted is He] [[Addition from manuscript T.]]: ﴿And [they will bear] burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge﴾ [al-Nahl: 25]. The callers to misguidance bear the sin of their own error, and another sin because of what they caused others to go astray, without that diminishing the burdens of those [who were misled], and without them bearing anything of those burdens on their behalf. This is from the justice of Allah and His mercy toward His servants.

Likewise His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ is an informing about His justice, exalted is He, and that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him by the sending of a messenger to him, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has not sent down anything; you are only in great error.'"﴾ [al-Mulk: 8-9]. Likewise His saying [exalted is He] [[Addition from manuscript T.]]: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers."﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness, other than what we used to do." Did We not give you lives long enough for whoever would remember to remember? And the warner came to you. So taste [it], for the wrongdoers will have no helper.﴾ [Fatir: 37]. And there are other verses indicating that Allah, exalted is He, does not cause anyone to enter the Fire except after a messenger has been sent to him. For this reason, a group of scholars criticised the wording that appears as an interpolation in Sahih al-Bukhari at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾ [al-A'raf: 56].

ʿUbaydullah ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Yaʿqub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from al-A'raj, with his isnad, to Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The Garden and the Fire disputed..." and he mentioned the hadith until he said: "As for the Garden, Allah does not wrong any of His creation; and He will create for the Fire a creation, and they will be thrown into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?'" [[In T, F, A: "Is there any more? ... and they will be thrown into it, and it will say: 'Is there any more?'"]] three times, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7449).]].

This [statement] came concerning the Garden because it is the abode of bounty; but as for the Fire, it is the abode of justice, and no one enters it except after the warning has been given to him and the proof has been established against him. A group of hafiz (scholars of hadith memorisation) have spoken about this wording [[In T: "al-fazlah", which is an error.]] and said: "Perhaps it was transposed by the narrator," based on what the two [Shaykhs] reported in the Two Sahihs, and the wording is that of al-Bukhari, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Garden and the Fire disputed..." and he mentioned the hadith until he said: "As for the Fire, it will not be filled until He places His foot in it, and it will say: 'Enough, enough,' and then it will be filled, and parts of it will draw together, and Allah does not wrong any of His creation. As for the Garden, Allah will create for it a creation" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4850), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2846).]].

A question remains here, concerning which the imams, may Allah have mercy on them, have differed, both in the past and in the present, namely: the children who died while young and whose parents were disbelievers, what is their ruling? Likewise the insane person, the deaf person, the senile elderly person, and whoever died in the fatrah (the interval between messengers) and to whom the call did not reach. Hadiths have been related concerning them, which I shall mention to you, with Allah's help and His enabling, then we shall mention a summarised section of the imams' discourse on that. And Allah is the One sought for help.

The first hadith: from al-Aswad ibn Sari':
Imam Ahmad said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, Muʿadh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from al-Aswad ibn Sari' [may Allah be pleased with him] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]] that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four will argue on the Day of Resurrection: a man who is deaf and hears nothing, a man who is foolish, a man who is senile, and a man who died in a fatrah. As for the deaf man, he will say: 'My Lord, Islam has come and I hear nothing.' As for the foolish man, he will say: 'My Lord, Islam has come, and the children are pelting me with dung.' As for the senile man, he will say: 'My Lord, Islam has come, and I understand nothing.' As for the one who died in the fatrah, he will say: 'My Lord, no messenger of Yours came to me.' Then He will take their covenants that they will obey Him, and He will send to them: 'Enter the Fire.' By He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if they had entered it, it would have been cool and safe for them" [[Al-Musnad (4/24), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/216): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]].

And with the isnad from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, a similar hadith, except that at its end it says: "Whoever enters it, it will be cool and safe for him, and whoever does not enter it will be dragged to it" [[Al-Musnad (4/24), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/216): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]].

Likewise Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated it from Muʿadh ibn Hisham. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Kitab al-I'tiqad, from the hadith of Hanbal ibn Ishaq, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Madini, with it [[Al-I'tiqad (p. 169).]], and he said: "This isnad is sahih." Likewise Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four, each of them will present an argument before Allah," and he mentioned something similar [[Narrated by Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Sunnah, no. (404), by way of al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Hammad ibn Salamah with it.]].

Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Maʿmar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, mentioning it as mawquf (attributed to the Companion, not traced to the Prophet). Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/41).]].

Likewise Maʿmar narrated it from ʿAbd Allah ibn Tawus, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, as mawquf.

The second hadith: from Anas ibn Malik:
Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: al-Rabiʿ narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Aban, who said: We said to Anas: "O Abu Hamzah, what do you say about the children of the polytheists?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They have no bad deeds for which they would be punished and thus be among the people of the Fire, and they have no good deeds for which they would be rewarded and thus be among the kings of the people of the Garden; they are among the servants of the people of the Garden" [[Narrated by Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilyah (6/308) by way of Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Subayh with it. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar weakened it in al-Fath (3/246), and it has supporting reports from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Samurah ibn Jundub, may Allah be pleased with them. It seems that there is something objectionable in the text, because it contradicts what is in the Two Sahihs first, and because Allah described the servants of the people of the Garden as eternal, saying: ﴿And there will circulate among them immortal youths﴾ [al-Insan: 19]. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir's weakening of it will come later, and Allah knows best.]].

The third hadith: also from Anas:
Al-Hafiz Abu Yaʿla said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿAbd al-Warith, from Anas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four will be brought on the Day of Resurrection: the infant, the mentally deficient, the one who died in the fatrah, and the aged old man in decrepitude. Each of them will speak with his argument. The Lord, blessed and exalted, will say to a portion of the Fire: 'Come forth!' And He will say to them: 'I used to send to My servants messengers from among themselves, and I am Myself a messenger to you. Enter this.' He said: Whoever was destined for wretchedness will say: 'O my Lord, how can we enter it when it is from it that we used to flee?' He said: And whoever was destined for happiness will go on and rush into it eagerly. He said: Then Allah, exalted is He, will say: 'You were more intensely in denial and disobedience toward My messengers.' So He will admit these to the Garden and those to the Fire."

Likewise al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it from Yusuf ibn Musa, from Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid, with its isnad, the same [[Musnad Abi Yaʿla (7/225), and Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2177), Kashf al-Astar. Layth ibn Abi Sulaym is weak, and ʿAbd al-Warith, al-Bukhari said of him: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in narration).]].

The fourth hadith: from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, may Allah be pleased with him:
Al-Hafiz Abu Yaʿla al-Mawsili also said in his Musnad: Qasim ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allah narrated to us. [He means Ibn Dawud], from ʿUmar ibn Dharr, from Yazid ibn Umayyah, from al-Bara' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the children of the Muslims, and he said: "They are with their fathers." He was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "They are with their fathers." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what will they do?" He said: "Allah knows best what they would do" [[The author mentioned it in Jami' al-Masanid wa al-Sunan (37/87) from Musnad Abi Yaʿla, but I have not found it in the printed Musnad.]].

ʿUmar ibn Dharr also narrated it from Yazid ibn Umayyah, from a man, from al-Bara', from ʿAisha, and he mentioned it [[I have not come upon this chain; perhaps I shall add it later, if Allah wills. Imam Ahmad also narrated in his Musnad (6/84), by way of Bahiyyah, from ʿAisha, something similar.]].

The fifth hadith: from Thawban:
Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn Saʿid al-Jawhari narrated to us, Rayhan ibn Saʿid narrated to us, ʿAbbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, that the Prophet (ﷺ) magnified the matter of the question, and said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) will come carrying their idols on their backs, and their Lord will question them. They will say: 'Our Lord, You did not send a messenger to us, and no command of Yours came to us. Had You sent a messenger to us, we would have been most obedient of Your servants.' Their Lord will say to them: 'Tell Me, if I command you with a command, will you obey Me?' They will say: 'Yes.' So He will command them to make for Jahannam and enter it. They will set off, until when they approach it, they find in it fury and roaring, so they return to their Lord and say: 'Our Lord, bring us out of it, or protect us from it.' He will say to them: 'Did you not claim that if I commanded you with a command, you would obey Me?' He will take their covenants upon that, and say: 'Make for it and enter it.'

They will set off, until when they see it they will be terrified and return, and say: 'Our Lord, we were terrified of it, and we cannot enter it.' He will say: 'Enter it, humiliated.'" The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had they entered it the first time, it would have been cool and safe for them." Then al-Bazzar said: "The text of this hadith is not known except through this route; no one narrated it from Ayyub except ʿAbbad, and no one narrated from ʿAbbad except Rayhan ibn Saʿid" [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (3433), Kashf al-Astar.]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 15 (part 2 of 3):

I say: Ibn Hibban mentioned him in his *Thiqat* (the book of reliable narrators). Yahya ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him." Abu Dawud did not approve of him. Abu Hatim said: "He is a shaykh with no harm in him; his hadith is written down but not used as evidence."

**The Sixth Hadith:** From Abu Sa'id, Sa'd ibn Malik ibn Sinan al-Khudri:

The Imam Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli said: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who died during the period of interruption (*fatrah*), the insane person, and the infant. The one who died in the *fatrah* will say: 'No messenger came to me.' The insane person will say: 'My Lord, You did not give me intellect by which I could distinguish good from evil.' The infant will say: 'My Lord, I did not reach the age of understanding.' Then a fire will be raised for them, and it will be said to them: 'Enter it.'" He said: "Whoever was among the people of happiness in Allah's knowledge would enter it, had he reached the age of action; and whoever was among the people of wretchedness in Allah's knowledge would hold back from it, had he reached the age of action. Then He will say: 'You disobeyed Me, so how would it be if My messengers had come to you?'"

Al-Bazzar also narrated it, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hayyaj al-Kufi, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, with the same wording.[1] Then he said: "This is not known from the hadith of Abu Sa'id except through this route, from 'Atiyyah, from him." At its end he said: "Allah will say: 'You disobeyed Me, so how about My messengers, in the unseen?'"

**The Seventh Hadith:** From Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him:

Hisham ibn 'Ammar and Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak al-Suri said: 'Umar ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Halbas, from Abu Idris al-Khawlani, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "On the Day of Resurrection, there will be brought the one who was mentally deficient, the one who died in the *fatrah*, and the one who died young. The mentally deficient one will say: 'My Lord, had You given me intellect, the one to whom You gave intellect would not have been happier than I.' (He mentioned the one who died in the *fatrah* and the child in a similar way.) The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'I command you with a command; will you obey Me?' They will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'Go and enter the Fire.'" He said: "Even if they had entered it, it would not have harmed them." Then it will emerge upon them as flames, and they will think it has destroyed everything Allah created, so they will return quickly. Then He will command them a second time, and they will return in the same way. The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say: "Before I created you, I knew what you would do, and upon My knowledge I created you, and to My knowledge you will return. Seize them," and the Fire will seize them.[2]

**The Eighth Hadith:** From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him:

Its narration has already passed, combined with the narration of al-Aswad ibn Sari', may Allah be pleased with him.

In the *Sahihayn* (the two authentic collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child is born upon the *fitrah* (natural disposition). Then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as an animal gives birth to a complete animal. Do you see any mutilation in it?"[3]

In another narration, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about one who dies young?" He said: "Allah knows best what they would have been doing."[4]

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn Qurrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Damrah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as far as I know (Musa was uncertain): "The offspring of the Muslims are in Paradise, and Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will take care of them."[5]

In Sahih Muslim, from 'Iyad ibn Himar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "I created My servants as *hunafa'* (upright monotheists)." In another narration by others, "Muslims."[6]

**The Ninth Hadith:** From Samurah, may Allah be pleased with him:

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Barqani narrated it in his book *al-Mustakhraj 'ala al-Bukhari* (a collection of hadiths that al-Barqani derived independently from al-Bukhari's chains), from the hadith of 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi, from Samurah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Every child is born upon the *fitrah*." The people called out: "O Messenger of Allah, and the children of the polytheists?" He said: "And the children of the polytheists."[7]

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Mukram al-Dabbi narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Shu'ayb, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from Abu Raja', from Samurah, who said: "We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the children of the polytheists, and he said: 'They are the servants of the people of Paradise.'"[8]

**The Tenth Hadith:** From the paternal uncle of Hasna' (or Khansa'):

Ahmad said: Ishaq (i.e., al-Azraq) narrated to us; Rawh informed us; 'Awf narrated to us, from Hasna' bint Mu'awiyah of the Banu Sarim, who said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, who is in Paradise?' He said: 'The Prophet is in Paradise, the martyr is in Paradise, the child is in Paradise, and the buried infant (*al-wa'id*) is in Paradise.'"[9]

Some scholars held a position of suspension (*tawaqquf*) regarding them, due to this hadith. Others determined that they are in Paradise, based on the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub in the Sahih of al-Bukhari: that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, in the course of that dream, when he passed by that old man under the tree with children around him, Jibril said to him: "This is Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and these are the children of the Muslims and the children of the polytheists." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, and the children of the polytheists?" He said: "Yes, and the children of the polytheists."[10]

Others determined that they are in the Fire, based on his saying (peace be upon him): "They are with their fathers."

Others held that they will be tested on the Day of Resurrection in the plains of judgment. Whoever obeys will enter Paradise, and Allah's knowledge of them will be revealed as having preceded happiness. Whoever disobeys will enter the Fire humiliated, and Allah's knowledge of him will be revealed as having preceded wretchedness.

This view reconciles all the evidences, and the hadiths previously mentioned clearly support it, as they strengthen one another. This is the view reported by Shaykh Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Isma'il al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, from the *Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah* (the people of the Sunnah and the community), and it is what Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi supported in *Kitab al-I'tiqad*, as did other verifying scholars and critical hadith masters.

Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari mentioned, after the hadiths of testing that preceded, then said: "The hadiths of this chapter are not strong, and they do not establish a proof, and the people of knowledge reject them, because the Hereafter is a place of recompense, not a place of action or trial. How can they be obligated to enter the Fire, when that is not within the capacity of created beings, and Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity?!"

The answer to what he said: some hadiths of this chapter are authentic, as several leading scholars have stated, some are good (*hasan*), and some are weak but strengthened by the authentic and good ones. When the hadiths of a single chapter strengthen one another in this manner, they establish proof for the one who examines them. As for his saying "the Hereafter is a place of recompense," there is no doubt that it is a place of recompense, and this does not contradict being obligated in its plains before entering Paradise or the Fire, as Shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari related from the position of the Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, regarding the testing of children. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿On the Day when a shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostrate﴾ [al-Qalam 68:42]. The Sunnah is established in the authentic collections and elsewhere that the believers will prostrate to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, while the hypocrite will be unable to do so; his back will become one solid plate, and whenever he tries to prostrate, he will fall on his back.[11]

In the *Sahihayn*, regarding the man who will be the last of the people of the Fire to leave it: Allah takes his covenants and pledges that he will not ask for anything other than what he is in, and this repeats many times, and Allah the Exalted says: "O son of Adam, how treacherous you are!" Then He permits him to enter Paradise.[12]

As for his saying: "How would He obligate them to enter the Fire, when that is not within their capacity?" this does not prevent the hadith's authenticity. Allah commands the servants on the Day of Resurrection to cross the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), which is sharper than a sword and finer than a hair. The believers cross it according to their deeds, like lightning, like the wind, like the finest horses and riding camels. Some run, some walk, some crawl crawling, and some are dragged on their faces into the Fire. What is reported about those is no greater than this; rather, this is more severe and greater. Also, the Sunnah establishes that the Dajjal (the false messiah) will have with him a Paradise and a Fire, and the Lawgiver commanded the believers who encounter him to drink from what appears to be fire, for it will be cool and safe for them. So this is similar to that. Also, Allah the Exalted commanded the Children of Israel to kill themselves, so some of them killed others, until, it is said, seventy thousand were killed in a single morning. A man killed his father and his brother, while they were under a dense cloud Allah had sent over them. That was a punishment for them for worshipping the calf. This too is extremely difficult for souls, and not less than what is mentioned in the aforementioned hadith. And Allah knows best.

**Ibn Kathir's Commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 17, Verse 15 (Part 3 of 3)**

The first of these views is that they are in Paradise. Its proponents cite the hadith of Samurah that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw Ibrahim (Abraham) with the children of the believers and the children of the polytheists. They also cite what has preceded in the narration of Ahmad from Hasna'[[in T, F: "Khansa'".]] from her paternal uncle, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The newborn is in Paradise." This is a valid line of argument. However, the hadiths about the trial (imtihan) are more specific than it. Whoever Allah [Azza wa Jalla] knows will obey, Allah makes his soul in the barzakh (intermediate realm) with Ibrahim and the children of the Muslims who died upon the fitrah (natural disposition). Whoever Allah knows will not respond, his affair is with Allah Most High, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be in the Fire, as the hadiths of the trial indicate. Al-Ash'ari transmitted this from Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah.

Among those who say they are in Paradise, some regard them as independent residents of it, while others regard them as servants to the people of Paradise, as came in the hadith of 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Anas, in the collection of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi. That hadith was already mentioned and discussed under this verse, and it is weak. And Allah knows best.

The second view: they are with their fathers in the Fire. Its proponent relies on what Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated from Abu al-Mughirah, who said: 'Utbah ibn Damrah[[in F: "Hamzah".]] ibn Habib told us, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Qays, client of Ghutayf, told me that he came to 'A'ishah and asked her about the offspring of the disbelievers. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They follow their fathers." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, without any deeds?" He said: "Allah knows best what they used to do."

Abu Dawud also transmitted it through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Harb, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Alhani, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Abi Qays say: I heard 'A'ishah say: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the offspring of the believers. He said: "They are of their fathers." I said: "What about the offspring of the polytheists?" He said: "They are with their fathers." I said: "Without any deeds?" He said: "Allah knows best what they used to do."

Ahmad also narrated it from Waki', from Abu 'Aqil Yahya ibn al-Mutawakkil, who is abandoned (matruk) in narration, from his freed slave-woman Buhayyah, from 'A'ishah, that she mentioned the children of the polytheists to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "If you wish, I will let you hear their wailing in the Fire."

'Abdullah, the son of Imam Ahmad, said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn[[in T: "from".]] Ghazwan, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zadhan, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Khadijah asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about two sons she had which died in the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period). He said: "They are in the Fire." He said: When he saw the dislike on her face, [he said:] "If you saw their place, you would hate them." She said: "And my son by you?" He said: ["In Paradise." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:] "Indeed the believers and their children are in Paradise, and indeed the polytheists and their children are in the Fire." Then he recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We will join their offspring with them﴾ [al-Tur: 21].

This is a strange (gharib) hadith, for Muhammad ibn 'Uthman here is of unknown reliability (majhul al-hal), and his teacher Zadhan did not meet 'Ali.

Abu Dawud narrated through the hadith of Ibn Abi Za'idah, from his father, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who buries a girl alive and the girl who is buried alive are in the Fire." Then al-Sha'bi said: 'Alqamah narrated this to me, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud.

A group also narrated it from Da'ud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Alqamah, from Salamah ibn Qays al-Ashja'i, who said: My brother and I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and we said: "Our mother died in the Jahiliyyah. She used to feed guests and maintain the ties of kinship, and she buried alive a sister of ours in the Jahiliyyah who had not reached puberty (al-hinth)." He said: "The one who buries alive and the one buried alive are in the Fire, unless the one who buried alive reaches Islam and embraces it." This is a sound chain (isnad hasan).

The third view: suspending judgement about them (tawaqquf), relying on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah knows best what they used to do." It is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Ja'far ibn Abi Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "Allah knows best what they used to do." Likewise, it is in the two Sahihs from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid, and from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "Allah knows best what they used to do."

Some scholars placed them among the people of al-A'raf (the Heights). This view returns to the view of those who held that they are among the people of Paradise, because al-A'raf is not a place of permanent abode, and the final destination of its people is Paradise, as the explanation of this was already given in the commentary on Surat al-A'raf. And Allah knows best.

**Section**

It should be known that this disagreement concerns only the children of the polytheists. As for the children of the believers, there is no disagreement among the scholars, as Qadi Abu Ya'la ibn al-Farra' al-Hanbali related from Imam Ahmad that he said: "There is no disagreement about them, that they are among the people of Paradise." This is the well-known position among people, and it is the one we are certain of, God willing, Azza wa Jalla. As for what Shaykh Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr mentioned from some scholars, that they suspended judgement regarding this, and that all the young children are under the will (mashi'ah) of Allah, Azza wa Jalla, Abu 'Umar said: A group of the jurists and hadith scholars held this view, among them Hammad ibn Zayd, Hammad ibn Salamah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and others. They said: "It resembles what Malik set down in his Muwatta' in the chapters on qadar (divine decree), and the hadiths he cited on that subject, and most of his companions follow this." Nothing explicit is reported from Malik on it, except that later companions of his held that the children of the Muslims are in Paradise, while the children of the polytheists specifically are under the will of Allah. End of his words, and it is very strange.

Abu 'Abdullah al-Qurtubi also mentioned something similar in his book al-Tadhkirah, and Allah knows best.

They also cited the hadith of 'A'ishah bint Talhah, from 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was called to the funeral of a young boy from the Ansar. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, good tidings to him! He is a little bird from the little birds of Paradise, who did no evil and did not reach it." He said: "Or is it otherwise, O 'A'ishah? Indeed Allah created Paradise and created for it people, and they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created the Fire and created for it people, and they were in the loins of their fathers." Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah.

Since discussion of this issue requires sound and strong evidence, and since one who has no knowledge from the Lawgiver (al-Shari') may speak about it, a group of scholars disliked speaking about it. This was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and others. Ibn Hibban in his Sahih recorded, from Jarir ibn Hazim, who said: I heard Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas, while he was on the pulpit, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The affair of this Ummah will remain agreeable, or nearly so, as long as they do not speak about the children (al-wildan) and qadar."

Ibn Hibban said: "He means the children of the polytheists."

Likewise, Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it through the route of Jarir ibn Hazim, with the same wording. Then he said: A group also narrated it from Abu Raja', from Ibn 'Abbas, as a statement of Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf).

The readers differed over the recitation of His words ﴿amarna﴾ (We commanded). The well-known reading is the lightened form (al-takhfif, the reading without doubling the letter). The exegetes differed over its meaning. It was said: its meaning is, "We commanded its affluent ones, and they transgressed therein, a decreed command (amran qadariyyan)," as in His words, ﴿Then Our command came to it by night or by day﴾ [Yunus: 24]. Indeed, Allah does not command indecency. They said: its meaning is that He drove them to commit abominations, so they deserved the punishment.

It was also said: its meaning is, "We commanded them to obey, but they committed abominations, so they deserved the punishment." This was narrated by Ibn Juraij from Ibn 'Abbas, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said it.

Ibn Jarir said: It may also be that its meaning is, "We made them rulers (umara')."

I say: This only fits the reading of the one who reads "ammarna mutrafiha" (with doubling, meaning "We made its affluent ones rulers").

'Ali ibn Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿We commanded its affluent ones, and they transgressed therein﴾, that he said: "We empowered its wicked ones, and they disobeyed therein. When they did that, We destroyed them with punishment." This is His words, ﴿And thus We placed in every town its greatest criminals to plot therein﴾ [al-An'am: 123]. Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said likewise.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they transgress therein﴾, that he said: "We increased their number." 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said likewise. And from Malik, from al-Zuhri, regarding His words, ﴿We commanded its affluent ones﴾: "We increased them."

Some of them cited the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Abu Na'amah al-'Adawi narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Budayl, from Iyas ibn Zuhayr, from Suwayd ibn Hubayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best property of a man is a fertile mare (mahrah ma'murah), or a well-pollinated row of palms (sikkah ma'burah)."

Imam Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book al-Gharib: "Ma'murah" means one with abundant offspring. "Sikkah" means a row of palm trees arranged in a line. "Ma'burah" is from al-ta'bir (pollination of the palm). Some of them said: this [word] came in parallel with His saying (ﷺ): "burdened with sins, not rewarded" (ma'zurat ghayr ma'jurat). [Al-Zayla'i mentioned this in his takhrij of al-Kashshaf (2/262) and added: "Because it is from ta'bid, which is what improves the palm, such as irrigation and other things."]

Allah, exalted is He, says, warning the disbelievers of Quraysh for their denial of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), that He has destroyed many nations of those who denied the messengers after Noah. This indicates that the generations that existed between Adam and Noah were upon Islam, as Ibn 'Abbas said: "There were ten generations between Adam and Noah, all of them upon Islam."

The meaning is: you deniers are not more honored by Allah than they were, and you have denied the most noble of the messengers and the best of creation, so your punishment is more fitting and more deserving.

He (exalted is He) informs us that not everyone who seeks this world and its pleasures attains them. Rather, they are attained only by those for whom Allah wills what He wills.
