[[Its takhrij was previously given in the commentary on verse 69 of Surah an-Nisa, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording differs somewhat from this wording. It was narrated with this wording by al-Humaydi in his Musnad, no. (775), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him.]]; for this reason the Exalted said: ﴿And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: The intended audience is the mukallafun (those legally responsible) of the Ummah. O you who are responsible, do not set up a partner with your Lord in your worship, ﴿lest you sit down reproached﴾ for your associating [others with Him], ﴿forsaken﴾, because the Lord, exalted is He, will not help you; rather, He will leave you to that which you worshipped alongside Him, and it does not possess for you any harm or benefit, for the possessor of harm and benefit is Allah alone, with no partner. Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us: Bashir ibn Salman narrated to us, from Sayyar Abi al-Hakam, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is afflicted with poverty and brings it upon the people, his poverty will not be relieved; and whoever brings it upon Allah, Allah will soon grant him provision, either by a swift death or by swift wealth."

Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of Bashir ibn Salman, with the same chain (Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1645; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2326). Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 17, verses 23–24:

He, exalted is He, says, commanding worship of Him alone, with no partner, for the decree (*al-qada'*) here means the command (*al-amr*).

Mujahid said: "﴿And your Lord has decreed﴾ means: has enjoined." Ubayy ibn Ka'b, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim also recited it this way: "And your Lord has enjoined that you worship none but Him." For this reason, He linked the honouring of parents with the worship of Him, saying: ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾, meaning: and He commanded kindness to parents. This is like His saying in another verse: ﴿Give thanks to Me and to your parents; to Me is the final return﴾ [Luqman: 14].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them, "Uff"﴾, meaning: do not let them hear any bad word, not even the "uff," which is the lowest level of harmful speech. ﴿And do not scold them﴾, meaning: no ugly act should come from you toward them. This is as 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said concerning His saying, ﴿and do not scold them﴾: it means do not raise your hand against your parents.

When He forbade him bad speech and bad action, He commanded him good speech and good action, saying: ﴿And speak to them a noble word﴾, meaning: gentle, good and pleasant speech, with courtesy, reverence and honour.

﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy﴾, meaning: be humble toward them in your conduct. ﴿And say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small"﴾, meaning: in their old age and at their death.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were near relatives﴾ [al-Tawbah: 113].

Many hadiths have come concerning the honouring of parents. Among them is the hadith narrated through several chains from Anas and others: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit, he said: "Amin, amin, amin." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, at what did you say amin?" He said: "Jibril came to me and said: 'O Muhammad, may the nose of a man be rubbed in dust, the man in whose presence you are mentioned and he does not send blessings upon you. Say amin.' So I said amin. Then he said: 'May the nose of a man be rubbed in dust, the man who lives to see Ramadan and then leaves without being forgiven. Say amin.' So I said amin. Then he said: 'May the nose of a man be rubbed in dust, the man who reaches his parents, or one of them, and they do not admit him to Paradise. Say amin.' So I said amin."
[[Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, no. 3168 (Kashf al-Astar), through Ja'far ibn 'Awn, from Salamah ibn Wardan, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: "Salamah is sound, and he has hadiths that are unsettling, and we do not know of anyone who narrated hadiths with these wordings besides him." It also came from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, recorded by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2551, and it will come. From the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (4/153). From the hadiths of 'Ammar ibn Yasir, Jabir ibn Samurah, Ibn Mas'ud and 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, nos. 3164–3167.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd narrated to us, Zurarah ibn Awfa informed us, from Malik ibn al-Harith, a man from among them, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever takes in an orphan between two Muslim parents, feeding and watering him until Allah makes him independent of him, Paradise is definitely due to him. And whoever frees a Muslim man, that will be his ransom from the Fire, one limb for each limb of his."

Then he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard 'Ali ibn Zayd, and he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: "from a man of his people called Malik or Ibn Malik," and he added: "And whoever reaches his parents, or one of them, and enters the Fire, may Allah distance him."
[[Musnad (4/344).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Zurarah ibn Awfa, from Malik ibn 'Amr al-Qushayri: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever frees a believing slave, it will be his ransom from the Fire, a bone for a bone of his. And whoever reaches one of his parents and is not forgiven, may Allah, mighty and majestic, distance him. And whoever takes in an orphan between two Muslim parents, feeding and watering him until Allah makes him independent, Paradise is due to him."
[[Musnad (4/344).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj and Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, both said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, I heard Zurarah ibn Awfa narrate from Ubayy ibn Malik al-Qushayri, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever reaches his parents, or one of them, and then enters the Fire afterwards, may Allah distance him and destroy him."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it similarly from Shu'bah, and in it are other additions.
[[Musnad (4/344).]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, Suhayl ibn Abi Salih narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "May his nose be rubbed in dust, then may his nose be rubbed in dust, then may his nose be rubbed in dust: the man who reaches his parents, one of them or both, in old age, and does not enter Paradise."

It is sound by this chain, and no one narrated it except Muslim, from the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, Jarir and Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Suhayl, with it.
[[Musnad (2/364) and Sahih Muslim, no. 2551.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ribʻi ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Ahmad said: he is the brother of Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, and he was preferred over his brother. From 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May the nose of a man be rubbed in dust, in whose presence I am mentioned and he does not send blessings upon me! May the nose of a man be rubbed in dust, upon whom Ramadan comes and passes before he is forgiven! And may the nose of a man be rubbed in dust, in whose presence his parents reach old age and they do not admit him to Paradise." Ribʻi said: "I do not know that he said anything other than 'one of them'."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, from Ribʻi ibn Ibrahim, and then said: "Gharib (strange) from this route."
[[Musnad (2/254) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3545.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, Usayd ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from his father, 'Ali ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Usayd, who is Malik ibn Rabi'ah al-Sa'idi, who said: While I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man of the Ansar came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there any part of the duty of honouring my parents still owed to them after their death, which I can perform?" He said: "Yes: four qualities: praying for them, asking forgiveness for them, carrying out their covenant, honouring their friends, and maintaining the ties of kinship which you have only through them. That is what remains of honouring them after their death."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it through the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, who is Ibn al-Ghasil, with it.
[[Musnad (3/497), Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 5142, and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3664.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Rawh narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, from his father, from Mu'awiyah ibn Jahimah al-Sulami, that Jahimah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I want to go on raid, and I have come to seek your counsel." He said: "Do you have a mother?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Stay with her, for Paradise is at her feet," then the second time, then the third time, in different positions, similar to this statement.

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it through the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, with it.
[[Musnad (3/429), Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/11) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 2781.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from al-Miqdam ibn Ma'd Yakrib al-Kindi, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Allah enjoins you concerning your fathers; Allah enjoins you concerning your mothers; Allah enjoins you concerning your mothers; Allah enjoins you concerning your mothers; Allah enjoins you concerning those nearest, then those nearest."

Ibn Majah also narrated it through the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Ayyash, with it.
[[Musnad (4/132) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 3661.]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath ibn Sulaym, from his father, from a man of Banu Yarbu', who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and I heard him speaking to people, saying: "The hand of the giver [the upper] is to your mother, your father, your sister and your brother; then the nearest, then the nearest."
[[Musnad (4/64).]]

Another hadith: The memorizer (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamirr al-'Urquri narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Sufyan narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from 'Alqamah ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father: that a man was circumambulating the Ka'bah carrying his mother, going around with her. He asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Have I fulfilled her right?" He said: "No, not even with one sigh," or as he said. Then al-Bazzar said: "We do not know it to be narrated except through this route."
[[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1872 (Kashf al-Astar); the text there reads "wa la bi-zafrah wahidah" ("not even with one sigh"); in Majma' al-Zawa'id it reads "wa la bi-barakah" ("nor with a blessing").]]

I say: al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far is weak, and Allah knows best.

* *

And His saying [the Exalted]: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back (to Him) often﴾. Qatadah said: to the obedient ones, the people of prayer.

And it is narrated from Ibn Abbas: to those who glorify (God). In another narration from him: to the obedient, the good-doers.

Some of them said: they are those who pray between the two evening prayers (Maghrib and Isha). Others said: they are those who pray the Duha (forenoon) prayer.

Shu'bah narrated, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back (to Him) often﴾, that he said: "It is the one who commits a sin and then repents, and commits a sin and then repents."

Abd al-Razzaq similarly narrated it from al-Thawri and Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Ibn al-Musayyib, something similar. Likewise al-Layth and Ibn Juraij narrated it from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Ibn al-Musayyib, with the same wording. Likewise Ata' ibn Yasar said it.

Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are those who return to good.

Mujahid narrated from Ubayd ibn Umayr regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back (to Him) often﴾, that he said: "It is the one who, when he remembers his sins in private, seeks forgiveness from God for them." Mujahid agreed with him on this.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back (to Him) often﴾, that he said: "We used to count the awwab (one who turns back often) as the one who guards (himself) and says: O Allah, forgive me for what I have done in this sitting of mine."

Ibn Jarir said: The most preferable view on this is the saying of the one who said: he is the one who repents from sin, who turns back from disobedience to obedience, from what God dislikes to what He loves and is pleased with.

And this which he said is correct, because the word awwab is derived from awb, which is return. It is said: "Fulan returned (aba)" when he came back. God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, to Us is their return (iyabahum)﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 25]. And in the authentic hadith, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he returned from a journey, would say: "Returning, repenting, worshipping, praising our Lord." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 1797, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]

When Allah mentioned kindness to one's parents, He followed it with mention of kindness to relatives and maintaining the ties of kinship, as has already been stated in the hadith: "Your mother and your father, then the nearest, then the nearest." In another narration: "Then the nearest, then the nearest."

The hadith says: "Whoever wishes that his provision be expanded for him and his lifespan be extended, let him maintain his ties of kinship."[[In manuscripts T, F, A: "lahu fi rizqihi" ("for him in his provision").]] [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5986), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2557).]]

Then he said: "We do not know this narrated from Fudayl ibn Marzuq except by Abu Yahya al-Taymi and Humayd ibn Hammad ibn Abi al-Kharrar."[[In manuscript T: "Abu Najy al-Tamimi." Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 17, verses 29–30:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding moderation in living and condemning stinginess and forbidding extravagance: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾, meaning: do not be stingy and withholding, giving nothing to anyone. Likewise the Jews, may the curses of Allah be upon them, said: ﴿The hand of Allah is chained﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64], meaning they attributed stinginess to Him. Exalted and sanctified is the Most Generous, the Bestower.

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not extend it with complete extension﴾ means: do not be extravagant in spending, so that you give beyond your capacity and spend more than your income, and thus you sit "blameworthy and regretful" (*mahsur*).

This is from the rhetorical device of *al-laff wa al-nashr* (a device in which several items are mentioned first and then each is matched with its counterpart, here the two extremes), meaning: if you are stingy, you will sit blameworthy, people will blame and disparage you and will be independent of you, as Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said in his *Mu'allaqah* (the "suspended" ode):

*And whoever has wealth yet withholds his wealth from his people, he will be done without and blamed.* [The verse is in his Diwan (p. 30).]

And when you extend your hand beyond your capacity, you will sit with nothing to spend, and you will be like *al-hasir*, which is the animal that has become unable to continue walking, so it stops out of weakness and incapacity. It is called *al-hasir*, and the word is derived from *al-kalal* (exhaustion), as Allah says: ﴿Then return the gaze; do you see any flaw? Then return the gaze twice; your gaze will return to you humbled while it is exhausted﴾ [al-Mulk: 3–4], meaning: weary from seeing any defect. This is how Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd and others explained this verse, that what is meant here is stinginess and extravagance.

It has come in the two *Sahihs* (Bukhari and Muslim), from the narration of Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The parable of the miser and the spender is like two men wearing coats of iron from their breasts up to their collarbones. As for the spender, he does not spend except that it extends over his skin until it covers his fingertips and conceals his traces. As for the miser, he does not want to spend anything except that each ring sticks in its place, so he tries to widen it but it does not widen."

This is the wording of Bukhari in the chapter on *zakah*. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1443. It is not in Sahih Muslim via the route of Abu al-Zinad; rather it is in Muslim via al-Hasan ibn Muslim and Abdullah ibn Tawus, from Tawus, from Abu Hurayrah, no. 1021.]

And in the two *Sahihs*, through the route of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his wife Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from her grandmother Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Spend, but do not hoard, lest Allah hoard for you; and do not withhold, lest Allah withhold from you." In another wording: "and do not count, lest Allah count against you." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1433; Sahih Muslim, no. 1029.]

In Sahih Muslim, through the route of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah said to me: Spend, and I will spend upon you." [Sahih Muslim, no. 993.]

In the two *Sahihs*, through the route of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No day dawns upon the servants except that two angels descend from the sky; one of them says: 'O Allah, give the spender a replacement,' and the other says: 'O Allah, give the withholder ruin.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1442; Sahih Muslim, no. 1010.]

Muslim narrated from Qutaybah, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from al-'Ala' [in Fa: "from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman"], from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet: "Wealth is never diminished by charity, Allah does not increase a servant through pardon except in honor, and whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2588.]

In the hadith of Abu Kathir, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, traced to the Prophet: "Beware of stinginess (*shuh*), for it destroyed those before you. It commanded them to be stingy and they were stingy; it commanded them to sever ties and they severed them; it commanded them to commit immorality and they committed it." [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/159), Abu Dawud in al-Sunan, no. 1698, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 1580 (Mawarid), through routes from Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Abu Kathir al-Zubaydi.]

Al-Bayhaqi narrated through the route of Sa'dan ibn Nasr, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, [from Ibn Buraydah — addition from Fa, A, and al-Sunan al-Kubra and Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah], from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man does not give charity until he unties seventy devils from his jaw." [Al-Sunan al-Kubra (4/187). Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2457, through the route of Muhammad al-Makhzumi, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with it, and he said: "If the report is sound, then I do not know whether al-A'mash heard from Ibn Buraydah or not."]

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Ubaydah al-Haddad narrated to us, Sukayn [in Ta: "Miskin"; in Fa and A: "Sukan"] ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Hijri narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One who practices moderation never becomes poor." [Al-Musnad (1/447). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/252): "In it is Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, who is weak."]

This noble verse indicates that Allah the Exalted is more merciful to His servants than a parent is to his child, because He forbids the killing of children, just as He enjoined provision for children in inheritance. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the time of ignorance before Islam) did not give inheritance to daughters. Rather, one of them might kill his daughter lest his dependents increase. So Allah [the Exalted] [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A.]] forbade that, saying: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾, meaning: for fear that you would become poor later on. For this reason He placed first the concern for their provision, saying: ﴿We provide for them and for you﴾. In Surat al-An'am [[In T, F, A: "And He said in Surat al-An'am."]] He said: ﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, meaning: out of destitution, ﴿We provide for you and for them [[In T: "narzuquhum wa iyyakum", which is an error.]]﴾ [al-An'am: 151].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, their killing has been a great sin﴾ means: a great wrongdoing.

Some of them recited it as "kāna khaṭa'an kabīran" (خَطَأً كَبِيرًا), and it has the same meaning. (Khiṭ' [خِطْءًا] and khaṭa' [خَطَأً] are both used for a sin or wrongdoing; the first is from the root of sinning deliberately, the second is the form that is often read as error or mistake, yet here it carries the same sense of a grave offence.)

In the Two Sahihs, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said, "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child lest he eat with you." I said, "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4477), and Sahih Muslim, no. (68).]

Allah the Exalted says, forbidding His servants from fornication (zina) and from approaching it, which means mixing with its causes and its incitements: ﴿And do not approach fornication. Indeed, it is ever an abomination and evil as a way.﴾ That is, it is a great sin, and it is an evil path and course.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, Sulaym ibn Amir narrated to us, from Abu Umamah, who said: A young man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to commit fornication." The people turned to him and rebuked him, saying: "Mah, mah!" (Stop, stop!) The Prophet ﷺ said: "Come closer." So he drew close to him, and he said: "Sit down." So he sat. He said: "Would you like it for your mother?" He said: "No, by Allah, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: "Neither do people like it for their mothers. Would you like it for your daughter?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: "Neither do people like it for their daughters. Would you like it for your sister?" He said: "No, by Allah, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: "Neither do people like it for their sisters. Would you like it for your paternal aunt?" He said: "No, by Allah, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: "Neither do people like it for their paternal aunts. Would you like it for your maternal aunt?" He said: "No, by Allah, may Allah make me your ransom." He said: "Neither do people like it for their maternal aunts." He said: Then he placed his hand upon him and said: "O Allah, forgive his sin, purify his heart, and guard his chastity (furj)." He said: After that, the young man never turned his attention to anything (of that sort). (Musnad, 5/356)

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ammar ibn Nasr narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from al-Haytham ibn Malik al-Ta'i, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "There is no sin after shirk greater in the sight of Allah than a drop of semen that a man places in a womb that is not lawful for him." (Al-Wara' by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 137. In its chain there are three defects: first, tadlis (concealment of sources) by Baqiyyah; second, Ibn Abi Maryam is weak; third, irsal (a break in the chain). Ended, as noted from the commentary of Ustadh Muhammad al-Hammud; the hadith will come again in the commentary on verse 68 of Surah al-Furqan.)

The Most High says, forbidding the killing of a soul without a lawful right, as is established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is not lawful to shed, except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married person who commits adultery, and one who abandons his religion and separates himself from the community" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6878), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1676), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

And in the Sunan: "The destruction of the world is less grave before Allah than the killing of a Muslim" [[In A: "the Muslim".]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority﴾, meaning authority over the killer. He has the choice regarding him: if he wishes, he may kill him by way of qisas (retaliation); if he wishes, he may pardon him in exchange for diyah (blood money); and if he wishes, he may pardon him without compensation, as the Sunnah has established. The Imam, the scholar Ibn Abbas, derived from the general sense of this noble verse that Mu'awiyah had the authority of rule and that he would come to possess it, because he was the guardian (wali) of Uthman, and Uthman was killed wrongfully, may Allah be pleased with him. Mu'awiyah used to demand that Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, hand over Uthman's killers so that he might exact retaliation from them, because he was of the Umayyads. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, would ask him to wait in the matter [[In T: "the matters".]] until he gained control and could do that. Ali asked Mu'awiyah to hand over Syria to him, but Mu'awiyah refused until he handed over the killers, and he refused to pledge allegiance to Ali, he and the people of Syria. Then, with the prolonged delay, Mu'awiyah gained power and the matter came to him, just as Ibn Abbas had foreseen [[In T, F, A: "said".]] and inferred from this noble verse. This is one of the remarkable matters. Al-Tabarani related this in his Mu'jam, where he said:

Yahya ibn Abd al-Baqi narrated to us: Abu Umayr ibn al-Nahhas narrated to us: Damrah ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mattar al-Warraq, from Zahdam al-Jarmi, who said: We were in an evening gathering with Ibn Abbas, and he said: "I will relate to you a narration that is neither secret nor public. When there occurred what occurred with this man (meaning Uthman), I said to Ali: 'Withdraw. Even if you were in a hole, you would be sought until you were dragged out.' But he disobeyed me. By Allah, Mu'awiyah will certainly become a ruler over you. That is because Allah the Most High says: ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have given his heir authority, so let him not commit excess in killing﴾ [the verse]. Quraysh will certainly compel you to follow the way of Persia and Rome, and the Christians, Jews and Magians will certainly rule over you. Whoever among you takes what is known on that day will be saved, and whoever leaves it while you are leaving it, you will be like a generation among generations, destroyed along with those who were destroyed." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/320). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/235): "In it are narrators whom I do not know."]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿So let him not commit excess in killing﴾, they said: its meaning is: the guardian should not commit excess in killing the killer, such as by mutilating him, or by exacting retaliation against someone other than the killer.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, he has been supported﴾, meaning that the guardian is supported against the killer by the Sharia, and in most cases by divine decree (qadar).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan, except in the best manner﴾, meaning: do not dispose of it except in a way that is beneficial to him. ﴿And do not consume their property along with your own. Indeed, that is a great sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 2]. And: ﴿Do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, [fearing] that they will grow up. And whoever is wealthy should abstain; and whoever is poor - let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾ [An-Nisa: 6].

It has been reported in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr: "O Abu Dharr, indeed I see you are weak, and indeed I love for you what I love for myself: do not take authority over two people, and do not manage the property of an orphan [[In another version: "a miser".]]" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1826).]].

* *

And His saying [the Exalted]: ﴿And fulfill the covenant﴾, meaning the covenant you make with people and the contracts by which you deal with them, for the covenant and the contract - each of them will be asked about by its party. ﴿Indeed, the covenant was ever [that about which one will be] questioned﴾, meaning: about it.

* *

And His saying [the Exalted]: ﴿And give full measure when you measure﴾, meaning: without shortchanging, and do not deprive people of their things. ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾. It was recited with a damma and a kasra on the qaf (al-qistas and al-qirtas), and it is the scale. Mujahid said: it is "al-adl" (justice) in Roman (Greek) language.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Straight﴾, meaning: that which has no crookedness, no deviation, and no instability.

﴿That is better﴾, meaning: for you in your livelihood and your return. Therefore He said: ﴿and better in result﴾, meaning: better in its outcome and final destination in your Hereafter.

Sa'id reported from Qatadah: ﴿That is better and best in result﴾, meaning: better in reward and consequence. As for Ibn Abbas, he used to say: "O assemblage of clients, you have been entrusted with two matters by which the people before you were destroyed: this measure and this scale." He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "No man is able to commit a sin and then leave it, with nothing prompting him except the fear of Allah, except that Allah will replace it for him in the immediate life of this world, before the Hereafter, with something better for him than that" [[It has come in Musnad Ahmad (5/78) from Abu Qatadah and Abu al-Dahma' from a man of the desert people that the Prophet (ﷺ) took his hand and said: "Indeed, you do not leave anything out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah gives you something better than it."]].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan, except in the best manner﴾, meaning: do not dispose of it except in a way that is beneficial to him. ﴿And do not consume their property along with your own. Indeed, that is a great sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 2]. And: ﴿Do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, [fearing] that they will grow up. And whoever is wealthy should abstain; and whoever is poor - let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾ [An-Nisa: 6].

It has been reported in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr: "O Abu Dharr, indeed I see you are weak, and indeed I love for you what I love for myself: do not take authority over two people, and do not manage the property of an orphan [[In another version: "a miser".]]" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (1826).]].

* *

And His saying [the Exalted]: ﴿And fulfill the covenant﴾, meaning the covenant you make with people and the contracts by which you deal with them, for the covenant and the contract - each of them will be asked about by its party. ﴿Indeed, the covenant was ever [that about which one will be] questioned﴾, meaning: about it.

* *

And His saying [the Exalted]: ﴿And give full measure when you measure﴾, meaning: without shortchanging, and do not deprive people of their things. ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾. It was recited with a damma and a kasra on the qaf (al-qistas and al-qirtas), and it is the scale. Mujahid said: it is "al-adl" (justice) in Roman (Greek) language.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Straight﴾, meaning: that which has no crookedness, no deviation, and no instability.

﴿That is better﴾, meaning: for you in your livelihood and your return. Therefore He said: ﴿and better in result﴾, meaning: better in its outcome and final destination in your Hereafter.

Sa'id reported from Qatadah: ﴿That is better and best in result﴾, meaning: better in reward and consequence. As for Ibn Abbas, he used to say: "O assemblage of clients, you have been entrusted with two matters by which the people before you were destroyed: this measure and this scale." He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "No man is able to commit a sin and then leave it, with nothing prompting him except the fear of Allah, except that Allah will replace it for him in the immediate life of this world, before the Hereafter, with something better for him than that" [[It has come in Musnad Ahmad (5/78) from Abu Qatadah and Abu al-Dahma' from a man of the desert people that the Prophet (ﷺ) took his hand and said: "Indeed, you do not leave anything out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah gives you something better than it."]].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "It means: do not say."

Al-Awfi narrated from him: "Do not accuse anyone of something you have no knowledge of."

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "It means false testimony."

Qatadah said: "Do not say: 'I saw,' when you did not see; 'I heard,' when you did not hear; or 'I knew,' when you did not know. For Allah will question you about all of that."

The gist of what they mentioned is that Allah the Exalted forbade speaking without knowledge, and this includes speaking on the basis of mere conjecture (zann), which is imagination and fancy, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Avoid much suspicion; indeed, some suspicion is sin﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 12]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 6066, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2563, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. In Sunan Abi Dawud: "Evil is the mount of a man: 'They claim...'" [[No. 4972.]]. In another hadith: "Among the greatest of slanders is that a man shows his eyes what they have not seen" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7043, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. In the Sahih also: "Whoever claims to have seen a dream he did not see will be commanded on the Day of Resurrection to tie together two barley grains, and he will never be able to do so" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7042, as a mu'allaq narration, and connected by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (8/215), from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿All of those﴾, meaning these faculties of hearing, sight and heart, ﴿each of them will be questioned about﴾, meaning the servant will be questioned about them on the Day of Resurrection, and will be questioned about what he did with them. It is permissible to use "ulā'ika" in place of "tilka," as the poet said [[He is Jarir ibn Atiyyah, and the verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/62).]]:

Blame the dwellings after the abode of al-Liwa,
and life after those days...

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, explaining the Most High's prohibition to His servants against arrogance and strutting in their gait:

﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾, meaning: strutting, swaying in gait like the tyrants. ﴿Indeed, you will never tear through the earth﴾, meaning: you will never cut through the earth with your walking. This is what Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said, and he cited as evidence the verse of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

"And a dark, deep abyss, hollow and pierced through."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/63).]

* *

As for His statement [Most High] [Addition from T.]: ﴿And you will never reach the mountains in height﴾, meaning: by your swaying, your pride, and your self-admiration. Rather, the doer of such may be repaid with the opposite of his intent, as is established in the Sahih: "While a man was walking among those who came before you, wearing two garments in which he strutted, the earth swallowed him up, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5789) and Sahih Muslim no. (2088), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Likewise, Allah [Most High] [Addition from F.] informed us about Qarun, that he went out to his people in his adornment, and that Allah the Most High caused the earth to swallow him and his home. In the hadith: "Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him up; he is small in his own eyes and great in the eyes of people. Whoever is arrogant, Allah abases him; he is great in his own eyes and small in the eyes of people, until he becomes more hateful to them than a dog or a pig." [Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (7/129) and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (2/110), through the route of Sa'id ibn Salam, from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim ibn Abis, from Rabi'ah, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, in similar wording. He said: "Gharib from the hadith of al-Thawri; it is transmitted solely by Sa'id ibn Salam, and he is a liar."]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said in his book "al-Khumul wa al-Tawadu'" (Obscurity and Humility): Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, who said: "While we were with al-Hasan, Ibn al-Ahtam passed by him, meaning al-Mansur, wearing a silk robe whose layers were piled one upon another over his leg, its front open, and he walked strutting. Al-Hasan looked at him and said: 'Uff, uff! Lofty with his nose, turning his side, turning his cheek away, looking at his own sides. What a fool, looking at his sides in blessings that are neither thanked nor mentioned, neither taken to account for by Allah's command regarding them, nor fulfilling Allah's right from them! By Allah, when one of them walks in his natural state, he sways like a madman; in every limb of his there is a blessing, and for Satan in him there is a curse.'" Ibn al-Ahtam heard him, returned apologizing to him, and said: "Do not apologize to me, but repent to your Lord. Have you not heard the saying of Allah the Most High: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear through the earth, and you will never reach the mountains in height﴾?" [Al-Khumul wa al-Tawadu' no. (237).]

Al-Bakhtari the worshipper saw a man from the family of 'Ali walking and swaggering in his gait, so he said to him: "O man, the One who honored you with it did not make this His way of walking!" He said: "The man then abandoned it afterwards."

Ibn 'Umar saw a man swaggering in his gait and said: "Indeed, the devils have brothers."

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: "Beware of swaggering, for a man's hand is [part] of the rest of his body." Both reports were narrated by Ibn Abi al-Dunya.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya also said: Khalaf ibn Hisham al-Bazzar narrated to us, Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Yahya, from Sa'id, from Yuhannas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When my nation walks the mutatta' (the proud gait), and Persia and Rome serve them, Allah will set some of them over others." [Al-Khumul wa al-Tawadu' no. (249), and it is mursal; it also came from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2261) through Zayd ibn al-Hubab from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah from Abdullah ibn Dinar from him, with the final wording "Allah will set the worst of them over the best of them." Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith."]

* *

As for His statement, the Most High: ﴿All that—its evil is hateful in the sight of your Lord﴾. As for the one who recited "sayyi'atun" (سَيِّئَةٌ), meaning: a grave sin. Its meaning then is: all of this which We have forbidden, from His statement ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾ up to here, is a sin for which one is held accountable, ﴿hateful﴾ in the sight of Allah, He does not love it nor is He pleased with it.

As for the one who recited ﴿sayyi'uhu﴾ with the idafah (construct), its meaning is: all of this which We mentioned from His statement ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him﴾ up to here, its evil, i.e., its ugliness, is hateful in the sight of Allah. Thus Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/63).]

Thus Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, explained it.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/63).]

This is Allah, the Exalted, saying: this is what We have commanded you of beautiful character and forbidden you of blameworthy traits, of what We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, that you may convey it to the people.

﴿And do not make with Allah another god, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.﴾ That is: your own self blames you [and Allah blames you][[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A.]] and the creation. ﴿Banished (madhuran)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: expelled.

The address in this verse is intended for the ummah through the Messenger ﷺ, for he, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, is protected from sin (ma'sum).

Allah says, refuting the lying polytheists who claim, may the curses of Allah be upon them, that the angels are the daughters of Allah.[[In F: "al-mukadhdhibin" (the deniers).]] They made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females, then claimed that they are the daughters of Allah, then worshipped them. In each of these three stages they erred greatly. Allah says, rebuking them: ﴿Has your Lord then favoured you with sons and taken for Himself females from among the angels?﴾ That is: has He singled you out with males, while taking for Himself, according to your claim, daughters? Then He intensified the rebuke against them, saying: ﴿Indeed, you utter a monstrous saying﴾, that is, in your claim that Allah has a son. Then you made His offspring the females, whom you yourselves are too disdainful to have, and you sometimes kill them by burying them alive. ﴿That, then, is an unjust division.﴾[[In T: "tu'allifun" (you cherish).]] Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something horrendous. The heavens are almost rent therefrom, and the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with [precise] counting. And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.﴾[[Addition from F.]] [Maryam: 88–95].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have certainly varied [the warnings] in this Qur'an that they may take heed﴾. That is: We have varied within it the warnings, so that they might be mindful of the proofs, clear evidences and admonitions contained in it, and thereby desist from the polytheism, wrongdoing and falsehood in which they are engaged. ﴿But it increases them in nothing except aversion﴾. That is: those of them who are wrongdoers are increased only in aversion from the truth and in distance from it.

He, exalted is He, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who claim that Allah has a partner from among His creation, and who worship others besides Him so that they may bring them closer to Him in nearness: "If the matter were as you say, and if there were with Him gods that are worshipped so that they bring one near to Him and intercede with Him, then those worshipped beings would themselves worship Him, draw near to Him, and seek the means (al-wasilah, the means of approach) and the nearness to Him. So worship Him alone, as those whom you call upon besides Him worship Him. You have no need of a worshipped being to be an intermediary between you and Him, for He does not love that, nor is He pleased with it; rather, He dislikes it and rejects it." He had forbidden this through the tongues of all His messengers and prophets.

Then He declared His noble Self free of imperfection and sanctified it, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they say﴾. That is, these polytheists, the transgressors and wrongdoers, in their claim that He has other gods with Him, ﴿exalted far above it﴾, that is, His exaltation is immense. Rather, He is Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal.

He, exalted is He, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who claim that Allah has a partner from among His creation, and who worship others besides Him so that they may bring them closer to Him in nearness: "If the matter were as you say, and if there were with Him gods that are worshipped so that they bring one near to Him and intercede with Him, then those worshipped beings would themselves worship Him, draw near to Him, and seek the means (al-wasilah, the means of approach) and the nearness to Him. So worship Him alone, as those whom you call upon besides Him worship Him. You have no need of a worshipped being to be an intermediary between you and Him, for He does not love that, nor is He pleased with it; rather, He dislikes it and rejects it." He had forbidden this through the tongues of all His messengers and prophets.

Then He declared His noble Self free of imperfection and sanctified it, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they say﴾. That is, these polytheists, the transgressors and wrongdoers, in their claim that He has other gods with Him, ﴿exalted far above it﴾, that is, His exaltation is immense. Rather, He is Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Allah, exalted is He, says: The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, that is, of the created beings, glorify Him, and declare Him free from what these polytheists say, and exalt Him, magnify Him, revere Him and proclaim His greatness, and they bear witness to His oneness in His lordship and His divinity:

*So in everything there is a sign of His,*
*pointing to the fact that He is One.*

As He said, exalted is He: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from it, and the earth is split open, and the mountains fall down in ruins, that they ascribe to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful that He should take a son.﴾ [Maryam: 90-92]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us, Miskin ibn Maymun, the muezzin of the Mosque of Ramla, narrated to us, Urwa ibn Ruwaym narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Qurt, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on the night he was taken by night to the Farthest Mosque, was between the Maqam and Zamzam, with Jibril on his right and Mika'il on his left, and he flew with him until he reached the seven heavens. When he returned he said: "I heard glorification in the highest heavens along with much glorification: *The highest heavens glorify the One of awe, fearful before the One of loftiness in what is exalted. Glory be to the Most High, the Highest, glory be to Him and exalted is He.*"

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise﴾, that is: there is not any created thing but it glorifies Allah with His praise. ﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾, that is: you do not understand their glorification, O people, because it is in a language other than your language. This applies generally to animals, plants and inanimate things, and this is the more well-known of the two opinions, as is established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "We used to hear the glorification of food while it was being eaten." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3579]

In the hadith of Abu Dhar: the Prophet (ﷺ) took some pebbles in his hand, and their glorification was heard like the humming of bees, and likewise in the hands of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them all. This is a well-known hadith in the Musnads. [Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, 4/415]

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, Zabban narrated to us, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he passed by some people who were standing beside their beasts and mounts, and he said to them: "Ride them while they are sound, and leave them while they are sound, and do not take them as seats for your conversations in the roads and markets, for a mount may be better than its rider and more remembrance of Allah than he is." [al-Musnad, 3/439]

In Sunan al-Nasa'i, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade killing frogs, and said: "Their croaking is glorification." [Sunan al-Nasa'i, 7/210, from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Qatada said, from Abd Allah ibn Babi, from Abd Allah ibn Amr: when a man says "There is no god but Allah," it is the word of sincerity, which Allah does not accept from anyone's deed until he says it. And when he says "Al-hamdu lillah (all praise is for Allah)," it is the word of gratitude, and no servant has ever thanked Allah until he says it. And when he says "Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest)," it fills what is between the heaven and the earth. And when he says "Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah)," it is the prayer of creation, by which Allah has made every creature pray and glorify. And when he says "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (There is no power and no strength except with Allah)," He says: My servant has submitted and surrendered.

Imam Ahmad said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, my father narrated to us, I heard al-Sa'qab ibn Zuhayr narrate from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: A bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) wearing a cloak of Tayalisa, edged with brocade, or embroidered with brocade, and said: "Your companion here wants to elevate every shepherd's son and lower every head's son." The Prophet (ﷺ) got up to him in anger, seized the edges of his cloak, pulled him, and said: "I do not see on you the garments of one who has no understanding." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned and sat down, and said: "When Nuh, peace be upon him, was approaching death, he called his two sons and said: I will recount to you the will: I command you with two things and forbid you from two things. I forbid you from associating partners with Allah and from arrogance, and I command you with 'La ilaha illa Allah (There is no god but Allah).' For if the heavens and the earth and what is between them were placed in one pan of a scale, and 'La ilaha illa Allah' were placed in the other pan, it would outweigh them. And if the heavens and the earth were a ring, and 'La ilaha illa Allah' were placed upon them, it would break them apart or crush them. And I command you with 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdih (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him),' for it is the prayer of every thing, and by it every thing is provided for." [al-Musnad, 2/225]

Imam Ahmad also narrated it, from Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from al-Sa'qab ibn Zuhayr, with the same chain, longer than this. He alone narrated it. [al-Musnad, 2/169]

Ibn Jarir said: Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Ya'la narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of something that Nuh commanded his son? Nuh, peace be upon him, said to his son: O my son, I command you to say 'Subhan Allah,' for it is the prayer of creation and the glorification of creation, and by it creation is provided for." Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/65] Its chain contains weakness, for al-Rabadhi is weak according to most scholars.

Ikrima said, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise﴾: He said: the pillar glorifies, and the tree glorifies, meaning the *ustuwana*, which is the column.

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: The creaking of the door is its glorification, and the gurgling of water is its glorification. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise﴾.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "Food glorifies."

The verse of prostration at the beginning of Surat al-Hajj supports this view.

Others said: Only that which has a spirit glorifies, meaning of animals or plants.

Qatada said regarding His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise﴾: every thing that has a spirit glorifies, whether a tree or something else.

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said regarding His saying: ﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with His praise﴾: both said: every thing that has a spirit.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadih and Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, both saying: Jarir Abu al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: We were with Yazid al-Raqashi, and al-Hasan was with him at a meal. They brought in the *khiwan* (table), and Yazid al-Raqashi said: "O Abu Sa'id, does this table glorify?" He said: "It used to glorify once." [Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/65]

I say: the *khiwan* is a table made of wood. It seems that al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, went to the view that while it was alive and had greenness, it used to glorify, and when it was cut and became dry dead wood, its glorification ceased. This opinion may find support in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by two graves and said: "They are being punished, and they are not being punished for a great matter. As for one of them, he did not guard himself from urine, and as for the other, he went about with tale-bearing." Then he took a fresh palm frond, split it into two halves, and planted one on each grave, and said: "Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as they have not dried out." [Agreed upon: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 218; Sahih Muslim, no. 292]

Some scholars who spoke on this hadith said: He only said "as long as they have not dried out" because they glorify as long as there is greenness in them; when they dry out, their glorification ceases. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying [exalted is He]: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾, that is: He [exalted is He] does not hasten to punish whoever disobeys Him, but gives him respite and reprieve. If he persists in his disbelief and obstinacy, He seizes him with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, as came in the two Sahihs: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿And such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe.﴾ [Hud: 102] Allah, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And how many a city did I give respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the destination.﴾ [al-Hajj: 48] Whoever desists from what he is engaged in of disbelief or disobedience, and returns to Allah and repents to Him, Allah will accept his repentance, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nisa': 110]

Here He said: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾, as He said at the end of Fatir: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving.﴾ Up to His saying: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they earned, He would not leave upon the earth a creature, but He defers them to an appointed term. And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants.﴾ [Fatir: 41-45]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 17, verses 45–46:

Allah says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "And when you recite the Qur'an, O Muhammad, to these polytheists, We place between you and them a hidden barrier."

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: it is the coverings (al-akinnah) over their hearts, as Allah says: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier."﴾ [Fussilat: 5], meaning: a preventing, intervening barrier that prevents anything of what you say from reaching us.

* *

As for His saying ﴿a hidden barrier﴾, it means "a concealing one" (satir), like maymun (blessed) and mash'um (ill-omened), meaning yamin (auspicious) and sha'im (inauspicious), because it comes from their right and left sides (yamin and sha'am).

It was also said: "hidden" means hidden from sight, so they cannot see it, yet it is nonetheless a barrier between them and guidance. Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) inclined to preferring this view.

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Abu Musa al-Harawi Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, from Yazid ibn Tadrus, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: When the verse ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad] was revealed, al-'Awra' Umm Jamil came, with a lump of [her] hand's stone (fihr) in her hand, and she was saying: "We have condemned Mudhammam (dispraised), we have disobeyed him, and we have rejected his command." (Abu Musa said: the doubt is from me, whether she said "atayna" or "abayna" — "we came" or "we refused"). The Messenger of Allah was sitting, and Abu Bakr was beside him — or he said: with him. Abu Bakr said: "This woman has come, and I fear she will see you." He (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, she will not see me," and he recited a Qur'an by which he sheltered himself from her: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier.﴾ She came until she stood over Abu Bakr, but she did not see the Prophet (ﷺ), and she said: "O Abu Bakr, I have been told that your companion has satirized me." Abu Bakr said: "No, by the Lord of this House, he did not satirize you." So she turned away, saying: "Quraysh has certainly known that I am the daughter of their chief."

[Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/53); authenticated by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Fath (7/169).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings (akinnah)﴾: it is the plural of kinan, which covers the heart, ﴿lest they understand it (yafqahuhu)﴾, meaning lest they comprehend the Qur'an, ﴿and in their ears is deafness (waqran)﴾, which is the heaviness that prevents them from hearing the Qur'an in a way that would benefit them and lead them to guidance.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an﴾, meaning: when you affirm the oneness of Allah in your recitation and say "There is no god but Allah," ﴿they turn away (wallaw) upon their backs in aversion (nufur)﴾, meaning they retreat turning their backs. Nufur is the plural of nafir, like qu'ud is the plural of qa'id. It may also be a verbal noun (masdar) from a verb not mentioned, and Allah knows best, as He says: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil, and when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾ [az-Zumar: 45].

Qatadah said regarding His saying ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away upon their backs in aversion﴾: when the Muslims said "There is no god but Allah," the polytheists denied it and it was grievous to them, and Iblis and his armies were distressed by it. But Allah would not allow anything but that it should be carried out, supported, made victorious, and made to prevail over whoever opposed it. It is a word by which whoever disputes with it prevails, and whoever fights with it is victorious. Only the people of this peninsula among the Muslims know it, the peninsula that a rider crosses in a few nights, and which a traveler journeys through for ages among people who do not know it nor acknowledge it.

Another view regarding the verse:

Ibn Jarir narrated: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhari' (al-Dharra') narrated to me, from Rawh ibn al-Musayyib Abu Raja' al-Kalbi, from Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away upon their backs in aversion﴾: they are the devils.

This is a very strange interpretation of it; otherwise, the devils, when the Qur'an is recited, or the adhan is called, or Allah is mentioned, turn away.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 17, verses 47–48:

God informs His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him, of what the chiefs of the disbelieving Quraysh conferred together about when they came to listen secretly to the recitation of the Messenger of God ﷺ, away from their people. What they said was that he is a man who has been bewitched (masḥūr), with sihr (magic) in its well-known sense, or from "al-saḥr" (السَّحْر), which is the lung (al-ri'ah). That is, "You follow nothing but a man (﴿إِلا بَشَرًا﴾) who eats and drinks, if you follow Muhammad." As the poet said:

"So if you ask us what we are, we are but sparrows among these people who are fed at dawn (al-musaḥḥar)."

And the rajaz poet said:

"We are fed (nusaḥḥar) with food and with drink."

That is, we are nourished. Ibn Jarir preferred this interpretation, but there is a problem with it, because they here meant only that he is bewitched and has a lung (ri'an) that brings him what they hear of the speech he recites. Some of them said "poet," some said "soothsayer," some said "madman," and some said "magician." For this reason God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you; so they have gone astray, and they cannot find a way﴾, that is, they are not guided to the truth, and they do not find a way out to it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the Sirah: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri told me that it was reported to him that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq ibn 'Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, an ally of the Banu Zuhrah, went out one night to listen to the Messenger of God ﷺ as he prayed at night in his house. Each of them took a place where he could listen, and each did not know where his companion was. They spent the night listening to him, until dawn broke, and then they dispersed. Then the road brought them together, and they blamed one another, and some said to others: "Do not return, for if some of your foolish young men see you, you will put something into their hearts." Then they left. The next night each man returned to his place and they spent the night listening to him, until dawn broke, and then they dispersed. Then the road brought them together again, and some said to others the same as they had said the first time. Then they left. On the third night, each man took his place, and they spent the night listening to him, until dawn broke, and then they dispersed. The road brought them together, and some said to others: "We will not leave until we make a pact that we will not return." So they made that pact, and then they dispersed.

When morning came, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff, went out, and came to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in his house, and said: "Tell me, O Abu Hanzalah, your opinion of what you heard from Muhammad." He said: "O Abu Tha'labah, by God, I heard things that I recognize and understand what is meant by them, and I heard things whose meaning I did not understand, nor what is meant by them." Al-Akhnas said: "And I, by the One I swear by." Then he left him and went to Abu Jahl, entered upon him in his house, and said: "O Abu al-Hakam, what is your opinion of what you heard from Muhammad?" He said: "What have I heard? We and the Banu 'Abd Manaf have competed for honor. They fed, and we fed; they carried, and we carried; they gave, and we gave; until when we were kneeling side by side like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven. When will we attain this?' By God, we will never believe in him or accept him." Al-Akhnas then rose from him and left him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the Sirah: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri told me that it was reported to him that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq ibn 'Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, an ally of the Banu Zuhrah, went out one night to listen to the Messenger of God ﷺ as he prayed at night in his house. Each of them took a place where he could listen, and each did not know where his companion was. They spent the night listening to him, until dawn broke, and then they dispersed. Then the road brought them together, and they blamed one another, and some said to others: "Do not return, for if some of your foolish young men see you, you will put something into their hearts." Then they left. The next night each man returned to his place and they spent the night listening to him, until dawn broke, and then they dispersed. Then the road brought them together again, and some said to others the same as they had said the first time. Then they left. On the third night, each man took his place, and they spent the night listening to him, until dawn broke, and then they dispersed. The road brought them together, and some said to others: "We will not leave until we make a pact that we will not return." So they made that pact, and then they dispersed.

When morning came, al-Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff, went out, and came to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in his house, and said: "Tell me, O Abu Hanzalah, your opinion of what you heard from Muhammad." He said: "O Abu Tha'labah, by God, I heard things that I recognize and understand what is meant by them, and I heard things whose meaning I did not understand, nor what is meant by them." Al-Akhnas said: "And I, by the One I swear by." Then he left him and went to Abu Jahl, entered upon him in his house, and said: "O Abu al-Hakam, what is your opinion of what you heard from Muhammad?" He said: "What have I heard? We and the Banu 'Abd Manaf have competed for honor. They fed, and we fed; they carried, and we carried; they gave, and we gave; until when we were kneeling side by side like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven. It is also related in another narration: "Be whatever you wish, and Allah will restore you after your death."

In the tafsir transmitted from Imam Malik, from al-Zuhri, regarding His words ﴿or a creation of what is greater in your breasts﴾, it occurs that he said: "The Prophet (ﷺ)." Malik said: "And they say it is death."

* *

His words ﴿Then they will say, "Who will restore us?"﴾ mean: who will restore us when we are stones, or iron, or another creation, hard? ﴿Say, "He who produced you the first time."﴾ That is, He who created you when you were not a thing worth mentioning, then you became human beings, dispersing. He is capable of restoring you, whatever state you have come to. ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [al-Rum: 27].

* *

His words ﴿Then they will shake their heads at you﴾: Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: they will move them in mockery.

What the two of them said is what the Arabs understand from their languages, because al-inghad (الإنغاض) is movement from below upward or from above downward. From this comes the name for the young ostrich (al-zalim, الظليم), which is the offspring of the ostrich: nagdan (نغضًا), because when it walks it hurries in its gait and moves its head. It is said: "His tooth shook (naghadat sinuhu) when it moved and rose from its socket." The rajaz poet says:

*"And her teeth loosened from the decay of old age..."* [[The rajaz verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/70).]]

* *

His words ﴿And they say, "When is it?"﴾ are a report about them, that they consider its occurrence far-fetched, as He said: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ [al-Mulk: 25], and He said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Shura: 18].

* *

His words ﴿Say, "It may be that it is near."﴾ That is: beware of it, for it is near to you, and it will come to you without doubt, since whatever is to come is coming.

* *

His words ﴿The Day He calls you﴾, that is, the Lord, exalted is He, ﴿with a call from the earth, when you come out﴾ [al-Rum: 25]. That is, when He commands you to come out of it, He cannot be opposed or prevented. Rather, as He said: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50], ﴿Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [al-Nahl: 40], and He said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 13–14]. That is, it is only one command with a single roar, and then people have come out from the inside of the earth to its surface, as He said: ﴿The Day He calls you, and you respond with His praise﴾, that is, you will all rise in response to His command and in obedience to His will.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and you respond with His praise﴾ means: by His command. Ibn Jurayj also said likewise.

Qatadah said: "By knowing Him and obeying Him."

Some of them said: ﴿The Day He calls you and you respond with His praise﴾ means: and to Him belongs praise in every state. It has come in a hadith: "There is no loneliness upon the people of 'There is no god but Allah' in their graves. It is as if I see the people of 'There is no god but Allah' rising from their graves, shaking the dust from their heads, saying: 'There is no god but Allah.'" In another narration they say: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾ [Fatir: 34]. It will come in Surah Fatir, if Allah the Exalted wills.

* *

His words ﴿And you will think﴾, that is, on the day you rise from your graves, ﴿that you remained [in the worldly life] only a little﴾. Just as He said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. He also said: ﴿The Day the Horn is blown, and We gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed. They will whisper among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days]. We are most knowing of what they say, when their best in conduct says, 'You remained not but a day.'"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102–104] He said: ﴿And the Day the Hour is established, the criminals will swear they remained not but an hour. Thus they were deluded﴾ [al-Rum: 55]. And He said: ﴿He will say, "How long did you remain on earth, counting years?" They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day, so ask those who count." He will say, "You remained only a little, if you had known"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112–114].

Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger ﷺ to instruct the believing servants of Allah that they should speak to one another in their addresses and conversations with the best speech and the good word. For when they do not do this, Satan stirs up discord between them, and turns speech into action, and evil, enmity and fighting occur. Indeed, Satan has been an enemy to Adam and his offspring since he refused to prostrate to Adam, so his enmity is manifest and clear. For this reason he forbade a man to point to his Muslim brother with an iron object, for Satan may incite (yanzaghu) in his hand, meaning that he may thereby strike him.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you should point to his brother with a weapon, for none of you knows, perhaps Satan may incite (yanzi') in his hand, and he falls into a pit of Fire."

Both al-Bukhari and Muslim related it through the narration of Abd al-Razzaq. [[Al-Musnad (2/317), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7073) and Sahih Muslim no. (2617).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from al-Hasan who said: A man from the Banu Salit narrated to me, saying: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in a crowd of people, and I heard him say: "The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him nor forsake him. Piety is here" — [Hammad said: and he pointed to his chest — "two men do not love each other for the sake of Allah and then separate except because of an innovation (hadath) one of them introduces, and the innovator is evil, the innovator is evil, the innovator is evil."]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Your Lord knows best about you﴾, O people, who among you deserves guidance and who does not deserve it. ﴿If He wills, He will have mercy upon you﴾ by granting you success in obeying Him and turning back to Him, ﴿or if He wills, He will punish you﴾. ﴿And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad]¹ over them as a guardian﴾. That is: We have only sent you as a warner. Whoever obeys you enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys you enters the Fire.

* *

His saying: ﴿And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their ranks in obedience and disobedience. ﴿And We certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾, as He said: ﴿Those messengers, We preferred some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253].

This does not contradict what is established in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Do not prefer one prophet over another"² . The intended meaning of that is preference based merely on whim and partisanship, not preference based on evidence. When evidence indicates something, it must be followed. There is no disagreement that the messengers are more excellent than the rest of the prophets, and that the steadfast messengers (Ulul-'Azm) are the most excellent of them. They are the five mentioned explicitly in two verses of the Qur'an, in Surah al-Ahzab: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7], and in Ash-Shura, in His saying: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not become divided therein﴾ [ash-Shura: 13]. There is no disagreement that Muhammad ﷺ is the most excellent of them, then after him Abraham, then Moses according to the well-known view. We have expanded on this with its evidences in other than this place, and Allah is the Granter of success.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We gave David the Psalms﴾ is an indication of his virtue and nobility.

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The recitation was made light for David. He would order his mount to be saddled, and he would finish reciting before it was saddled." That is, the Qur'an³ .

² Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3414), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2373), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.
³ Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4713).

The Most High says: ﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, to these polytheists who worship other than Allah: ﴿Call upon those you claim besides Him﴾, from among the idols and the rivals, ﴿so turn to them. Indeed, they do not possess the removal of harm from you﴾ meaning entirely, ﴿nor any transfer﴾ meaning, they cannot transfer it to anyone other than you.

The meaning is that the One who has power over all this is Allah alone, with no partner, the One to whom belong creation and command.

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Say, "Call upon those you claim besides Him, and they do not possess the removal of harm from you, nor any transfer."﴾ He said: The people of polytheism used to say, "We worship the angels, al-Masih (the Messiah), and 'Uzayr (Ezra)," and these are the ones they call upon, meaning the angels, al-Masih, and 'Uzayr.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of nearness to their Lord, [as to] which of them would be nearest﴾. Al-Bukhari narrated, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abdullah concerning His words: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of nearness to their Lord﴾. He said: They were some people among the jinn who were worshipped, and then they embraced Islam. In another narration he said: There were some people from mankind who used to worship some people from the jinn, and then the jinn embraced Islam, while these people held fast to their religion. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4714, 4715).]]

Qatadah said, from Ma'bad ibn 'Abdullah al-Zimmani [in T: "Sa'id"; in T and F: "al-Rummani"], from 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Mas'ud concerning His words: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of nearness to their Lord﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of the jinn. Then the jinn embraced Islam, while the humans who worshipped them did not perceive their Islam, so this verse was revealed.

In another narration from Ibn Mas'ud: They used to worship a class of angels called the jinn, and he mentioned it.

Al-Suddi said, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of nearness to their Lord, [as to] which of them would be nearest﴾. He said: 'Isa (Jesus) and his mother, and 'Uzayr.

Mughirah said, from Ibrahim: Ibn 'Abbas used to say concerning this verse: They are 'Isa, 'Uzayr, the sun, and the moon.

Mujahid said: 'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels.

Ibn Jarir chose the view of Ibn Mas'ud, because of His words: ﴿seek means of nearness to their Lord﴾, and this [wording] is not used for the past, so 'Isa and 'Uzayr are not included in it. He said: Al-Wasilah (the means of nearness) is closeness, as Qatadah said; and for this reason He said: ﴿which of them would be nearest﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾: worship is not complete except with fear and hope. With fear one refrains from what is forbidden, and with hope one is driven to acts of obedience.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared﴾, meaning it should be guarded against, and one should fear its occurrence and taking place, seeking refuge in Allah from it.
