* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is something to be feared﴾, meaning it should be guarded against, and one should fear its occurrence and taking place, seeking refuge in Allah from it.

This is an announcement from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He has decreed and determined, by what He has already written with Him in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), that there is no town but that He will destroy it, by annihilating all its people or punishing them ﴿with a severe punishment﴾, whether by killing or by affliction, as He wills. This only happens because of their sins and their wrongdoings. As He said about the past nations: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ [Hud: 101]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment. So it tasted the consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 7, 8].

Sunayd said, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The polytheists said, "O Muhammad, you claim that there were prophets before you. Among them was one for whom the wind was subjected, and among them was one who used to bring the dead back to life. If you want us to believe in you and affirm you, then ask your Lord to make Safa gold for us." Then Allah revealed to him: "I have heard what they have said. If you wish, We will do what they have said; but if they do not believe, the punishment will descend, for after the descent of the sign there is no further debate. Or if you wish, We will give your people respite, and We will grant them a delay." He said: "O Lord, grant them respite."

Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj and others said the same.

Imam Ahmad said: Uthman ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas (in manuscripts F and A: "Ibn Abi Iyas"), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to make Safa gold for them and to remove the mountains from them so that they could farm. It was said to him: "If you wish, We will give them respite; and if you wish, We will give them what they asked for. But if they disbelieve, they will be destroyed as the nations before them were destroyed." He said: "No, rather, grant them respite." And Allah revealed: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her.﴾ This was related by al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Jarir, with the same chain.

Imam Ahmad also said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Imran Abu al-Hakim (in manuscript H: "Imran ibn Hakim"; the correction is from the Atraf of al-Musnad and the books of biographical evaluation), from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Ask your Lord to make Safa gold for us, and we will believe in you." He said: "Will you really do so?" They said: "Yes." He said: So he supplicated, and Jibril came to him and said: "Your Lord conveys His greetings to you and says: If you wish, Safa will become gold for them; but whoever among them disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, the door of repentance and mercy."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said in his Musnad: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ali al-Ansari narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Tamim al-Misisi narrated to us, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn Ammar al-Ayli, from Abdullah ibn Ata ibn Ibrahim, from his grandmother Umm Ata, the freed woman of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: I heard al-Zubayr say: When this was revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214], the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out from Abu Qubays: "O family of Abd Manaf, I am a warner!" The Quraysh came to him, and he warned them and admonished them. They said: "You claim that you are a prophet to whom revelation is sent, and that Sulayman had the wind and the mountains subjected to him, that Musa had the sea subjected to him, and that Isa used to bring the dead to life. So ask Allah to remove these mountains from us and to make the earth burst forth rivers for us, so that we may make them into farmland and plant and eat. And if not, ask Allah to bring back to life our dead, so that we may speak with them and they may speak with us. And if not, ask Allah to turn this rock beneath you into gold, so that we may carve from it and be spared the journeys of winter and summer, for you claim that you are like them!" He said: While we were around him, revelation descended upon him. When it had passed from him, he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, He has given me what you asked for; and if I wished, it would have been. But He gave me the choice between your entering the door of mercy, so that your believer may be made secure, and His leaving you to what you have chosen for yourselves, so that you would stray from the door of mercy and none of you would be secure. So I chose the door of mercy, so that your believer may be made secure. And He informed me that if He gives you that and you then disbelieve, He will punish you with a punishment that He will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds." And it was revealed: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾

And [the revelation continued] until he recited three verses, and then this was revealed: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split, or the dead could be spoken to...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31]. [Al-Musnad of Abu Ya'la (2/40). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/85): "Abu Ya'la related it through the chain of Abd al-Jabbar ibn Umar al-Ayli, from Abdullah ibn Ata ibn Ibrahim. Both were deemed trustworthy, but the majority of scholars have declared them weak."]

For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs﴾, meaning: We would send the signs and bring them as your people asked of you, for that is easy for Us and not difficult in Our sight. But the former peoples denied them after they had asked for them, and Our way with them and with those like them was that they would not be given respite if they denied them after their descent, as Allah, exalted is He, said in al-Ma'idah: ﴿Allah said: Indeed, I will send it down upon you. But whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will surely punish him with a punishment that I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 115]. And He, exalted is He, said concerning Thamud, when they asked for a sign: a she-camel that would come out from a rock which they specified. So Salih supplicated to his Lord, and He brought forth for him from it a she-camel as they had asked. But they "wronged her," meaning they disbelieved in the One who created her, denied His messenger, and hamstrung the she-camel. So He said: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise not to be denied.﴾ [Hud: 65]. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel﴾, meaning as a clear proof of the oneness of the One who created her and as confirmation of the Messenger whose supplication was answered through her. ﴿But they wronged her﴾, meaning they disbelieved in her, prevented her from drinking, and killed her. So Allah annihilated them to the last one, took vengeance upon them, and seized them with the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, Qatadah said: Allah frightens people with whatever of His signs He wills, so that perhaps they will take heed, remember, and return. It was mentioned to us that Kufa was shaken in the time of Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: "O people, your Lord is asking you to make amends, so make amends to Him."

Similarly, it is related that Medina was shaken several times in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Umar said: "You have done something new! By Allah, if it returns, I will certainly do such-and-such." And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in the hadith agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim): "Indeed, the sun and the moon are two of the signs of Allah, and they do not eclipse for the death or the life of anyone. But Allah, mighty and majestic, sends them to frighten His servants. So when you see that, turn to His remembrance, His supplication, and His forgiveness." Then he said: "O community of Muhammad, by Allah, there is none more jealous than Allah when His servant commits adultery or His female servant commits adultery. O community of Muhammad, by Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." [Sahih al-Bukhari (1044) and Sahih Muslim (901).]

Allah says to His Messenger ﷺ, urging him to convey his message and informing him that He has protected him from the people, for He is the One who has power over them, and they are within His grip and under His subjugation and dominion.

Mujahid, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said concerning His words: ﴿And [remember] when We told you that your Lord has encompassed the people﴾

That is: He protected you from them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾, al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾ He said: "It is a vision of the eye which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [[In F: "the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace."]] was shown on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), ﴿and the accursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, the tree of Zaqqum." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4716).]]

Similarly, Ahmad and Abd al-Razzaq and others related it from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with this chain [[al-Musnad (1/221).]]. Likewise, al-Awfi related it from Ibn Abbas. Thus did Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Masruq, Ibrahim, Qatadah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd and others besides them interpret it as the Night of the Isra'. The hadiths of the Isra' have already been mentioned in full at the beginning of the surah, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. It has also been mentioned that some people turned back from their religion after they had been upon the truth, because their hearts and minds could not bear that; so they denied what they had not encompassed in knowledge, while Allah made it a source of firmness and certainty for others. For this reason He said: ﴿except as a trial﴾, that is, a test and an examination. As for "the accursed tree", it is the tree of Zaqqum, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed them that he had seen Paradise and Hellfire, and saw the tree of Zaqqum; and they denied this, until Abu Jahl, may Allah curse him, said: "Bring us dates and butter," and he began eating this with that and said: "Tazaqqamu (eat the Zaqqum)." We know of no Zaqqum other than this.

This was related by Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Abu Malik, al-Hasan al-Basri and others, and everyone who said that it was the Night of the Isra' interpreted it in this way as the tree of Zaqqum.

It has also been said that the intended "accursed tree" is the Banu Umayyah. But this is strange and weak.

Ibn Jarir said: It was related to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabalah, who said: Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from my father, from my grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the sons of so-and-so leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that grieved him, and he was never seen laughing again until he died. He said: And Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾, to the end of the verse. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/77).]]

This chain is extremely weak, for Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabalah is abandoned (matruk), and his shaykh is also entirely weak. For this reason Ibn Jarir chose that the intended meaning is the Night of the Isra', and that the accursed tree is the tree of Zaqqum, saying: because of the consensus of the authoritative scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) upon this, namely regarding the vision and the tree.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We warn them﴾, that is, the disbelievers, with threat, punishment and retribution, ﴿but it only increases them in great transgression﴾, that is, persistence in the disbelief and misguidance they are in. And that is from Allah's abandonment of them.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) mentions the enmity of Iblis (may Allah curse him) toward Adam (peace be upon him) and his descendants, and that this enmity is ancient, dating back to the creation of Adam. When Allah commanded the angels to prostrate, they all prostrated except Iblis, who was arrogant and refused to prostrate to him, out of pride over him and contempt for him. ﴿He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ as He said in another verse: ﴿"I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay."﴾ [al-A'raf: 12].

He also said: ﴿"Have You considered?"﴾ He speaks to the Lord with audacity and disbelief, while the Lord is forbearing and watching. ﴿He said, "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few."﴾

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "He says: 'I will surely take control over his descendants, except for a few.'"

Mujahid said: "I will surely overpower them." Ibn Zayd said: "I will surely lead them astray."

All of these are close in meaning, and the sense is: he says, "Have You considered this one whom You have honored and exalted above me? If You give me respite, I will surely lead his descendants astray, except for a few of them."

As He said in another verse: ﴿He said, "Indeed you are among those granted respite, until the Day of the Appointed Time"﴾ [al-Hijr: 37-38]. Then He threatened him and those among the offspring of Adam who follow him with Hell, saying: ﴿As for those who follow you among them, Hell will be your recompense, a full recompense﴾, meaning: for your deeds, ﴿a full recompense﴾.

Mujahid said: "Complete." Qatadah said: "Fully given to you, nothing will be reduced from it for you."

* *

Regarding His saying: ﴿And incite whoever you can among them with your voice﴾, it was said: this is singing. Mujahid said: with frivolity and singing, meaning: lead them astray with that.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His saying: ﴿And incite whoever you can among them with your voice﴾: "Every caller who calls to disobedience of Allah, mighty and majestic is He." Qatadah said likewise, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view.

* *

Regarding His saying: ﴿And muster against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾, it means: bring against them your armies, their horsemen and their foot soldiers. The word "rijl" (infantry) is the plural of "rajil" (on foot), just as "rakb" (riders) is the plural of "rakib" (rider), and "sahb" (companions) is the plural of "sahib" (companion).

Its meaning is: empower over them with everything you are able to. This is a matter of divine decree, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do you not see that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?﴾ [Maryam: 83], meaning: they provoke them to sins with provocation and drive them towards them with driving. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿And muster against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾: "Every rider and walker in disobedience of Allah."

Qatadah said: "He has cavalry and infantry from among the jinn and mankind, who obey him."

The Arabs say: "So-and-so incited (ajlaba) against so-and-so," meaning: when he shouted at him. From this comes the saying: "He forbade in racing the *jalab* and the *janab*," and from it is derived *al-jalabah*, which is the raising of voices.

* *

Regarding His saying: ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: it is what he commanded them of spending wealth in acts of disobedience to Allah.

'Ata' said: it is usury (riba). Al-Hasan said: it is gathering it from what is impure and spending it on what is forbidden. Qatadah said likewise.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: As for his sharing with them in their wealth, it is what they forbade of their livestock, meaning: the bahirah, the sa'ibah and the like. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said likewise.

Then Ibn Jarir said: "The most appropriate view is that the verse encompasses all of that."

* *

Regarding His saying: ﴿And in children﴾, al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and al-Dahhak: it means children born of fornication.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: it is what they killed of their children out of foolishness, without knowledge.

Qatadah related from al-Hasan al-Basri: "By Allah, he has indeed shared with them in wealth and children: they became Magians, Jews and Christians, and dyed themselves with other than the dye of Islam, and they set aside a portion of their wealth for Satan." Qatadah said the same.

Abu Salih related from Ibn 'Abbas: it is their naming their children "Abd al-Harith", "Abd Shams" and "Abd so-and-so."

Ibn Jarir said: "The most correct of the views is that it should be said: every child a woman bears, in which Allah is disobeyed, by naming him with what Allah dislikes, or by bringing him into a religion other than that which Allah has approved, or by fornication with his mother, or by killing him and burying him alive, and other such matters by which Allah is disobeyed through acting upon him or in him, then he has entered into sharing with Iblis in that child, from the child's own offspring or from him; because Allah, in His saying: ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, did not specify the sense of sharing in it to one meaning over another. So everything in which Allah is disobeyed, or in which Satan is obeyed, is a form of sharing."

This view which he stated is sound, and each of the early scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, explained some aspect of this sharing. It is established in Sahih Muslim, from 'Iyad ibn Himar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, mighty and majestic, says: 'I created My servants as ḥunafa' (upright), then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and made unlawful for them what I had made lawful for them.'" [Sahih Muslim, no. 2865.]

And in the two Sahihs, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If any one of them, when he wishes to have intercourse with his wife, says: 'In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You provide us,' then if a child is decreed between them, Satan will never harm him." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 141; Sahih Muslim, no. 1434.]

* *

Regarding His saying: ﴿And promise them, but Satan promises them only delusion﴾, as Allah, the Exalted, informed about Iblis that he will say when the truth is made manifest on the Day when judgment is passed in truth: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. Allah, the Exalted, informs about His kindness toward His creation in subjecting the ships (al-fulk) at sea to His servants, and in making them easy for them, for the benefit of His servants, so that they may seek of His bounty through trade from one region to another. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you.﴾ That is: He has done this for you only out of His bounty upon you and His mercy toward you.

It informs us, may He be exalted, that when harm touches people, they call upon Him, turning to Him in repentance and sincerely devoting religion to Him. For this reason He said: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish from you except Him﴾. That is, every other thing you worship besides Allah leaves your hearts. This is what happened to Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl when he fled from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the conquest of Makkah. He fled and boarded a ship at sea to reach Abyssinia. A violent wind came upon them [[In F: "فجاءهم" ("came upon them")]]. The people said to one another: "Surely nothing will avail you except that you call upon Allah alone." Ikrimah said to himself: "By Allah, if nothing else helps at sea, then nothing else will help on land. O Allah, I make a covenant with You: if You deliver me from this, I will surely go and place my hand in his hand, and I will certainly find him kind and merciful." They came out of the sea, and he returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), embraced Islam, and his Islam was good. May Allah be pleased with him and content him.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then when He brings you safely to land, you turn away﴾. That is, you forgot the Tawhid you recognised at sea, and you turned away from calling upon Him alone, with no partner.

﴿And man has always been ungrateful﴾. That is, this is his disposition: he forgets the blessings and denies them, except those whom Allah protects.

Allah, the Exalted, says: "Do you feel secure that He will not cause you to go back to the land, and then send upon you a violent wind that drowns you for your disbelief? Then you would find none to pursue you for it against Us." Or do you feel secure that He will not make the side of the land swallow you up, or send against you a hasasib (a storm of stones)?

Ibn Kathir's commentary:

Allah, the Exalted, says: "Do you think that We will take you back to the land [[In T: "that He will bring them out", and in F and A: "that He will bring you out".]] and that you will be safe from His vengeance and His punishment?"

﴿Lest He cause the side of the land to swallow you up, or send against you a violent wind (ḥāṣib)﴾, and this is: rain containing stones. This was said by Mujahid and others. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind, except the family of Lot; We saved them before dawn﴾ [al-Qamar: 34]. And in another verse He said: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾ [[In T, F and A: "of clay", which is an error.]] [Hud: 82]. And He said: ﴿Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you, and behold, it shakes? Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a violent wind? Then you will know how My warning was﴾ [al-Mulk: 16, 17].

* *

His saying: ﴿Then you will not find for yourselves a guardian (wakīl)﴾ means: a helper who will turn that away from you and rescue you from it. [And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, knows best.] [[Addition from F.]]

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do you feel secure﴾ O you who turn away from Us, after you acknowledged Our Oneness at sea and then came out onto the land [[In another manuscript: "to the dust."]] ﴿that He will cause you to return to it [the sea] a second time, and send against you a violent wind (qasif) from the wind﴾, meaning, a wind that breaks the masts and sinks the ships.

Ibn Abbas and others said: al-qasif is the sea wind that breaks the ships and drowns them [[In another manuscript: "the seafarers." In manuscript F: "breaks the ships and drowns them."]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and drown you because of your disbelief﴾ [[In another manuscript: "then He drowns you." In manuscript F: "so He drowns you."]], meaning, because of your disbelief and your turning away from Allah the Exalted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿then you will not find for yourselves any avenger against Us for it﴾, Ibn Abbas said: "a helper."

Mujahid said: "a helper seeking vengeance," meaning, one who will take revenge for you after you.

Qatadah said: "We do not fear anyone who will pursue us for anything of that."

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 17, verse 70:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of His honouring of the children of Adam and His ennobling of them, in creating them in the best and most complete form, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4]. That is, he walks upright, standing on his two feet, and eats with his hands, whereas other animals walk on four limbs and eat with their mouths. He gave him hearing, sight and heart (fu'ad), by which he understands all of this, benefits from it, distinguishes between things, and knows their benefits, properties and harms, in worldly and religious matters.

﴿And We carried them on the land﴾ [[Variant in B and C: "on the land and the sea".]] That is, on beasts of burden: camels, horses and mules. And "on the sea" also means on large and small ships.

﴿And provided for them of the good things﴾: that is, of crops and fruits, meats and milk, of all kinds of foods and flavours that are desirable and delicious, of pleasing sights, and of fine clothing [[Variant in B: "raised" (al-murtafi'a).]] of every kind, in their many types, colours and shapes, both what they make for themselves and what others bring to them from the distant regions and areas.

﴿And preferred them above many of those whom We created, with [marked] preference﴾: that is, above all animals and all kinds of created beings.

This verse has been cited as evidence for the superiority of the human race over the race of angels. 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: The angels said: "O Lord, You have given the children of Adam this world, they eat from it and enjoy it, and You have not given us this, so give it to us in the Hereafter." Allah said: "By My might and My majesty, I will not make the righteous of the offspring of those whom I created with My hand like those to whom I said: 'Be,' and they were."

This hadith is mursal (a report in which the chain omits the Companion who narrated from the Prophet) through this route, but it has been transmitted through another route, connected.

Al-Hafiz (the memoriser of hadith) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sadaqa al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Khalid al-Misisi narrated to us; Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutarrif narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The angels said: 'O Lord, You gave the children of Adam this world; they eat in it, drink, and wear clothing, while we glorify You with Your praise and do not eat, drink or amuse ourselves. So, just as You gave them the world, give us the Hereafter.' He said: 'I will not make the righteous of the offspring of those whom I created with My hand like those to whom I said: "Be," and they were.'"
[[In its chain is Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Misisi, who is a liar. It was also narrated in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 87), Majma' al-Bahrayn, through the route of Talha ibn Zayd, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, with the same wording, and he said: "No one narrated it from Safwan except Talha, and Abu Ghassan Muhammad ibn Mutarrif." Its chain includes Talha ibn Zayd, who is a liar.]]

Ibn 'Asakir narrated through the route of Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Razi: al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Khalaf al-Saydalani narrated to us; Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us; 'Uthman ibn Hisn ibn 'Ubayda ibn 'Ulaq narrated to me; I heard 'Urwa ibn Ruwaym al-Lakhmi, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to me, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The angels said: 'Our Lord, You created us and You created the children of Adam, and You made them eat food, drink drink, wear garments, marry women, ride beasts, sleep and rest, but You have not given us any of that. So give them the world and give us the Hereafter.' Allah, exalted and majestic, said: 'I will not make the one whom I created with My hand and into whom I breathed of My spirit like the one to whom I said: "Be," and he was.'"
[[Al-Hindi mentioned it in Kanz al-'Ummal (12/191) and attributed it to Ibn 'Asakir from the hadith of Anas. It has also come through another route: al-Tabarani narrated it in Musnad al-Shamiyyin through the route of Ahmad ibn Ya'la, from Hisham ibn 'Ammar, from 'Uthman ibn 'Ulaq, who said: I heard 'Urwa ibn Ruwaym narrate from Jabir, and so he mentioned it. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat through the route of Junayd ibn Hakim, from Hisham ibn 'Ammar, from 'Abd Rabbih ibn Salih, who said: I heard 'Urwa ibn Ruwaym narrate from Jabir, and so he mentioned it. End of quotation, as cited by al-Zayla'i in his book Takhrij al-Kashshaf.]]

Al-Tabarani also said: 'Abdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us; 'Umar ibn Sahl narrated to us; 'Ubayd Allah ibn Tammam narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Bishr ibn Shighaf, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Nothing is more honoured by Allah on the Day of Resurrection than the son of Adam." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, not even the angels?" He said: "Not even the angels; the angels are compelled, in the position of the sun and the moon."
[[Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/82): "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir, and in its chain is 'Ubayd Allah ibn Tammam, who is weak."]] This hadith is extremely strange (gharib jiddan).

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 71–72:

He, may He be blessed and exalted, informs us about the Day of Resurrection: that He will call every nation to account through their imam.

The scholars differed regarding this. Mujahid and Qatadah said: that is, through their prophet (nabi). This is like His saying: ﴿For every nation there is a messenger. When their messenger comes, judgment will be made between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus: 47].

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) said: This is the greatest honour for the people of hadith (ahl al-hadith), because their imam is the Prophet ﷺ.

Ibn Zayd said: through their Book that was revealed to their prophet, concerning the legislation (al-tashri').

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view, and it is narrated from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he said: through their books. It is possible that he meant this, and that he meant what al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿The Day We will call every people by their imam﴾, that is: by the book of their deeds. Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise. This view is the most preponderant (al-arjah), because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have enumerated everything in a clear imam﴾ [Ya-Sin: 12]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling; every nation will be called to its record. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do. This is Our Book, which speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have transcribed what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 28–29].

This does not preclude that the Prophet will be brought when Allah judges among his nation, for he must be a witness over them concerning their deeds, as He said: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the martyrs will be brought﴾ [al-Zumar: 69], and He said: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you against these as a witness?﴾ [al-Nisa: 41].

But the intended meaning of the imam here is the book of deeds; for this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The Day We will call every people by their imam. Whoever is given his record in his right hand, those will read their record﴾, that is: out of their joy and happiness at what is in it of righteous deeds, they read it and love to read it, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account."﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "I wish I had not been given my record and had not known my account."﴾ [al-Haqqah: 19–26].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will not be wronged, even as much as the thread in a date-pit﴾, it has already been mentioned that the "fatil" is the thin thread running along the split of the date-stone.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated a hadith on this, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'mar [in some manuscripts: Ma'mar] and Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Karamah told us, they said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa told us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ concerning Allah's saying: ﴿The Day We will call every people by their imam﴾. He said: "One of them will be called, and his book will be given to him in his right hand, and his body will be extended for him, and his face will be made bright, and a crown of pearls will be placed on his head, glittering. He will set out to his companions, and they will see him from afar, and they will say: 'O Allah, bring him to us, and bless us with him.' He will come to them and say to them: 'Rejoice, for each of you has the like of this.' As for the disbeliever, his face will be blackened, and his body will be extended for him, and his companions will see him and say: 'We seek refuge in Allah from this—or from the evil of this—O Allah, do not bring him to us.' He will come to them and they will say: 'O Allah, disgrace him!' And he will say: 'May Allah remove you far away, for each of you has the like of this.'"

Then al-Bazzar said: It is not narrated except through this chain. [It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 3136, through 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa with the same chain, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter, and further astray in way﴾, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Whoever is blind in this﴾ means: in the life of this world, ﴿blind﴾ to the proofs (hujaj), signs (ayat) and clear evidences (bayyinat) of Allah. ﴿Then he will be blind in the Hereafter﴾, that is: he will be likewise. ﴿And further astray in way﴾, that is: more astray than he was in the world, seeking refuge with Allah from that.

It is said: it was revealed concerning the Jews, when they advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to settle in al-Sham (the land of the Prophets) and to leave off settling in al-Madinah.

This view is weak, because this verse is Meccan, and the settling in al-Madinah came after that.

It is also said that it was revealed at Tabuk, but its soundness is open to question.

Al-Bayhaqi said, from al-Hakim, from al-Asamm, from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Attaridi, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm: that the Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one day and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, if you are truthful that you are a Prophet, then go to al-Sham, for al-Sham is the land of the Gathering and the land of the Prophets." So he accepted what they said and set out on the expedition of Tabuk, intending nothing but al-Sham. When he reached Tabuk, Allah revealed to him verses from the Surah of Bani Isra'il after the surah had been completed: ﴿And indeed they almost incited you to drive you out of the land, but then they would not have remained after you, except for a little﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a transformation﴾. So Allah commanded him to return to al-Madinah, and said: "In it is your living and your dying, and from it you will be raised."

There is scrutiny regarding this chain. The more apparent view is that this report is not sound; for the Prophet ﷺ did not go out to Tabuk because of the statement of the Jews. Rather, he went out in compliance with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you﴾ [at-Tawbah: 123], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ [at-Tawbah: 29]. He went out to exact retaliation against those who killed the people of Mu'tah from among his companions, and Allah knows best. And if this were sound, it would be interpreted in light of the hadith narrated by al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Ufayr ibn Ma'dan, from Sulaym ibn Amir, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Qur'an was revealed in three places: Makkah, al-Madinah, and al-Sham." And explaining al-Sham as Tabuk is better than what al-Walid said, that it is Bayt al-Maqdis; and Allah knows best.

It is also said: it was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Quraysh, who intended to expel the Messenger from among them. So Allah threatened them with this verse, and that if they had expelled him, they would not have remained in Makkah after him except for a little. He killed their nobles and took captive their chieftains. Therefore He said: ﴿As is the practice regarding those We sent before you of Our messengers﴾, meaning: this is Our custom concerning those who disbelieved in Our messengers and harmed them: the messenger is brought out from among them, and the punishment comes upon them. And had he, upon him be peace, not been the messenger of mercy, there would have come upon them from punishments in this world that which no one could withstand. Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ [al-Anfal: 33].
