Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 78–79 (part 1 of 3):

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger ﷺ, commanding him to establish the obligatory prayers (al-salawat al-maktubat) at their appointed times: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾. It was said [[in T: "qabl" (before)]] that this refers to its setting. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd.

Hushaym related from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas: "Dulukuha" (its decline) means its zenith (zawaluha). This was also related by Nafi', from Ibn Umar. Malik related it in his tafsir (exegesis), from al-Zuhri, from Ibn Umar. Abu Barza al-Aslami also said it, and it is likewise a narration from Ibn Mas'ud and from Mujahid. Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, and Qatada also said this. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view, and among the evidence he cited is what he related from Ibn Humayd, from al-Hakam ibn Bashir, who said: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, [from a man] [[addition from F, A, and al-Tabari]], from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: I invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and whoever of his companions wished, and they ate at my house. Then they went out when the sun had passed its zenith. The Prophet ﷺ went out and said: "Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is the time when the sun has declined" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/93)]].

He then related it from Sahl ibn Bakkar, from Abu Awana, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Nubayh al-Anazi, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in similar wording. Accordingly, this verse includes the five times of prayer. From His saying ﴿from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, where "ghasaq al-layl" means its darkness, and it was also said that it means the setting of the sun, the Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers are derived. And His saying [[addition from T]]: ﴿and the Qur'an of dawn﴾ means the dawn prayer (Salat al-Fajr).

The Sunnah (the prophetic practice and teaching) has been established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through mass-transmission (tawatur), both from his actions and his sayings [[in T: "his sayings and his actions"]], with the details of these times. This is what the people of Islam practise today, having received it from predecessor to successor, generation after generation, as is established in its proper place. And to Allah belongs all praise.

﴿Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾. Al-A'mash related from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, and [from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him [[in T, F, A: "with them both"]]], from the Prophet ﷺ regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾, that he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

Al-Bukhari said: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama [and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab], from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The virtue of congregational prayer over the prayer of an individual is twenty-five degrees, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer." Abu Hurayra would say: Recite if you wish: ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4717)]].

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ. [And al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying: ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾] that he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah all related it, all three from Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad, from his father, with the same wording [[Musnad (2/474); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3135); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11293); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (670). It is in the collections of the Sunan scholars through the narration of al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

In a wording in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), through the route of Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day take turns among you, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the 'Asr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them—and He knows best about you—'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (555); Sahih Muslim no. (632)]].

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "The two guards [[in T, F: "al-harastan"]] gather at the dawn prayer: these ascend, and those remain."

Similarly said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Mujahid, Qatada, and others in explaining this verse.

As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir related here, from the narration of Layth ibn Sa'd, from Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which mentions the hadith of the Descent (al-nuzul), in which He, exalted is He, says: "Whoever asks forgiveness of Me, I will forgive him; whoever asks Me, I will give to him; whoever calls upon Me, I will respond to him, until dawn breaks." Therefore He says: ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ — Allah witnesses it, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/94)]]. Yet he (Ziyad) was alone in this addition, and there is a hadith for it in Sunan Abi Dawud [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3892), whose beginning is: "Whoever among you complains of something, or a brother of his complains to him, let him say..." and the addition is that of a munkar (rejected) narrator]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a supererogatory (nafilah) for you﴾ is a command to him to stand in prayer during the night (qiyam al-layl) after the obligatory prayer, as is recorded in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he was asked: "Which prayer is best after the obligatory prayer?" He said: "The prayer of the night" [[Sahih Muslim no. (1163)]].

Therefore Allah commanded His Messenger, after the obligatory prayers, to stand in prayer during the night. The tahajjud is what is done after sleep. This was said by Alqama, al-Aswad, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and others, and it is the well-known meaning in the Arabic language. Likewise, the hadiths are established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he would perform tahajjud after his sleep, from Ibn Abbas, Aisha, and many other companions, may Allah be pleased with them, as is expounded in its proper place. And to Allah belong praise and favour.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it is what is done after the 'Isha' prayer. But it may be understood as referring to what is done after sleep.

Scholars differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿as a supererogatory for you﴾. It was said: its meaning is that you are specifically singled out with the obligation of this alone, so they made the night prayer obligatory for him and not for the community (ummah). Al-Aufi related this from Ibn Abbas, and it is one of the two opinions of scholars, and one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

It was also said: the night prayer was made a supererogatory for him specifically, because his past and future sins have been forgiven, whereas for others of his community, it is the supererogatory prayers that expiate the sins upon them. This was said by Mujahid, and it is in the Musnad from Abu Umama al-Bahili, may Allah be pleased with him [[Musnad (5/256)]].

* *

His saying: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ means: do this which I have commanded you, so that We may place you, on the Day of Resurrection, in a station for which all of creation and their Creator, blessed and exalted is He, will envy you.

Ibn Jarir said: Most of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said: that is the station which he ﷺ will occupy on the Day of Resurrection for intercession (shafa'ah) for the people, so that their Lord may relieve them of the great distress they are in because of the severity of that day.

Mention of who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from [[in T: "ibn"]] Abi Ishaq, from Silat ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfa, who said: "People will be gathered in one plain. The caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all, barefoot, naked, as they were created, standing. No soul will speak except by His permission. He will be called: 'O Muhammad!' and he will say: 'Here I am at Your service, and happiness is in Your hands, and evil is not to You. The guided is the one whom You guide. Your servant is before You, by You and to You. There is no refuge or escape from You except to You. You are blessed and exalted. Glory be to You, Lord of the House.' This is the praiseworthy station which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/97)]].

Then he related it from Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'ba, from Abu Ishaq, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/97). The narration as it is in al-Tabari: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far (Ghundar) narrated to us; perhaps this is a slip of sight.]]. Likewise, Abd al-Razzaq related it from Ma'mar and al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/98)]].

Ibn Abbas said: "This praiseworthy station is the station of intercession." Ibn Abi Najih said the same, from Mujahid. Al-Hasan al-Basri also said it.

Qatada said: "It is the first one from whom the earth will split open, and the first intercessor. The people of knowledge used to regard it as the praiseworthy station about which Allah said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾."

I say: For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there are honours (tashrifat) on the Day of Resurrection in which no one shares with him, and honours in which no one equals him. He is the first from whom the earth will split open, and he will be raised riding to the place of gathering (al-mahshar). He will have the banner (al-liwa') under which Adam and those after him will be. He will have the Pool (al-hawd), at which there will be no more numerous visitors in the place of standing. He will have the Great Intercession (al-shafa'ah al-'uzma) with Allah, so that He may come to judge between the creation. This will be after people have asked Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, and each will say: "I am not fit for it," until they come to Muhammad ﷺ, and he will say: "I am fit for it, I am fit for it," as we will mention in detail in its proper place, if Allah wills. Among this is that he will intercede for groups who have been commanded to the Fire, and they will be turned back from it. He is the first of the prophets to have judgment passed between his community, and the first of them to cross the Sirat (bridge) with his community. He is the first intercessor into Paradise, as is established in Sahih Muslim. In the hadith of the Trumpet: "Indeed, all the believers will not enter Paradise except by his intercession, and he is the first to enter it, and his community is before all the nations." He will intercede for the raising of the ranks of groups whose deeds do not reach them. He is the owner of the Wasilah, which is the highest rank in Paradise, suitable for none but him. When Allah, exalted is He, permits intercession for the disobedient (al-'usat), the angels, the prophets, and the believers will intercede, and he will intercede for multitudes whose number none knows except Allah, and none intercedes like him or equals him in that. I have explained this fully at the end of the book "al-Sirah" in the chapter on the distinctive features (al-khasa'is), and to Allah belong praise and favour.

Now let us mention the hadiths related concerning the praiseworthy station, and in Allah is the help sought:

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Adam ibn Ali, I heard Ibn Umar [saying] [[addition from T, F, A, and al-Bukhari]]: "People will come on the Day of Resurrection kneeling (judha), each community following its prophet, saying: 'O so-and-so, intercede! O so-and-so, intercede!' until the intercession reaches the Prophet ﷺ. That is the day on which Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4718)]].

Hamza ibn Abd Allah related it from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 17, verses 78–79 (part 2 of 3):

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us [In manuscript T: "He said: narrated to us."], saying: al-Layth narrated to me [In manuscript T: "He said: narrated to me."], from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, that he said: I heard Hamzah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar saying: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sun will draw so near that the sweat will reach the middle of the ear. While they are in that state, they will seek help from Adam, and he will say: 'I am not the one for that.' Then they will go to Musa (Moses), and he will say the same. Then they will go to Muhammad (ﷺ), and he will intercede between the creation [In manuscript T: "the creatures"]. He will walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door of Paradise. On that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station [maqam mahmud, the 'praised station' of intercession]," [Everyone among the people of Paradise will praise him].

Similarly, al-Bukhari related it in "al-Zakah" (the book of obligatory charity), from Yahya ibn Bukayr and 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, both from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with the same chain. He added: "On that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station, and all the people of the gathering will praise him."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, grant Muhammad the wasilah (a station near the Throne in Paradise) and the fadilah (a superior rank), and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him,' my intercession will be lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Bukhari alone reported it, without Muslim.

The Hadith of Ubayy:
Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will be the imam (leader) of the prophets, their orator, and the one who holds their intercession, without boasting."

al-Tirmidhi also reported it through the narration of Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr al-'Aqadi, and he said: "Hasan sahih" (good and sound). Ibn Majah reported it through 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil with the same wording. We have already mentioned, in the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning the recitation of the Qur'an in seven ahruf (modes or dialects), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at its end: "I said: 'O Allah, forgive my ummah (community), O Allah, forgive my ummah.' And I postponed the third request to a day when the creation will long for me, until Ibrahim (Abraham) (peace be upon him)."

The Hadith of Anas ibn Malik:
Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be inspired to say: 'If only we could ask our Lord to intercede for us, so that He would relieve us from this place of ours.' So they will come to Adam and say: 'O Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His own hand, commanded His angels to prostrate to you, and taught you the names of all things. So intercede for us with your Lord, so that He may relieve us from this place of ours.' Adam will say to them: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention the sin he committed, and he will feel shy before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, because of it, and he will say: 'But go to Nuh (Noah), for he was the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth.' So they will come to Nuh, and he will say: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention his error in asking his Lord about what he had no knowledge of, and he will feel shy before his Lord because of it, and he will say: 'But go to Ibrahim, the Khalil al-Rahman (Friend of the Most Merciful).' So they will come to him, and he will say: 'I am not in that position. But go to Musa, a servant whom Allah spoke to and to whom He gave the Torah.' So they will come to Musa, and he will say: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention to them the soul he killed without a soul [In manuscript F: "without right"], and he will feel shy before his Lord because of it. But go to 'Isa (Jesus), the servant of Allah and His messenger, His word and His spirit.' So they will come to 'Isa, and he will say: 'I am not in that position. But go to Muhammad, a servant whose past and future sins have been forgiven, and they will come to me.'" Al-Hasan said: "This word [In manuscript T: "the fear"] is: 'So I will stand and walk between two rows of believers.'" Anas said: "Until I ask permission to enter upon my Lord. When I see my Lord, I will fall down, or he said: I will drop down, prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me in that state for as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak and you will be heard; intercede and your intercession will be accepted; ask and you will be given.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise." Then I will return to Him a second time, and when I see my Lord, I will fall down, or he said: I will drop down, prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me in that state for as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return for the third time; when I see my Lord, I will fall down, or he said: I will drop down, prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me in that state for as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return for the fourth time and say: 'O Lord, there remain only those whom the Qur'an has detained.'" He related to us, Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah' (there is no god but Allah) and has in his heart good equal to the weight of a barley grain will be brought out of the Fire. Then whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah' and has in his heart good equal to the weight of a wheat grain will be brought out of the Fire. Then whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah' and has in his heart good equal to the weight of an atom will be brought out of the Fire."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) reported it in the Sahihayn (the two Sahih books) through the narration of Sa'id, with the same wording. Similarly, Imam Ahmad reported it from 'Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, in full.

Imam Ahmad also said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Harb ibn Maymun Abu al-Khattab al-Ansari narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Anas, who said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me, saying: "I was standing waiting for my ummah to cross the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), when 'Isa (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'These prophets have come to you, O Muhammad, asking [or he said: gathering to you], and they are calling upon Allah to separate all the nations to wherever Allah wills, because of the distress they are in. The creation is bridled with sweat. As for the believer, it is like a cold in his head; as for the disbelievers, death overtakes them.' He said: 'Wait until I return to you.' So the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) went and stood beneath the Throne, and he encountered what no angel brought near or prophet sent had encountered. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inspired Jibril (Gabriel): 'Go to Muhammad and say to him: Raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I interceded for my ummah, that one out of every ninety-nine people be brought out [of Hell]. I kept returning to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and every time I stood before Him I was granted intercession, until Allah gave me from that [the permission] that He said: 'O Muhammad, admit from your ummah [In manuscripts T, A and al-Musnad: "from among"] the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whoever bore witness that there is no god but Allah, sincerely, for a single day, and died upon that.'" [Al-Musnad (3/178), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/374): "its narrators are the narrators of the sahih."]

The Hadith of Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him):
Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: al-Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Abu Isra'il informed us, from al-Harith ibn Hasirah, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that he entered upon Mu'awiyah, and there was a man speaking. Buraydah said: "O Mu'awiyah, will you permit me to speak?" He said: "Yes" (and he thought that he was speaking in a similar manner to what the other had said). Buraydah said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'I truly hope to be granted intercession on the Day of Resurrection in number equal to whatever trees and clods of earth there are on the earth.'" He said: "Do you hope for it, O Mu'awiyah, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, does not hope for it?!" [Al-Musnad (5/347); Abu Isra'il al-Mala'i is weak.]

The Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud:
Imam Ahmad said: 'Arim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hakam al-Bunani narrated to us, from 'Uthman, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The two sons of Mulaykah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Our mother [In manuscripts T, F, A and al-Musnad: "was"] used to honour her husband and be kind to her children" (he said: and he mentioned hospitality to guests), "but she had buried [alive daughters] in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance)." He said: "Your mother is in the Fire." They said: "They turned away, and evil could be seen in their faces. He ordered that they be brought back, and they returned, with happiness visible in their faces, hoping that something had happened." He said: "My mother is with your mother." A hypocrite said: "Does this avail her anything at all? We walk over her heels!" A man from the Ansar, and I have never seen a man who asked more questions than he did, said: "O Messenger of Allah, has your Lord promised you regarding her or regarding them?" He said: He thought that it was something he had heard, so he said: "What Allah wills (ma sha' Allah), my Lord, and He did not make me hopeful about it. Indeed, I will stand in the praiseworthy station on the Day of Resurrection." The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is that praiseworthy station?" He said: "That is when you are brought together barefoot, naked, uncircumcised [ghurl]. The first to be clothed will be Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He will say: 'Clothe my friend.' So two white garments will be brought, and he will put them on. Then he will be seated facing the Throne. Then I will be brought my garment, and I will put it on, and I will stand at his right side in a station that no one else will stand in, and the first and last will envy me for it. A river from al-Kawthar will flow to the Basin (al-Hawd)." The hypocrites said: "Water has never flowed except over pebbles or gravel." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its earth is musk, and its gravel is pearls." [The hypocrite said: "I have never heard the like of this today. Water has rarely flowed over pebbles or gravel without a plant growing from it." The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have plants?" He said: "Yes, stems of gold."] The hypocrite said: "I have never heard the like of this today. For a stem rarely grows without leaves and fruit!" The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have fruit?" He said: "Yes, fruits of various jewels; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Whoever drinks from it a single sip will never be thirsty after it, and whoever is deprived of it will never be quenched after it." [Al-Musnad (1/398).]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Yahya ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Za'ra', from 'Abd Allah, who said: "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will give permission for intercession. Ruh al-Qudus (the Holy Spirit), Jibril, will stand, then Ibrahim, the Khalil of Allah, will stand, then 'Isa or Musa will stand" (Abu al-Za'ra' said: "I do not know which of the two"), "then your Prophet (ﷺ) will stand fourth, and he will intercede, and no one after him will intercede more than he has interceded. This is the praiseworthy station of which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.﴾" [Al-Nasa'i reported it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11296) through the chain of Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, with similar wording.]

The Hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him):

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 78–79 (part 3 of 3):

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, al-Zubaidi narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah [ibn Ka'b] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]] ibn Malik, from Ka'b ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my Ummah will be upon a hill, and my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe me in a green garment [[In T: "red".]], then I will be given permission and I will speak what Allah wills me to speak. That is the Praiseworthy Station (al-Maqam al-Mahmud)." [[al-Musnad (3/456).]]

Hadith of Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him:
Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Darda, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I will be the first to be given permission to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to be given permission to raise my head. I will look at what is before me, and I will recognize my Ummah among the nations. And behind me, the same; and to my right, the same; and to my left, the same." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize your Ummah among the nations, among all the nations from Noah until your Ummah?" He said: "They will be radiant with white marks from the traces of wudu', and no one else will be like that. I will recognize them by their books being given to them in their right hands, and I will recognize them by their offspring running before them." [[al-Musnad (5/199).]]

Hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him:
Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to us, Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a foreleg was raised to him, and it was what he liked, so he took a bite from it. Then he said: "I am the master of the people on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why? Allah will gather the first and the last in one plain. The caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all. The sun will draw near, and the people will suffer such distress and anguish that they cannot bear or endure it. Some people will say to others: 'Do you not see what you are in? Do you not see what has reached you? Will you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord, Mighty and Majestic?' Some people will say to others: [Do you not see what you are in? Do you not see what has reached you? Will you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord, Mighty and Majestic? Some people will say to others] [[Addition from al-Musnad.]]: 'Your father is Adam!'

They will come to Adam and say: 'O Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His own hand, breathed into you of His spirit, commanded the angels and they prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Adam will say: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it. He forbade me from the tree and I disobeyed Him. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me. Go to Noah.'

They will come to Noah and say: 'O Noah, you are the first of the Messengers to the people of the earth, and Allah named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Noah will say: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it. I had a supplication against my people. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me. Go to Abraham.'

They will come to Abraham and say: 'O Abraham, you are the Prophet of Allah and His friend (khalil) from among the people of the earth, [intercede for us with your Lord] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]] Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' He will say: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it,' and he mentioned his lies. 'Myself, myself, myself [go to someone other than me] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. Go to Moses.'

They will come to Moses and say: 'O Moses, you are the Messenger of Allah, whom Allah chose above the people with His messages and His speech. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Moses will say to them: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it, and I killed a soul which I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Jesus.'

They will come to Jesus and say: 'O Jesus, you are the Messenger of Allah and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him' [he said: 'Thus it is'] 'and you spoke to the people in the cradle. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Jesus will say to them: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it,' and he did not mention a sin. 'Go to someone other than me. Go to Muhammad.'

They will come to me and say: 'O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' So I will stand and come beneath the Throne, and fall down in prostration to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Then Allah will open to me and inspire me with praises of Him and fine glorification of Him, which He had not opened to anyone before me. It will be said: 'O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' I will say: 'O Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah! O Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah! O Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah!' It will be said: 'O Muhammad, admit from your Ummah those who have no reckoning through the right-hand door of the gates of Paradise, and they will share with the people the other doors.'" Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between two leaves of the gates of Paradise is like the distance between Makkah and Hajar, or like the distance between Makkah and Busra." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs. [[al-Musnad (2/435); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4712); Sahih Muslim no. (894).]]

Muslim said: al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to us, Hiql ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, Abu Ammar narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn Farrukh narrated to me, Abu Hurayrah narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, the first whose grave will be split open, the first intercessor, and the first whose intercession is accepted." [[Sahih Muslim no. (2278).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Yazid al-Za'afiri, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding the verse ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾, and he was asked about it, and he said: "It is the intercession." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/98).]]

Imam Ahmad narrated it from Waki' and from Muhammad [[In H: "from Waki' from Muhammad ibn Ubayd", the text from T is adopted.]] ibn Ubayd, from Dawud, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾, he said: "It is the station in which I will intercede for my Ummah." [[al-Musnad (2/441, 444).]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will stretch the earth like a leather hide, until no person among the people has anything but the place of his foot. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'I will be the first to be called, and Jibril will be at the right of the Most Merciful, whom he had never seen before. I will say: My Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say: He has spoken the truth. Then I will intercede. I will say: O Lord, Your servants have worshipped You at the far ends of the earth.'" He said: "That is the Praiseworthy Station." [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/328).]] This is a mursal hadith.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 78–79 (part 1 of 3):

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger ﷺ, commanding him to establish the obligatory prayers (al-salawat al-maktubat) at their appointed times: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾. It was said [[in T: "qabl" (before)]] that this refers to its setting. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd.

Hushaym related from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas: "Dulukuha" (its decline) means its zenith (zawaluha). This was also related by Nafi', from Ibn Umar. Malik related it in his tafsir (exegesis), from al-Zuhri, from Ibn Umar. Abu Barza al-Aslami also said it, and it is likewise a narration from Ibn Mas'ud and from Mujahid. Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, and Qatada also said this. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose this view, and among the evidence he cited is what he related from Ibn Humayd, from al-Hakam ibn Bashir, who said: Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, [from a man] [[addition from F, A, and al-Tabari]], from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: I invited the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and whoever of his companions wished, and they ate at my house. Then they went out when the sun had passed its zenith. The Prophet ﷺ went out and said: "Go out, O Abu Bakr, for this is the time when the sun has declined" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/93)]].

He then related it from Sahl ibn Bakkar, from Abu Awana, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Nubayh al-Anazi, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in similar wording. Accordingly, this verse includes the five times of prayer. From His saying ﴿from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, where "ghasaq al-layl" means its darkness, and it was also said that it means the setting of the sun, the Zuhr, 'Asr, Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers are derived. And His saying [[addition from T]]: ﴿and the Qur'an of dawn﴾ means the dawn prayer (Salat al-Fajr).

The Sunnah (the prophetic practice and teaching) has been established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ through mass-transmission (tawatur), both from his actions and his sayings [[in T: "his sayings and his actions"]], with the details of these times. This is what the people of Islam practise today, having received it from predecessor to successor, generation after generation, as is established in its proper place. And to Allah belongs all praise.

﴿Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾. Al-A'mash related from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, and [from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him [[in T, F, A: "with them both"]]], from the Prophet ﷺ regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾, that he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

Al-Bukhari said: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama [and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab], from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The virtue of congregational prayer over the prayer of an individual is twenty-five degrees, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer." Abu Hurayra would say: Recite if you wish: ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4717)]].

Imam Ahmad said: Asbat narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ. [And al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying: ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾] that he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah all related it, all three from Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad, from his father, with the same wording [[Musnad (2/474); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3135); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11293); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (670). It is in the collections of the Sunan scholars through the narration of al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

In a wording in the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), through the route of Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day take turns among you, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the 'Asr prayer. Then those who spent the night among you ascend, and He asks them—and He knows best about you—'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying'" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (555); Sahih Muslim no. (632)]].

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "The two guards [[in T, F: "al-harastan"]] gather at the dawn prayer: these ascend, and those remain."

Similarly said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Mujahid, Qatada, and others in explaining this verse.

As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir related here, from the narration of Layth ibn Sa'd, from Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which mentions the hadith of the Descent (al-nuzul), in which He, exalted is He, says: "Whoever asks forgiveness of Me, I will forgive him; whoever asks Me, I will give to him; whoever calls upon Me, I will respond to him, until dawn breaks." Therefore He says: ﴿And the Qur'an of dawn; indeed, the Qur'an of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ — Allah witnesses it, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/94)]]. Yet he (Ziyad) was alone in this addition, and there is a hadith for it in Sunan Abi Dawud [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3892), whose beginning is: "Whoever among you complains of something, or a brother of his complains to him, let him say..." and the addition is that of a munkar (rejected) narrator]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a supererogatory (nafilah) for you﴾ is a command to him to stand in prayer during the night (qiyam al-layl) after the obligatory prayer, as is recorded in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he was asked: "Which prayer is best after the obligatory prayer?" He said: "The prayer of the night" [[Sahih Muslim no. (1163)]].

Therefore Allah commanded His Messenger, after the obligatory prayers, to stand in prayer during the night. The tahajjud is what is done after sleep. This was said by Alqama, al-Aswad, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and others, and it is the well-known meaning in the Arabic language. Likewise, the hadiths are established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he would perform tahajjud after his sleep, from Ibn Abbas, Aisha, and many other companions, may Allah be pleased with them, as is expounded in its proper place. And to Allah belong praise and favour.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it is what is done after the 'Isha' prayer. But it may be understood as referring to what is done after sleep.

Scholars differed regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿as a supererogatory for you﴾. It was said: its meaning is that you are specifically singled out with the obligation of this alone, so they made the night prayer obligatory for him and not for the community (ummah). Al-Aufi related this from Ibn Abbas, and it is one of the two opinions of scholars, and one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

It was also said: the night prayer was made a supererogatory for him specifically, because his past and future sins have been forgiven, whereas for others of his community, it is the supererogatory prayers that expiate the sins upon them. This was said by Mujahid, and it is in the Musnad from Abu Umama al-Bahili, may Allah be pleased with him [[Musnad (5/256)]].

* *

His saying: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ means: do this which I have commanded you, so that We may place you, on the Day of Resurrection, in a station for which all of creation and their Creator, blessed and exalted is He, will envy you.

Ibn Jarir said: Most of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said: that is the station which he ﷺ will occupy on the Day of Resurrection for intercession (shafa'ah) for the people, so that their Lord may relieve them of the great distress they are in because of the severity of that day.

Mention of who said that: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from [[in T: "ibn"]] Abi Ishaq, from Silat ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfa, who said: "People will be gathered in one plain. The caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all, barefoot, naked, as they were created, standing. No soul will speak except by His permission. He will be called: 'O Muhammad!' and he will say: 'Here I am at Your service, and happiness is in Your hands, and evil is not to You. The guided is the one whom You guide. Your servant is before You, by You and to You. There is no refuge or escape from You except to You. You are blessed and exalted. Glory be to You, Lord of the House.' This is the praiseworthy station which Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/97)]].

Then he related it from Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'ba, from Abu Ishaq, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/97). The narration as it is in al-Tabari: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far (Ghundar) narrated to us; perhaps this is a slip of sight.]]. Likewise, Abd al-Razzaq related it from Ma'mar and al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, with the same chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/98)]].

Ibn Abbas said: "This praiseworthy station is the station of intercession." Ibn Abi Najih said the same, from Mujahid. Al-Hasan al-Basri also said it.

Qatada said: "It is the first one from whom the earth will split open, and the first intercessor. The people of knowledge used to regard it as the praiseworthy station about which Allah said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾."

I say: For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there are honours (tashrifat) on the Day of Resurrection in which no one shares with him, and honours in which no one equals him. He is the first from whom the earth will split open, and he will be raised riding to the place of gathering (al-mahshar). He will have the banner (al-liwa') under which Adam and those after him will be. He will have the Pool (al-hawd), at which there will be no more numerous visitors in the place of standing. He will have the Great Intercession (al-shafa'ah al-'uzma) with Allah, so that He may come to judge between the creation. This will be after people have asked Adam, then Noah, then Abraham, then Moses, then Jesus, and each will say: "I am not fit for it," until they come to Muhammad ﷺ, and he will say: "I am fit for it, I am fit for it," as we will mention in detail in its proper place, if Allah wills. Among this is that he will intercede for groups who have been commanded to the Fire, and they will be turned back from it. He is the first of the prophets to have judgment passed between his community, and the first of them to cross the Sirat (bridge) with his community. He is the first intercessor into Paradise, as is established in Sahih Muslim. In the hadith of the Trumpet: "Indeed, all the believers will not enter Paradise except by his intercession, and he is the first to enter it, and his community is before all the nations." He will intercede for the raising of the ranks of groups whose deeds do not reach them. He is the owner of the Wasilah, which is the highest rank in Paradise, suitable for none but him. When Allah, exalted is He, permits intercession for the disobedient (al-'usat), the angels, the prophets, and the believers will intercede, and he will intercede for multitudes whose number none knows except Allah, and none intercedes like him or equals him in that. I have explained this fully at the end of the book "al-Sirah" in the chapter on the distinctive features (al-khasa'is), and to Allah belong praise and favour.

Now let us mention the hadiths related concerning the praiseworthy station, and in Allah is the help sought:

Al-Bukhari said: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Adam ibn Ali, I heard Ibn Umar [saying] [[addition from T, F, A, and al-Bukhari]]: "People will come on the Day of Resurrection kneeling (judha), each community following its prophet, saying: 'O so-and-so, intercede! O so-and-so, intercede!' until the intercession reaches the Prophet ﷺ. That is the day on which Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4718)]].

Hamza ibn Abd Allah related it from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 17, verses 78–79 (part 2 of 3):

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us [In manuscript T: "He said: narrated to us."], saying: al-Layth narrated to me [In manuscript T: "He said: narrated to me."], from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, that he said: I heard Hamzah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar saying: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sun will draw so near that the sweat will reach the middle of the ear. While they are in that state, they will seek help from Adam, and he will say: 'I am not the one for that.' Then they will go to Musa (Moses), and he will say the same. Then they will go to Muhammad (ﷺ), and he will intercede between the creation [In manuscript T: "the creatures"]. He will walk until he takes hold of the ring of the door of Paradise. On that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station [maqam mahmud, the 'praised station' of intercession]," [Everyone among the people of Paradise will praise him].

Similarly, al-Bukhari related it in "al-Zakah" (the book of obligatory charity), from Yahya ibn Bukayr and 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, both from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with the same chain. He added: "On that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station, and all the people of the gathering will praise him."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, grant Muhammad the wasilah (a station near the Throne in Paradise) and the fadilah (a superior rank), and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him,' my intercession will be lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Bukhari alone reported it, without Muslim.

The Hadith of Ubayy:
Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will be the imam (leader) of the prophets, their orator, and the one who holds their intercession, without boasting."

al-Tirmidhi also reported it through the narration of Abu 'Amir 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr al-'Aqadi, and he said: "Hasan sahih" (good and sound). Ibn Majah reported it through 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil with the same wording. We have already mentioned, in the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning the recitation of the Qur'an in seven ahruf (modes or dialects), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at its end: "I said: 'O Allah, forgive my ummah (community), O Allah, forgive my ummah.' And I postponed the third request to a day when the creation will long for me, until Ibrahim (Abraham) (peace be upon him)."

The Hadith of Anas ibn Malik:
Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The believers will gather on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be inspired to say: 'If only we could ask our Lord to intercede for us, so that He would relieve us from this place of ours.' So they will come to Adam and say: 'O Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His own hand, commanded His angels to prostrate to you, and taught you the names of all things. So intercede for us with your Lord, so that He may relieve us from this place of ours.' Adam will say to them: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention the sin he committed, and he will feel shy before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, because of it, and he will say: 'But go to Nuh (Noah), for he was the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth.' So they will come to Nuh, and he will say: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention his error in asking his Lord about what he had no knowledge of, and he will feel shy before his Lord because of it, and he will say: 'But go to Ibrahim, the Khalil al-Rahman (Friend of the Most Merciful).' So they will come to him, and he will say: 'I am not in that position. But go to Musa, a servant whom Allah spoke to and to whom He gave the Torah.' So they will come to Musa, and he will say: 'I am not in that position,' and he will mention to them the soul he killed without a soul [In manuscript F: "without right"], and he will feel shy before his Lord because of it. But go to 'Isa (Jesus), the servant of Allah and His messenger, His word and His spirit.' So they will come to 'Isa, and he will say: 'I am not in that position. But go to Muhammad, a servant whose past and future sins have been forgiven, and they will come to me.'" Al-Hasan said: "This word [In manuscript T: "the fear"] is: 'So I will stand and walk between two rows of believers.'" Anas said: "Until I ask permission to enter upon my Lord. When I see my Lord, I will fall down, or he said: I will drop down, prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me in that state for as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak and you will be heard; intercede and your intercession will be accepted; ask and you will be given.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise." Then I will return to Him a second time, and when I see my Lord, I will fall down, or he said: I will drop down, prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me in that state for as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return for the third time; when I see my Lord, I will fall down, or he said: I will drop down, prostrate to my Lord, and He will leave me in that state for as long as Allah wills. Then it will be said: 'Raise your head, O Muhammad; speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I will raise my head and praise Him with a praise that He will teach me. Then I will intercede, and He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return for the fourth time and say: 'O Lord, there remain only those whom the Qur'an has detained.'" He related to us, Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah' (there is no god but Allah) and has in his heart good equal to the weight of a barley grain will be brought out of the Fire. Then whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah' and has in his heart good equal to the weight of a wheat grain will be brought out of the Fire. Then whoever says 'La ilaha illa Allah' and has in his heart good equal to the weight of an atom will be brought out of the Fire."

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) reported it in the Sahihayn (the two Sahih books) through the narration of Sa'id, with the same wording. Similarly, Imam Ahmad reported it from 'Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas, in full.

Imam Ahmad also said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Harb ibn Maymun Abu al-Khattab al-Ansari narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Anas, who said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me, saying: "I was standing waiting for my ummah to cross the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), when 'Isa (peace be upon him) came to me and said: 'These prophets have come to you, O Muhammad, asking [or he said: gathering to you], and they are calling upon Allah to separate all the nations to wherever Allah wills, because of the distress they are in. The creation is bridled with sweat. As for the believer, it is like a cold in his head; as for the disbelievers, death overtakes them.' He said: 'Wait until I return to you.' So the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) went and stood beneath the Throne, and he encountered what no angel brought near or prophet sent had encountered. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inspired Jibril (Gabriel): 'Go to Muhammad and say to him: Raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' So I interceded for my ummah, that one out of every ninety-nine people be brought out [of Hell]. I kept returning to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and every time I stood before Him I was granted intercession, until Allah gave me from that [the permission] that He said: 'O Muhammad, admit from your ummah [In manuscripts T, A and al-Musnad: "from among"] the creation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whoever bore witness that there is no god but Allah, sincerely, for a single day, and died upon that.'" [Al-Musnad (3/178), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/374): "its narrators are the narrators of the sahih."]

The Hadith of Buraydah (may Allah be pleased with him):
Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: al-Aswad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Abu Isra'il informed us, from al-Harith ibn Hasirah, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father, that he entered upon Mu'awiyah, and there was a man speaking. Buraydah said: "O Mu'awiyah, will you permit me to speak?" He said: "Yes" (and he thought that he was speaking in a similar manner to what the other had said). Buraydah said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: 'I truly hope to be granted intercession on the Day of Resurrection in number equal to whatever trees and clods of earth there are on the earth.'" He said: "Do you hope for it, O Mu'awiyah, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, does not hope for it?!" [Al-Musnad (5/347); Abu Isra'il al-Mala'i is weak.]

The Hadith of Ibn Mas'ud:
Imam Ahmad said: 'Arim ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hakam al-Bunani narrated to us, from 'Uthman, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The two sons of Mulaykah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Our mother [In manuscripts T, F, A and al-Musnad: "was"] used to honour her husband and be kind to her children" (he said: and he mentioned hospitality to guests), "but she had buried [alive daughters] in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance)." He said: "Your mother is in the Fire." They said: "They turned away, and evil could be seen in their faces. He ordered that they be brought back, and they returned, with happiness visible in their faces, hoping that something had happened." He said: "My mother is with your mother." A hypocrite said: "Does this avail her anything at all? We walk over her heels!" A man from the Ansar, and I have never seen a man who asked more questions than he did, said: "O Messenger of Allah, has your Lord promised you regarding her or regarding them?" He said: He thought that it was something he had heard, so he said: "What Allah wills (ma sha' Allah), my Lord, and He did not make me hopeful about it. Indeed, I will stand in the praiseworthy station on the Day of Resurrection." The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is that praiseworthy station?" He said: "That is when you are brought together barefoot, naked, uncircumcised [ghurl]. The first to be clothed will be Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He will say: 'Clothe my friend.' So two white garments will be brought, and he will put them on. Then he will be seated facing the Throne. Then I will be brought my garment, and I will put it on, and I will stand at his right side in a station that no one else will stand in, and the first and last will envy me for it. A river from al-Kawthar will flow to the Basin (al-Hawd)." The hypocrites said: "Water has never flowed except over pebbles or gravel." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its earth is musk, and its gravel is pearls." [The hypocrite said: "I have never heard the like of this today. Water has rarely flowed over pebbles or gravel without a plant growing from it." The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have plants?" He said: "Yes, stems of gold."] The hypocrite said: "I have never heard the like of this today. For a stem rarely grows without leaves and fruit!" The Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does it have fruit?" He said: "Yes, fruits of various jewels; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. Whoever drinks from it a single sip will never be thirsty after it, and whoever is deprived of it will never be quenched after it." [Al-Musnad (1/398).]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Yahya ibn Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to us, from his father, from Abu al-Za'ra', from 'Abd Allah, who said: "Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will give permission for intercession. Ruh al-Qudus (the Holy Spirit), Jibril, will stand, then Ibrahim, the Khalil of Allah, will stand, then 'Isa or Musa will stand" (Abu al-Za'ra' said: "I do not know which of the two"), "then your Prophet (ﷺ) will stand fourth, and he will intercede, and no one after him will intercede more than he has interceded. This is the praiseworthy station of which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station.﴾" [Al-Nasa'i reported it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11296) through the chain of Bundar, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, with similar wording.]

The Hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him):

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 78–79 (part 3 of 3):

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us, al-Zubaidi narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah [ibn Ka'b] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]] ibn Malik, from Ka'b ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my Ummah will be upon a hill, and my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe me in a green garment [[In T: "red".]], then I will be given permission and I will speak what Allah wills me to speak. That is the Praiseworthy Station (al-Maqam al-Mahmud)." [[al-Musnad (3/456).]]

Hadith of Abu al-Darda, may Allah be pleased with him:
Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu al-Darda, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I will be the first to be given permission to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to be given permission to raise my head. I will look at what is before me, and I will recognize my Ummah among the nations. And behind me, the same; and to my right, the same; and to my left, the same." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize your Ummah among the nations, among all the nations from Noah until your Ummah?" He said: "They will be radiant with white marks from the traces of wudu', and no one else will be like that. I will recognize them by their books being given to them in their right hands, and I will recognize them by their offspring running before them." [[al-Musnad (5/199).]]

Hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him:
Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Abu Hayyan narrated to us, Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Meat was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and a foreleg was raised to him, and it was what he liked, so he took a bite from it. Then he said: "I am the master of the people on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why? Allah will gather the first and the last in one plain. The caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all. The sun will draw near, and the people will suffer such distress and anguish that they cannot bear or endure it. Some people will say to others: 'Do you not see what you are in? Do you not see what has reached you? Will you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord, Mighty and Majestic?' Some people will say to others: [Do you not see what you are in? Do you not see what has reached you? Will you not look for someone to intercede for you with your Lord, Mighty and Majestic? Some people will say to others] [[Addition from al-Musnad.]]: 'Your father is Adam!'

They will come to Adam and say: 'O Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His own hand, breathed into you of His spirit, commanded the angels and they prostrated to you. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Adam will say: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it. He forbade me from the tree and I disobeyed Him. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me. Go to Noah.'

They will come to Noah and say: 'O Noah, you are the first of the Messengers to the people of the earth, and Allah named you a grateful servant. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Noah will say: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it. I had a supplication against my people. Myself, myself, myself! Go to someone other than me. Go to Abraham.'

They will come to Abraham and say: 'O Abraham, you are the Prophet of Allah and His friend (khalil) from among the people of the earth, [intercede for us with your Lord] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]] Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' He will say: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it,' and he mentioned his lies. 'Myself, myself, myself [go to someone other than me] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]]. Go to Moses.'

They will come to Moses and say: 'O Moses, you are the Messenger of Allah, whom Allah chose above the people with His messages and His speech. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Moses will say to them: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it, and I killed a soul which I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone other than me. Go to Jesus.'

They will come to Jesus and say: 'O Jesus, you are the Messenger of Allah and His word which He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him' [he said: 'Thus it is'] 'and you spoke to the people in the cradle. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' Jesus will say to them: 'My Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after it,' and he did not mention a sin. 'Go to someone other than me. Go to Muhammad.'

They will come to me and say: 'O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. Allah has forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after. Intercede for us with your Lord. Do you not see what we are in? Do you not see what has reached us?' So I will stand and come beneath the Throne, and fall down in prostration to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic. Then Allah will open to me and inspire me with praises of Him and fine glorification of Him, which He had not opened to anyone before me. It will be said: 'O Muhammad, raise your head, ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' I will say: 'O Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah! O Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah! O Lord, my Ummah, my Ummah!' It will be said: 'O Muhammad, admit from your Ummah those who have no reckoning through the right-hand door of the gates of Paradise, and they will share with the people the other doors.'" Then he said: "By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the distance between two leaves of the gates of Paradise is like the distance between Makkah and Hajar, or like the distance between Makkah and Busra." Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs. [[al-Musnad (2/435); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4712); Sahih Muslim no. (894).]]

Muslim said: al-Hakam ibn Musa narrated to us, Hiql ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, Abu Ammar narrated to me, Abd Allah ibn Farrukh narrated to me, Abu Hurayrah narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, the first whose grave will be split open, the first intercessor, and the first whose intercession is accepted." [[Sahih Muslim no. (2278).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Yazid al-Za'afiri, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding the verse ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾, and he was asked about it, and he said: "It is the intercession." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/98).]]

Imam Ahmad narrated it from Waki' and from Muhammad [[In H: "from Waki' from Muhammad ibn Ubayd", the text from T is adopted.]] ibn Ubayd, from Dawud, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾, he said: "It is the station in which I will intercede for my Ummah." [[al-Musnad (2/441, 444).]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will stretch the earth like a leather hide, until no person among the people has anything but the place of his foot. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'I will be the first to be called, and Jibril will be at the right of the Most Merciful, whom he had never seen before. I will say: My Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say: He has spoken the truth. Then I will intercede. I will say: O Lord, Your servants have worshipped You at the far ends of the earth.'" He said: "That is the Praiseworthy Station." [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/328).]] This is a mursal hadith.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 80–81:

Imam Ahmad said: Jarir narrated to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, then he was commanded to emigrate (hijrah), and Allah revealed: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."﴾ [1]

Al-Hasan al-Basri said in explaining this verse: When the disbelievers of Makkah plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to kill him, or to expel him, or to imprison him, and Allah intended to fight the people of Makkah, He commanded him to leave for Madinah. It is this that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, referred to when He said: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit."﴾

Qatadah said: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance"﴾ means Madinah, ﴿"and cause me to exit a sound exit"﴾ means Makkah.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise, and this view is the most well-known of the opinions.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Enter a sound entrance﴾ means death, and ﴿exit a sound exit﴾ means life after death. Other opinions have also been reported, but the first is more correct, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said in explaining it: His Lord promised him that He would surely strip Persia of its kingdom and its might and give them to him, and the kingdom and might of the Romans, and He would surely give them to him.

Qatadah said concerning it: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) knew that he had no capacity for this matter except with an authority, so he asked for a supporting authority for the Book of Allah, for the limits of Allah, for the obligations of Allah, and for establishing the religion of Allah. Indeed, authority is a mercy from Allah which He placed among His servants, and were it not for it, some of them would raid others, and the strong among them would devour the weak.

Mujahid said: ﴿a supporting authority﴾ means a clear proof.

Ibn Jarir chose the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it is the more preponderant, because with the truth there must necessarily be domination over those who oppose it and contend with it. For this reason Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book and the Balance so that people may maintain justice. And We sent down iron, wherein is great military might and benefits for people, and that Allah may make evident those who support Him and His messengers unseen.﴾ [al-Hadid: 25] And in a hadith: "Indeed Allah restrains by the authority what He does not restrain by the Qur'an," meaning: He prevents by the authority from committing abominations and sins what many people are not restrained from by the Qur'an, despite its firm warnings and severe threats. And this is what actually happens.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And say, "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish."﴾ it is a threat and warning to the Quraysh disbelievers, for there has come to them from Allah the truth about which there is no doubt and against which they have no power, namely what Allah sent him with of the Qur'an, faith, and beneficial knowledge. Their falsehood vanished, meaning it perished and was destroyed, for falsehood has no permanence or survival alongside the truth: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18]

Al-Bukhari said: al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah while around the House there were three hundred and sixty idols, and he began striking them with a stick in his hand, saying: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish.﴾ "The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores." [2]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in other places, as did Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i, all through various chains from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah with the same wording. [3] [Likewise, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Najih.]

Likewise, the hafiz Abu Ya'la narrated: Zuhayr narrated to us, Shababah narrated to us, al-Mughirah narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: We entered Makkah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols worshipped besides Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them, and they were overturned on their faces, and he said: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished, indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish." [4]

---

[1] Musnad (1/223).
[2] Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4720).
[3] Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2478, 4287); Sahih Muslim, no. (1781); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3138); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11297).
[4] Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (14/487) from Shababah ibn Sawwar.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 17, verse 82:

He, the Exalted, says, informing about His Book which He sent down to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), which is the Qur'an, "that falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it; a revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy" — that it is ﴿a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾. That is, it removes the diseases in the hearts: doubt, hypocrisy, polytheism, deviation, and inclination (to falsehood). So the Qur'an heals from all of that. It is also a mercy, through which faith, wisdom, the seeking of good, and the desire for it are attained. This is only for those who believe in it, affirm it, and follow it, for it becomes a healing and a mercy for them. As for the disbelieving wrongdoer who wrongs himself thereby, hearing the Qur'an increases him only in distance, denial, and disbelief. The affliction is from the disbeliever, not from the Qur'an, as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and a healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is for them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place."﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, among them are some who say, "Which of you has this increased in faith?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it has increased them in evil, along with their evil, and they die while they are disbelievers.﴾ [At-Tawbah: 124-125]. The verses on this are [[In T and F: "this"]] numerous.

Qatada said, regarding His saying: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾: when the believer hears it, he benefits from it, memorizes it, and comprehends it. ﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾: indeed, he does not benefit from it, nor does he memorize it, nor comprehend it [[In F: "he does not memorize it nor benefit from it"]]. For Allah has made this Qur'an a healing and a mercy for the believers.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verses 83–84:

He, exalted is He, informs about the deficiency of man as such, except for the one whom Allah protects, in both his states of ease and hardship. When Allah bestows upon him wealth, health, opening (of affairs), provision and victory, and he attains what he wants, he turns away from the obedience of Allah and His worship, and turns aside (nata bi-janibihi).

Mujahid said: "He distances himself from us."

I say: This is like His saying: ﴿So when We removed from him his harm, he passed on as if he had never invoked Us for a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12], and His saying ﴿Then when He brings you safely to land, you turn away﴾ [al-Isra: 67].

And [he is deficient] in that when evil touches him — and that is calamities, events and misfortunes — ﴿he is despairing﴾, meaning he despairs that good will ever come to him again after that, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We let him taste favor after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: "The evils have gone from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful. Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; for those there is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Hud: 10–11].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, each works according to his manner (shakilatihi)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "According to his way (nahiyatihi)." Mujahid said: "According to his disposition and nature (tabi'atihi)." Qatadah said: "According to his intention (niyyatihi)." Ibn Zayd said: "According to his religion (dinihi)."

All these statements are close in meaning. This verse — and Allah knows best — is a warning and threat to the polytheists, like His saying: ﴿And say to those who do not believe: "Work according to your position; indeed, we are working. And wait; indeed, we are waiting"﴾ [Hud: 121–122]. Therefore He said: ﴿Say, each works according to his manner, but your Lord is most knowing of who is best guided in way﴾, meaning: of us and of you. He will recompense every worker for his deed, for nothing is hidden from Him.
