Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 85:

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a field in Madinah, and he was leaning on a palm-stick. He passed by a group of Jews, and some of them said to others: 'Ask him about the spirit.' Some of them said: 'Do not ask him.' He said: So they asked him about the spirit, and they said: 'O Muhammad, what is the spirit?' He kept leaning on the palm-stick and did not answer. I thought that he was being revealed to, so he said: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾"

Then some of them said to others: "We told you not to ask him."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it in this way from the hadith (prophetic report) of al-A'mash, with the same chain. [[Musnad (1/389), Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (125, 7462), Sahih Muslim no. (2794).]] The wording of al-Bukhari, under the tafsir of this verse, is from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "While I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a field, and he was leaning on a palm-stick, the Jews passed by. Some of them said to others: 'Ask him about the spirit.' Others said: 'Do not let him confront you with something you dislike.' They said: 'Ask him.' So they asked him about the spirit. The Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent and did not answer him at all. I knew that he was being revealed to, so I stood in my place. When the revelation came down, he said: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord⦆, [the verse]." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4721).]]

This context indicates, at first glance, that this verse is Madani (revealed in Madinah), and that it was revealed when the Jews asked him about this in Madinah, although the whole surah is Makki (revealed in Makkah). It may be answered that it was possibly revealed to him in Madinah a second time, just as it had been revealed to him in Makkah before that, or that revelation came to him instructing him to answer them about what they asked, by means of the verse previously revealed to him, which is this verse: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit⦆. Among what indicates that this verse was revealed in Makkah is what Imam Ahmad said:

Qutayba narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Quraysh said to the Jews: 'Give us something to ask this man about.' They said: 'Ask him about the spirit.' So they asked him, and the verse came down: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.⦆ They said: 'We have been given much knowledge; we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good.' He said: Allah revealed: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement⦆ [al-Kahf: 109]. [[Musnad (1/255).]]

Ibn Jarir narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Dawud, from 'Ikrima, who said: "The People of the Book asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the spirit, so Allah revealed: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.⦆ They said: 'He claims that we have been given only a little knowledge, while we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom, and whoever is given wisdom has been given much good?' [al-Baqara: 269]. He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted⦆ [Luqman: 27]. He said: 'What you have been given of knowledge, by which Allah has saved you from the Fire, is much and good, though it is little in the knowledge of Allah.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/104).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some of his companions, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: "The verse ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little⦆ was revealed in Makkah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, the rabbis of the Jews came to him and said: 'O Muhammad, has it not reached us that you say: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little⦆? Do you mean us, or do you mean your people?' He said: 'Both of you are meant.' They said: 'You recite that we have been given the Torah, and in it is the explanation of everything.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'It is little in the knowledge of Allah, and He has given you what, if you act upon it, you will be upright.' And Allah revealed: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Almighty and Wise⦆ [Luqman: 27]."

The exegetes (mufassirun) differed about what is meant by "the spirit" here, in several opinions:

The first: that what is meant by "the spirit" is the spirits of the children of Adam.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit⦆, the verse, and that is because the Jews said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Tell us about the spirit: How is the spirit that is in the body punished, when the spirit is from Allah?" Nothing had been revealed to him about it, so he did not answer them with anything. Then Jibril came to him and said: ﴿Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.⦆ The Prophet (ﷺ) informed them of that, and they said: "Who brought you this?" He said: "Jibril brought it to me from Allah." They said: "By Allah, only an enemy of ours told you this." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Jibril – indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah, confirming what came before it⦆ [al-Baqara: 97].

It was also said: What is meant by "the spirit" here is Jibril. This was said by Qatada, who added: "Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal it."

It was also said: What is meant by it here is a great angel, equal in size to all created beings. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his saying: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit⦆, that he said: "The spirit is an angel."

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Urs al-Misri narrated to us, Wahb ibn Rizq Abu Hurayra narrated to us, Bishr ibn Bakr narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, 'Ata' narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed, Allah has an angel who, if he were told to swallow the seven heavens and the earths in one mouthful, would do it. His glorification is: Glory be to You wherever You are.'" [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/195). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/80): "I have not seen anyone mention a biography for Wahb ibn Rizq."]]

This is a gharib (strange, weak in chain) hadith, rather munkar (rejected).

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him: "'Ali narrated to me, 'Abdullah narrated to me, Abu Nimran Yazid ibn Sumra, companion of Qaysariyya, narrated to me, from one who narrated to him from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said regarding His saying: ﴿And they ask you about the spirit⦆: 'It is an angel among the angels, who has seventy thousand faces, for each face seventy thousand tongues, for each tongue seventy thousand languages, glorifying Allah the Exalted in all those languages. Allah creates from each glorification an angel that flies with the angels until the Day of Resurrection.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/105).]]

This is a gharib and wondrous report, and Allah knows best.

Al-Suhayli said: It was narrated from 'Ali that he said: "It is an angel, who has one hundred thousand heads, for each head one hundred thousand faces, in each face one hundred thousand mouths, in each mouth one hundred thousand tongues, glorifying Allah the Exalted in different languages."

Al-Suhayli said: It was also said that what is meant by that is a group of angels in the form of the children of Adam.

It was also said: a group who see the angels, but the angels do not see them; they are to the angels as the angels are to the children of Adam.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord⦆ means: it is of His affair, and of what He has kept to His own knowledge apart from you. Therefore He said: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little⦆, meaning: He has not informed you of His knowledge except a little. No one encompasses anything of His knowledge except what He wills, blessed and exalted is He.

The meaning is: your knowledge in the knowledge of Allah is little, and this which you ask about, of the matter of the spirit, is among what He has kept to Himself, and has not informed you about, just as He has not informed you except of a little of His knowledge, exalted is He. It will come, Allah willing, in the story of Musa and al-Khidr: that al-Khidr looked at a sparrow that alighted on the edge of the boat and pecked once into the sea, meaning it drank from it with its beak. He said: "O Musa, my knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of all creatures, in the knowledge of Allah, is no more than what this sparrow has taken from this sea." Or as he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said. Therefore the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And you have been given of knowledge only a little.⦆

Al-Suhayli said: Some people said: "He did not answer them in what they asked, because they asked in a spirit of provocation (ta'annut)." It was also said: "He did answer them." Al-Suhayli relied on the view that what is meant by His saying: ﴿Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord⦆ is: of His legislation (shar'), that is, enter into it, and you already know that, because there is no path to knowing this through nature or philosophy, but it is attained only through the revealed law (shar'). There is scrutiny in this path which he followed and took, and Allah knows best.

Then al-Suhayli mentioned the disagreement among scholars about whether the spirit is the soul (nafs) or something else, and he established that it is a subtle entity like air, flowing in the body as water flows in the roots of a tree. He established that the spirit which the angel breathes into the fetus is the soul, on condition of its connection to the body, and its acquiring, through it, qualities of praise or blame; so it is either a soul at peace (mutma'inna) or one that commands to evil (ammara bi-l-su'). He said: Just as water is the life of a tree, then by its mixing with it, it acquires a specific name; when it is joined to a grape and pressed from it, it becomes either must (musattar) or wine, and it is no longer called "water" then except figuratively. Likewise the soul is not called "spirit" except in this manner, and similarly the spirit is not called "soul" except in regard to what it will become. So the summary of what he says is that the spirit is the origin and substance of the soul, and the soul is composed of it and of its connection to the body; so it is itself in one respect, but not in every respect. [[Al-Rawd al-Unf (1/198, 199).]] This is a good meaning, and Allah knows best.

I say: People have spoken about the reality (mahiyya) of the spirit and its rulings, and have written books on that. Among the best who spoke on it is the Hafiz Ibn Mandah, in a book we heard, titled: al-Ruh. [[The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, has a book al-Ruh, published with the edition of Bassam al-'Amush; he quotes most of it from this book of Ibn Mandah and mentions its summary.]]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 17, verses 86–89:

Allah mentions His blessing and His great favour upon His servant and noble messenger, in what He revealed to him of the glorious Qur'an, "which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it; a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy" (Qur'an 41:42).

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "A red wind will sweep over the people from the direction of al-Sham (Greater Syria) at the end of time, and no verse will remain in a man's mushaf (copy of the Qur'an) or in his heart." Then Ibn Mas'ud recited: "And if We willed, We could surely take away what We have revealed to you" (Qur'an 17:86), to the end of the verse.

Then Allah draws attention to the nobility of this great Qur'an. He informs that even if all of mankind and the jinn were gathered together and agreed to produce the like of what He sent down to His messenger, they would not be able to do so, and they would not be capable of it, even if they helped one another, supported one another and backed one another, for this is a matter that cannot be accomplished. How could the speech of created beings resemble the speech of the Creator, who has no equal, no like and no peer?

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Sa'id [ibn Jubayr] [[An addition from manuscripts Fa and A, and al-Tabari (15/106).]] or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: "We can bring you the like of what you have brought," so Allah revealed this verse.

This is questionable, because this surah is Meccan, its whole context concerns the Quraysh, and the Jews only gathered with him in Medina. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: "And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example" (Qur'an 17:89), it means: We have made clear to them the decisive proofs and evidences, and We have explained the truth to them, clarified it and expounded it. Yet despite this, "most of the people refuse except to deny" (Qur'an 17:89), meaning: they persist in denial and reject what is right.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, a shaykh from the people of Egypt who had arrived some forty-odd years earlier told me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that 'Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and a man from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, and Abu al-Bakhtari, a brother of the Banu Asad, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad, and Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham [[In (manuscript) T: "Hashim", which is an error.]] and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and al-'As ibn Wa'il, and Nubayh and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj of the Banu Sahm, gathered, or: those of them who gathered, after sunset beside the back of the Ka'bah. Some of them said to others: "Send to Muhammad, speak with him and dispute with him until you have an excuse regarding him." So they sent to him: "The nobles of your people have gathered for you so that they may speak with you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them quickly, thinking that some new thing had appeared to them regarding his affair, and he was eager for them, desiring their guidance and grieved by their distress, until he sat down with them. They said: "O Muhammad, we sent for you so that we may have an excuse concerning you. By Allah, we know of no man among the Arabs who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people! You have reviled the forefathers, you have found fault with the religion, you have declared the minds foolish, you have cursed the gods, and you have divided the community. There is no ugly matter left that you have not brought between us and you! If you came with this speech seeking wealth, we will gather for you of our wealth until you are the richest of us. If you seek nobility among us, we will make you our chief. If you want kingship, we will make you our king. And if what comes to you is a jinn [[In (manuscript) F: "and".]] that you see has overcome you—and they used to call the companion from the jinn the ri'y (a companion jinn)—then perhaps that is the case, and we will spend our wealth seeking a physician, until we cure you of it or have an excuse regarding you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is nothing in me of what you say. I did not come to you with what I have brought seeking your wealth, nor nobility among you, nor kingship over you. Rather, Allah sent me to you as a messenger and revealed to me a Book, and commanded me to be for you a bringer of good news and a warner. So I conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely. If you accept from me what I have brought you, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I will be patient over the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you." Or as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, with peace.

They said: "O Muhammad, if you will not accept from us what we have offered you, then you know that no one among the people is more restricted in land than we are, nor has less wealth, nor a harder life. So ask your Lord who sent you with what He sent you, that He remove from us these mountains that have constricted us, and that He spread out our lands for us, and that He make rivers gush forth in them like the rivers of al-Sham and al-'Iraq, and that He raise for us those of our forefathers who have passed away—and let Qusayy ibn Kilab be among those raised for us, for he was an elderly and truthful shaykh—so that we may ask them about what you say: is it true or false? If you do what we asked of you, and they confirm you, we will confirm you, and we will know your standing with Allah, and that He sent you as a messenger as you claim!"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I was not sent with this. I have only come to you from Allah with what He sent me with. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with. If you accept it, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I will be patient over the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you."

They said: "If you will not do this for us, then ask for yourself: ask your Lord to send an angel who will confirm what you say and answer us on your behalf, and you ask Him to give you gardens, treasures, and palaces of gold and silver, and to make you independent of what we see you seeking. For you walk in the markets and seek livelihood as we seek it, so that we may recognize the excellence of your standing with your Lord, if you are a messenger as you claim."

By Allah, I will never believe in you until you take a ladder up to the sky and climb it while I watch, until you reach it and come to me with a published scroll, with four angels with you bearing witness that you are as you say. By Allah, even if you did that, I would think that I do not believe you!" Then he turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his household, grieved and saddened over what he had lost of what he had hoped for from his people when they called him, and because of what he saw of their distancing themselves from him [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/296).]].

As for this assembly which these people gathered for: if Allah had known of them that they were asking that out of seeking guidance, they would have been answered. But He knew that they were only seeking it out of disbelief and obstinacy. So it was said to the Messenger: "If you wish, We will give them what they asked for, but if they disbelieve, I will punish them with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, We will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, open for them the door of repentance and mercy," as has already passed in the two hadiths of Ibn Abbas and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam as well, at the words of His Exalted saying: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We do not send the signs except as a warning.﴾ [al-Isra': 59]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿They said: "What is this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him to be a warner with him, or a treasure cast down to him, or a garden for him to eat from?" And the wrongdoers said: "You follow only a man bewitched." See how they have struck for you comparisons, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way. Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and will give you palaces. But they denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire.﴾ [al-Furqan: 7–11].

* *

And His Exalted saying: ﴿Until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.﴾ Al-yanbu' is the flowing spring. They asked him to make a flowing spring come forth for them in the land of al-Hijaz here and there. That is easy and simple for Allah, Exalted. Had He willed, He would have done it and answered them in all that they asked and demanded. But He knew that they would not be guided, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those against whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96, 97]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered against them all things before them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed; but most of them are ignorant.﴾ [al-An'am: 111].

And His Exalted saying: ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed.﴾ That is: you promised us that on the Day of Resurrection the sky will be split open and will crumble, and its edges will hang down. And so it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Or there be for you a house of gold." ﴿Or you ascend into the sky.﴾ That is: you climb up a ladder while we look at you. ﴿And we will not believe in your ascent until you bring down to us a book we can read.﴾ Mujahid said: that is, written in it for each one of them a sheet: "This is a book from Allah for so-and-so son of so-and-so," placed in the morning at his head.

I said: No, my Lord, but I would like to be satisfied one day and hungry one day, or something like that. When I am hungry, I will humble myself before You and remember You, and when I am satisfied, I will praise You and thank You."

And al-Tirmidhi related it in "al-Zuhd" from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain [[Musnad (5/245) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2347). Abd Allah ibn Zahr, Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim are weak narrators.]] and said: This is a hasan (sound-to-fair) hadith. And Ali ibn Yazid is declared weak in hadith.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, a shaykh from the people of Egypt who had arrived some forty-odd years earlier told me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that 'Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and a man from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, and Abu al-Bakhtari, a brother of the Banu Asad, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad, and Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham [[In (manuscript) T: "Hashim", which is an error.]] and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and al-'As ibn Wa'il, and Nubayh and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj of the Banu Sahm, gathered, or: those of them who gathered, after sunset beside the back of the Ka'bah. Some of them said to others: "Send to Muhammad, speak with him and dispute with him until you have an excuse regarding him." So they sent to him: "The nobles of your people have gathered for you so that they may speak with you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them quickly, thinking that some new thing had appeared to them regarding his affair, and he was eager for them, desiring their guidance and grieved by their distress, until he sat down with them. They said: "O Muhammad, we sent for you so that we may have an excuse concerning you. By Allah, we know of no man among the Arabs who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people! You have reviled the forefathers, you have found fault with the religion, you have declared the minds foolish, you have cursed the gods, and you have divided the community. There is no ugly matter left that you have not brought between us and you! If you came with this speech seeking wealth, we will gather for you of our wealth until you are the richest of us. If you seek nobility among us, we will make you our chief. If you want kingship, we will make you our king. And if what comes to you is a jinn [[In (manuscript) F: "and".]] that you see has overcome you—and they used to call the companion from the jinn the ri'y (a companion jinn)—then perhaps that is the case, and we will spend our wealth seeking a physician, until we cure you of it or have an excuse regarding you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is nothing in me of what you say. I did not come to you with what I have brought seeking your wealth, nor nobility among you, nor kingship over you. Rather, Allah sent me to you as a messenger and revealed to me a Book, and commanded me to be for you a bringer of good news and a warner. So I conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely. If you accept from me what I have brought you, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I will be patient over the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you." Or as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, with peace.

They said: "O Muhammad, if you will not accept from us what we have offered you, then you know that no one among the people is more restricted in land than we are, nor has less wealth, nor a harder life. So ask your Lord who sent you with what He sent you, that He remove from us these mountains that have constricted us, and that He spread out our lands for us, and that He make rivers gush forth in them like the rivers of al-Sham and al-'Iraq, and that He raise for us those of our forefathers who have passed away—and let Qusayy ibn Kilab be among those raised for us, for he was an elderly and truthful shaykh—so that we may ask them about what you say: is it true or false? If you do what we asked of you, and they confirm you, we will confirm you, and we will know your standing with Allah, and that He sent you as a messenger as you claim!"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I was not sent with this. I have only come to you from Allah with what He sent me with. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with. If you accept it, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I will be patient over the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you."

They said: "If you will not do this for us, then ask for yourself: ask your Lord to send an angel who will confirm what you say and answer us on your behalf, and you ask Him to give you gardens, treasures, and palaces of gold and silver, and to make you independent of what we see you seeking. For you walk in the markets and seek livelihood as we seek it, so that we may recognize the excellence of your standing with your Lord, if you are a messenger as you claim."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I will not do it. I am not one who asks his Lord for this, and I was not sent to you with this. Rather, Allah sent me as a bringer of good news and a warner. If you accept what I have brought you, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I will be patient over the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you."

They said: "Then make the sky fall upon us, as you claimed your Lord would do if He willed, for we will not believe you unless you do."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "That is up to Allah. If He wills, He will do that to you."

They said: "O Muhammad, does your Lord not know that we will sit with you, and ask you about what we asked you about, and demand from you what we demand, so that He would send ahead to you and teach you what you should answer us with, and inform you what He will do with us if we do not accept from you what you have brought us? It has reached us that what teaches you this is only a man in al-Yamamah called al-Rahman, and by Allah, we will never believe in al-Rahman! So we have given you an excuse, O Muhammad. By Allah, we will not leave you and what you have done to us until we destroy you or you destroy us." And one of them said: "We worship the angels, and they are the daughters of Allah." And another of them said: "We will not believe you until you bring Allah and the angels as a tribal guarantee [[In (manuscript) F: "bring us".]]."

When they said that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose from them, and there rose with him 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Makhzum, who was his paternal cousin (son of his aunt), son of 'Atikah daughter of 'Abd al-Muttalib. He said: "O Muhammad, your people offered you what they offered, and you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for things for themselves, so that they might recognize your standing with Allah, and you did not do that. Then they asked you to hasten for them what you warn them of of punishment, and you did not do that. By Allah, I will never believe in you until you take a ladder up to the sky and climb it while I watch, until you reach it and come to me with a published scroll, with four angels with you bearing witness that you are as you say. By Allah, even if you did that, I would think that I do not believe you!" Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verse 90–93 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Ubaid Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim [[In T: "Alatim".]] from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "My Lord, mighty and majestic, offered me that the valley of Makkah be made gold for me. I said: No, my Lord, but I would like to be satisfied one day and hungry one day, or something like that. When I am hungry, I will humble myself before You and remember You, and when I am satisfied, I will praise You and thank You."

And al-Tirmidhi related it in "al-Zuhd" from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with the same chain [[Musnad (5/245) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2347). Abd Allah ibn Zahr, Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim are weak narrators.]] and said: This is a hasan (sound-to-fair) hadith. And Ali ibn Yazid is declared weak in hadith.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And nothing prevented the people﴾, meaning most of them, ﴿from believing﴾ and following the messengers, except their astonishment that He sent humans as messengers. As He says: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them: "Warn the people and give good news to those who believe"?﴾ [Yunus: 2]

And He says: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Would mortals guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient, and Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy.﴾ [al-Taghabun: 6] Pharaoh and his chiefs said: ﴿Shall we believe two mortals like us, while their people are servants to us?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 47] Likewise the nations said to their messengers: ﴿You are only mortals like us. You want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship, so bring us a clear authority.﴾ [Ibrahim: 10] The verses on this are many.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, drawing attention to His gentleness and mercy toward His servants: He sends to them a messenger of their own kind, so that they may understand him and comprehend from him, and so that they are able to address him and converse with him. Had He sent an angel as a messenger to mankind, they would not have been able to face him or take knowledge from him. As He says: ﴿Allah certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 164]. And He says: ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128]. And He says: ﴿Just as We sent among you a messenger from yourselves, who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you what you did not know. So remember Me, and I will remember you; and be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 151–152]

For this reason He says here: ﴿If there were angels walking calmly on the earth﴾, meaning as you walk upon it, ﴿We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾, meaning of their own kind. And since you are humans, We have sent among you messengers from among you, out of gentleness and mercy.

[Variant in manuscript T: "قالوا" (qalu).]
[Variant in manuscript T: "رسلا" (rusulan).]

Allah, exalted is He, says, guiding His Prophet to the proof against his people regarding the truth of what he brought them: "He is a witness between me and you, knowing what I have brought you. Had I been lying [against Him] [[addition from A.]], He would have taken vengeance upon me with the utmost vengeance," as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if he had invented against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 44-46].

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ means: He is Knowing of them, of who deserves favor, kindness and guidance, and of who deserves wretchedness, misguidance [[in T: "ḍalāl"]] and turning away. Therefore He said:

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, explaining God's disposal of His creation, the execution of His judgment, and that there is no one to repel it:

Whoever Allah guides, he is the one rightly guided, and whoever He leaves astray, you will not find for them protectors other than Him (i.e., who would guide them), as He said: ﴿Whoever Allah guides is the one rightly guided, and whoever He leaves astray - you will not find for him any guiding ally﴾ [al-Kahf: 17].

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces﴾, Imam Ahmad said:

Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Isma'il narrated to us from Nufay' [[In T: "Nufay' - so he said."]], who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will people be gathered upon their faces?" He said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs.

Imam Ahmad also said: [Yazid narrated to us] [[Addition from T, F, A, and the Musnad.]], al-Walid ibn Jumay' al-Qurashi narrated to us, from his father, Abu al-Tufayl 'Amir ibn Wathila narrated to us, from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, who said: Abu Dhar stood up and said: "O Banu Ghifar, speak and do not swear, for the truthful, the believed one (ﷺ) told me that people will be gathered in three groups: a group riding, eating, and clothed; a group walking and running; and a group whom the angels will drag upon their faces and gather to the Fire." One of them said: "These two we know, so what about those who walk and run?" He said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will send the calamity upon the mounts, until no mount remains, so much so that a man would have a pleasing garden and would give it in exchange for a she-camel with a saddle, and he would not be able to obtain it."[[Musnad (5/164).]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿Blind﴾, meaning they cannot see; ﴿dumb﴾, meaning they cannot speak; and ﴿deaf﴾, meaning they cannot hear. This will be in some states and not others, as a recompense for them, just as they were in the world dumb, blind, and deaf to the truth; so they are repaid in their gathering with that at the time they most need. ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾, meaning their place of return and their destination. ﴿Whenever it subsides﴾ - Ibn 'Abbas said: it dies down. Mujahid said: it is extinguished. ﴿We will increase them in blaze﴾, meaning flame, blazing heat, and embers, as He said: ﴿So taste, for We will not increase you except in punishment﴾ [an-Naba': 30].

This is what We requite them with: being raised blind, dumb and deaf. That is their deserved recompense, because they denied Our signs (بِآيَاتِنَا), that is, Our proofs and arguments, and they considered the resurrection unlikely. (They said: "When we are bones and crumbled dust"), decayed and rotten, ("Shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"), that is: after we have become what we have become of decay and destruction, and of being scattered and dispersed in the earth, shall we be brought back again a second time?

Allah says to His Messenger (ﷺ): Say to them, O Muhammad: If you, O people, were to possess control over the treasures of Allah, you would withhold them for fear of spending.

Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: "Al-infaq" here means poverty, i.e., for fear that you would exhaust them, even though they never run out nor are ever depleted, because this is from your natures and dispositions. For this reason He said: ﴿And man has ever been tight-fisted﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: that is, stingy and withholding.

Indeed, miserliness, impatience and anxiety are characteristics of him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, man was created anxious. When evil touches him, he is distressed. Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verses 102–104:

He, exalted is He, informs that He sent Musa with nine clear signs (ayat bayyinat), which are the decisive proofs of the authenticity of his prophethood and the truthfulness of what he reported from the One who sent him to Pharaoh. They are: the staff, the hand, the years (of drought), the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, as detailed signs (ayat mufassalat). This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: they are the hand, the staff, the five in al-A'raf, the effacement (al-tamsah) and the stone.

Ibn 'Abbas also said, as did Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi and Qatadah: they are his hand, his staff, the years, the loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood.

This opinion is apparent, clear, sound and strong. Al-Hasan al-Basri counted "the years and the loss of fruits" as one, and according to him the ninth is: the staff's swallowing of what they fabricated (talaqquf al-'asa ma ya'fikun).

Allah says: ﴿So they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people﴾ [al-A'raf: 133], meaning: despite these signs and their witnessing of them, they disbelieved in them and denied them, and their souls were certain of them out of injustice and haughtiness, and it did not benefit them. Likewise, if We had answered these people who asked you, and they had asked, saying: ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth﴾ [al-Isra': 90], to the end of them, they would not have responded nor believed, except that Allah wills. Just as Pharaoh said to Musa, after he had witnessed from him what he witnessed of these signs: "Indeed, I think you, O Musa, are bewitched (masluran)." It was said: meaning, a sorcerer. And Allah knows best.

These nine signs mentioned by these imams are what is intended here, and they are what is meant in the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And throw down your staff.' And when he saw it moving as if it were a snake, he turned in retreat and did not return. 'O Musa, do not fear. Indeed, the messengers do not fear in My presence. Except one who wrongs and then substitutes good after evil - indeed, I am Forgiving and Merciful. And put your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without disease, as one of nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they have always been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾ [an-Naml: 10–12]. So He mentioned these two verses: the staff and the hand, and explained the remaining signs in Surat al-A'raf and detailed them.

Musa, peace be upon him, was also given many other signs, among them his striking the stone with the staff and the gushing of rivers from it, and the shading of them with clouds, and the sending down of manna and quail, and other things that the Children of Israel were given after they left the land of Egypt. But here He mentioned the nine signs that Pharaoh and his people from the people of Egypt witnessed, and which were a proof against them, yet they opposed them and obstinately denied them out of disbelief and denial.

As for the hadith which Imam [Ahmad] narrated:

Yazid told us: Shu'bah told us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Salamah narrate, from Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A Jew said to his companion: "Come, let us go to this Prophet (ﷺ) so that we may ask him about this verse: (And We certainly gave Musa nine clear signs)." His companion said: "Do not call him a prophet, for if he hears you, he will have four eyes." So they asked him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not associate anything with Allah, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, do not practise sorcery, do not consume usury, do not walk with an innocent person to a ruler to have him killed, do not slander a chaste woman" - or he said: "do not flee from the battle line" - Shu'bah being doubtful - "and for you, O Jews, especially, is that you not transgress on the Sabbath." So they kissed his hands and feet and said: "We testify that you are a prophet." He said: "What prevents you both from following me?" They said: "Because Dawud, peace be upon him, supplicated that there should never cease to be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we embrace Islam, the Jews will kill us."

This hadith was narrated in this form by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, through various chains from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, with the same wording. [al-Musnad (4/239), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3144), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/111), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3705), and Tafsir al-Tabari (15/115).] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

It is a problematic hadith. 'Abdullah ibn Salamah has some weakness in his memory, and they have spoken about him. Perhaps the nine signs were confused for him with the ten words (al-'Ashr al-Kalimat), for those are the commandments in the Torah, which have no connection with establishing the proof against Pharaoh. And Allah knows best.

For this reason Musa said to Pharaoh: ﴿You have certainly known that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence﴾ — meaning, proofs and indications of the truth of what I have brought you — ﴿and indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ — meaning, destroyed. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn 'Abbas said: cursed. He also said, as did al-Dahhak: "mathbur" means defeated. And "al-halik" (the destroyed), as Mujahid said, encompasses all of this. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said:

"When I contend with Satan on the paths of error, and whoever inclines to its inclination is mathbur"

[with the meaning of halik].

Some read the taʾ in His words "ʿalimtu" with a damma, and this is narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib. But the reading of the majority is with a fatha on the taʾ, addressed to Pharaoh, as Allah says: ﴿So when Our signs came to them as visible, they said, "This is obvious magic." And they denied them, while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾ [an-Naml: 13–14].

All of this indicates that what is intended by the nine signs is only what was mentioned before: the staff, the hand, the years, the loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, in which there are proofs and demonstrations against Pharaoh and his people, and extraordinary events and indications of the truthfulness of Musa and the existence of the Free Chooser who sent him. What is meant is not what occurs in this hadith, for these commandments contain no proofs against Pharaoh and his people, and what relation is there between this and establishing the demonstrations against Pharaoh? This confusion came only from 'Abdullah ibn Salamah, for he has some things that are disapproved of. And Allah knows best. Perhaps those two Jews were asking about the ten words, but the narrator confused them with the nine signs, and so an error arose in this. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿so he wanted to expel them from the land﴾ — meaning, to clear them out of it and remove them from it — ﴿so We drowned him and those with him, all together. And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land."﴾ In this is good news for Muhammad (ﷺ) of the conquest of Makkah, although the surah was revealed before the Hijrah, and so it happened. For the people of Makkah planned to expel the Messenger from it, as Allah says: ﴿And indeed, they almost drove you from the land to expel you from it, but then they would not remain after you except for a little. And here He says: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land. [al-Musnad (4/239), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3144), Sunan al-Nasa'i (7/111), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3705), and Tafsir al-Tabari (15/115).] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih.

It is a problematic hadith. 'Abdullah ibn Salamah has some weakness in his memory, and they have spoken about him. Perhaps the nine signs were confused for him with the ten words (al-'Ashr al-Kalimat), for those are the commandments in the Torah, which have no connection with establishing the proof against Pharaoh. And Allah knows best.

For this reason Musa said to Pharaoh: ﴿You have certainly known that these have not sent down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence﴾ — meaning, proofs and indications of the truth of what I have brought you — ﴿and indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾ — meaning, destroyed. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn 'Abbas said: cursed. He also said, as did al-Dahhak: "mathbur" means defeated. And "al-halik" (the destroyed), as Mujahid said, encompasses all of this. 'Abdullah ibn al-Zib'ara said:

"When I contend with Satan on the paths of error, and whoever inclines to its inclination is mathbur"

[with the meaning of halik].

Some read the taʾ in His words "ʿalimtu" with a damma, and this is narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib. But the reading of the majority is with a fatha on the taʾ, addressed to Pharaoh, as Allah says: ﴿So when Our signs came to them as visible, they said, "This is obvious magic." And they denied them, while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾ [an-Naml: 13–14].

All of this indicates that what is intended by the nine signs is only what was mentioned before: the staff, the hand, the years, the loss of fruits, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, in which there are proofs and demonstrations against Pharaoh and his people, and extraordinary events and indications of the truthfulness of Musa and the existence of the Free Chooser who sent him. What is meant is not what occurs in this hadith, for these commandments contain no proofs against Pharaoh and his people, and what relation is there between this and establishing the demonstrations against Pharaoh? This confusion came only from 'Abdullah ibn Salamah, for he has some things that are disapproved of. And Allah knows best. Perhaps those two Jews were asking about the ten words, but the narrator confused them with the nine signs, and so an error arose in this. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿so he wanted to expel them from the land﴾ — meaning, to clear them out of it and remove them from it — ﴿so We drowned him and those with him, all together. And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land."﴾ In this is good news for Muhammad (ﷺ) of the conquest of Makkah, although the surah was revealed before the Hijrah, and so it happened. For the people of Makkah planned to expel the Messenger from it, as Allah says: ﴿And indeed, they almost drove you from the land to expel you from it, but then they would not remain after you except for a little. [It is] the way of those We sent before you of Our messengers, and you will not find any alteration in Our way﴾ [al-Isra': 76–77]. For this reason Allah made His Messenger inherit Makkah, and he entered it by force according to the more well-known of the two opinions, subdued its people, then released them out of forbearance and generosity, just as Allah made the people who had been oppressed among the Children of Israel inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth, and gave them the land of Pharaoh, his wealth, his crops, his fruits and his treasures, as He says: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 59]. And here He says: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land. So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you forth as a mixed multitude."﴾ — meaning, all of you together with your enemy.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: "lafifan" means all together.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 17, verses 105–106:

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about His Mighty Book, which is the Glorious Qur'an, that it was sent down with the truth. That is, it contains the truth, as He said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾ [An-Nisa: 166]. That is, it contains the knowledge of Allah, which He wished to make you aware of, concerning His rulings, His commands and His prohibitions.

* *

His saying: ﴿and with the truth it has descended﴾ means: it reached you, O Muhammad, preserved and guarded, not mixed with anything else, nor was anything added to it or taken from it. Rather, it reached you with the truth, for it was brought down by one of great power, the trustworthy, the honored, the one obeyed in the Exalted Assembly (al-Mala' al-A'la, the angels of the heavens).

* *

His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you﴾ means: O Muhammad, ﴿except as a bringer of good news﴾ to those among the believers who obey you, ﴿and a warner﴾ to those among the disbelievers who disobey you.

* *

His saying: ﴿And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated﴾. As for the reading of the one who recites it with the light pronunciation (farraqnahu with takhfif), its meaning is: We detailed it from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the House of Honor (Bayt al-Izzah) in the lowest heaven. Then it descended in separated portions, staggered according to events, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over twenty-three years. This was said by Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas.

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: ﴿farraqnahu﴾ with the heavy pronunciation (tashdid) means: We sent it down verse by verse, clarified and explained. Therefore He said: ﴿so that you may recite it to the people﴾, that is, so that you may convey it to the people and recite it to them, ﴿at a gradual pace﴾, that is, with deliberation, ﴿and We have sent it down in stages﴾, that is, little by little.

Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these disbelievers concerning this Great Qur'an that you have brought them: ﴿Believe in it or do not believe.﴾ That is, whether you believe in it or not, it is true in itself. Allah sent it down and mentioned it in earlier times, in the Scriptures He revealed to His messengers. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it﴾, that is, from among the righteous People of the Book who hold fast to their Scripture and establish it, and who have neither altered nor distorted it, ﴿when it is recited to them﴾, this Qur'an, ﴿they fall down upon their faces prostrating﴾. The word "adhqan" is the plural of "dhaqn," which is the lower part of the face. ﴿Prostrating﴾, that is, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in gratitude for what He has bestowed upon them, by making them people who, if they lived to see this Messenger to whom this Book was sent down, would be worthy of it. For this reason they say: ﴿Glory be to our Lord﴾, that is, in exaltation and reverence of His complete power, and that He does not break the promise He made to them through the tongues of the prophets who came before, concerning the sending of Muhammad ﷺ. For this reason they said: ﴿Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they fall down upon their faces weeping﴾, that is, in humility before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in faith and affirmation of His Book and His Messenger. And Allah increases them in ﴿khushu'﴾, that is, in faith and submission, as He said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 17, verses 110–111:

He, may He be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny the attribute of mercy to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, and who refuse to name Him "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahman): ﴿Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names.﴾ That is, there is no difference between your calling upon Him by the name "Allah" or by the name "al-Rahman", for He is the Possessor of the most beautiful names, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth exalts Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [al-Hashr: 22–24].

Makhul [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/121); it seems the Hafiz abridged it here.]] narrated that a man among the polytheists heard the Prophet ﷺ saying in his prostration: "O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate," and said: "He claims that he calls upon one God, yet he calls upon two." So Allah revealed this verse. Similarly, it is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Jarir narrated both.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾ and the rest of the verse, Imam Ahmad said:

Hushaym narrated to us: Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed while he was hiding in Mecca: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way [[Addition from A.]]﴾. He said: When he led his companions in prayer, he would raise his voice with the Qur'an. When the polytheists heard that, they reviled the Qur'an, reviled the one who revealed it, and reviled the one who brought it. He said: So Allah, may He be exalted, said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾, that is, in your recitation, so that the polytheists hear and revile the Qur'an; ﴿nor be silent therein﴾, from your companions, so that you do not make them hear the Qur'an until they take it from you; ﴿but seek between that a way.﴾

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs from the narration of Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Iyas, with this chain. [[Musnad (1/23); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2722); Sahih Muslim no. (446).]] Likewise al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, adding: "When he migrated to Medina, that ceased, and he did whichever he wished." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/123).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his voice with the Qur'an while praying, they dispersed from him and refused to listen to him. A man who wished to hear some of what he recited while praying would steal a listen apart from them, out of fear of them. If he saw that they had realized he was listening, he would leave, fearing their harm, and so would not listen. If he lowered his voice ﷺ [[In F: "And if the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lowered his voice."]], those who listened would not hear any of his recitation. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾, so that they disperse from you; ﴿nor be silent therein﴾, so that one who wishes to hear it from among those who steal a listen apart from them is not made to hear it; perhaps he will be moved toward some of what he hears and benefit from it; ﴿but seek between that a way.﴾

Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah likewise said: this verse was revealed concerning the recitation in prayer.

Shu'bah narrated from Ash'ath ibn Abi Sulaym [[In H and T: "from Abu Sulaym." The adopted reading is from al-Tabari.]], from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Mas'ud: "It is not silent therein if one makes his own ears hear it."

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn 'Alqamah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was informed that Abu Bakr, when he prayed and recited, would lower his voice, and that 'Umar would raise his voice. It was said to Abu Bakr: Why do you do this? He said: I am conversing with my Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, and He knows my need. It was said: You have done well. It was said to 'Umar: Why do you do this? He said: I drive away the devil and wake the drowsy. It was said: You have done well. When the verse was revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾, it was said to Abu Bakr: Raise your voice a little, and it was said to 'Umar: Lower your voice a little. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/124).]]

Ash'ath ibn Sawwar said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning supplication (du'a'). Similarly, al-Thawri and Malik narrated from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah: it was revealed concerning supplication. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu 'Iyad, Makhul and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Al-Thawri said, from [Ibn] [[Addition from F.]] 'Ayyash al-'Amiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, who said: Some Bedouins of the Banu Tamim, when the Prophet ﷺ finished (the prayer) with the salam, would say: "O Allah, grant us camels and children." He said: So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein.﴾

Another view: Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that this verse was revealed concerning the tashahhud: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein.﴾

Hafs said likewise, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, the same.

Another view: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, that he said: Do not pray for the sake of showing off to people, and do not abandon it out of fear of people. al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from al-Hasan al-Basri: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: Do not beautify its outward appearance while spoiling its inward state. 'Abd al-Razzaq likewise narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, with this wording; Hushaym from 'Awf, from him, with this; and Sa'id from Qatadah, from him, similarly.

Another view: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning His saying: ﴿but seek between that a way﴾, he said: The People of the Book would speak in a low voice, then one of them would raise his voice with a letter and cry out, and they would cry out behind him. So He forbade him to cry out as these do, and to be silent as these people are silent. Then the way that lies between that is what Gabriel prescribed for him in prayer.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion﴾, when He, may He be exalted, affirmed for His noble self the most beautiful names, He declared Himself free of deficiencies, saying: ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness.﴾ Rather, He is Allah, the One, the Self-Sufficient (al-Samad), who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is comparable.

﴿Nor has He any protector out of weakness﴾, that is: He is not weak, so as to need a protector, a helper, or a counsellor. Rather, He, may He be exalted [[Addition from A.]], is the sole Creator of things with no partner, and the sole Determiner and Manager of them by His will, with no partner.

Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿Nor has He any protector out of weakness﴾: He does not form an alliance with anyone, nor does He seek the help of anyone.

﴿And magnify Him with great magnificence﴾, that is: exalt Him and glorify Him above what the wrongdoers and transgressors say, with great exaltation.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr informed me, from al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son…﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: The Jews and the Christians said: Allah has taken a son. The Arabs said: [Labbayka] [[Addition from F.]] Labbayka, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You own him and what he owns. The Sabians and the Magians said: Were it not for the friends of Allah, He would be humiliated. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with great magnificence.﴾

He also said: Bishr narrated to us, [Yazid narrated to us] [[Addition from T, F, A.]], Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ used to teach his family this verse: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with great magnificence,﴾ to the young and the old among them.

I say: It has come in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named it the verse of honour (ayat al-'izz) [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/440) from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Anas, raised to the Prophet: "The verse of honour: 'Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son…' the whole verse."]], and in some reports: that it is not recited in a house on a night when theft or calamity would befall it. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Bishr ibn Sayhan al-Basri narrated to us, Harb ibn Maymun narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, my hand in his hand, and he came upon a man in shabby condition, and he said: "O so-and-so, what has brought you to what I see?" He said: Sickness and harm, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Shall I not teach you words that will remove from you sickness and harm?" He said: No. He said: It would not please me to have them, even if I had been present with you at Badr or Uhud. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said: "Do the people of Badr and the people of Uhud attain what the poor, contented one attains?" He said: Abu Hurayrah then said: O Messenger of Allah, teach them to me. He said: "Say, O Abu Hurayrah: 'I place my trust in the Living One who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with great magnificence.'" He said: Then the Messenger of Allah came to me, and my condition had improved. He said to me: "Mah-yam?" [[In T: "Upon him be the blessing."]] I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have not ceased saying the words you taught me. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (12/23). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/52): "It contains Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak."]]

Its chain is weak, and its text contains an unusual element. [And Allah knows best.] [[Addition from F, A. In T: "End of the tafsir of Surat al-Isra'. Praise and grace belong to Allah; with Him is success and protection. May Allah forgive its copyist, those who read it, his parents, his teachers, and all the Muslims, all of them. Amin."]]

He said: When he led his companions in prayer, he would raise his voice with the Qur'an. When the polytheists heard that, they reviled the Qur'an, reviled the one who revealed it, and reviled the one who brought it. He said: So Allah, may He be exalted, said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾, that is, in your recitation, so that the polytheists hear and revile the Qur'an; ﴿nor be silent therein﴾, from your companions, so that you do not make them hear the Qur'an until they take it from you; ﴿but seek between that a way.﴾

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs from the narration of Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Iyas, with this chain. [[Musnad (1/23); Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2722); Sahih Muslim no. (446).]] Likewise al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, adding: "When he migrated to Medina, that ceased, and he did whichever he wished." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/123).]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his voice with the Qur'an while praying, they dispersed from him and refused to listen to him. A man who wished to hear some of what he recited while praying would steal a listen apart from them, out of fear of them. If he saw that they had realized he was listening, he would leave, fearing their harm, and so would not listen. If he lowered his voice ﷺ [[In F: "And if the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, lowered his voice."]], those who listened would not hear any of his recitation. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾, so that they disperse from you; ﴿nor be silent therein﴾, so that one who wishes to hear it from among those who steal a listen apart from them is not made to hear it; perhaps he will be moved toward some of what he hears and benefit from it; ﴿but seek between that a way.﴾

Ikrimah, al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatadah likewise said: this verse was revealed concerning the recitation in prayer.

Shu'bah narrated from Ash'ath ibn Abi Sulaym [[In H and T: "from Abu Sulaym." The adopted reading is from al-Tabari.]], from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Ibn Mas'ud: "It is not silent therein if one makes his own ears hear it."

Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub narrated to us, Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn 'Alqamah, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was informed that Abu Bakr, when he prayed and recited, would lower his voice, and that 'Umar would raise his voice. It was said to Abu Bakr: Why do you do this? He said: I am conversing with my Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, and He knows my need. It was said: You have done well. It was said to 'Umar: Why do you do this? He said: I drive away the devil and wake the drowsy. It was said: You have done well. When the verse was revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾, it was said to Abu Bakr: Raise your voice a little, and it was said to 'Umar: Lower your voice a little. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/124).]]

Ash'ath ibn Sawwar said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: it was revealed concerning supplication (du'a'). Similarly, al-Thawri and Malik narrated from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah: it was revealed concerning supplication. Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu 'Iyad, Makhul and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Al-Thawri said, from [Ibn] [[Addition from F.]] 'Ayyash al-'Amiri, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, who said: Some Bedouins of the Banu Tamim, when the Prophet ﷺ finished (the prayer) with the salam, would say: "O Allah, grant us camels and children." He said: So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein.﴾

Another view: Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that this verse was revealed concerning the tashahhud: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein.﴾

Hafs said likewise, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, the same.

Another view: 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, that he said: Do not pray for the sake of showing off to people, and do not abandon it out of fear of people. al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from al-Hasan al-Basri: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: Do not beautify its outward appearance while spoiling its inward state. 'Abd al-Razzaq likewise narrated it from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, with this wording; Hushaym from 'Awf, from him, with this; and Sa'id from Qatadah, from him, similarly.

Another view: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning His saying: ﴿but seek between that a way﴾, he said: The People of the Book would speak in a low voice, then one of them would raise his voice with a letter and cry out, and they would cry out behind him. So He forbade him to cry out as these do, and to be silent as these people are silent. Then the way that lies between that is what Gabriel prescribed for him in prayer.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion﴾, when He, may He be exalted, affirmed for His noble self the most beautiful names, He declared Himself free of deficiencies, saying: ﴿And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness.﴾ Rather, He is Allah, the One, the Self-Sufficient (al-Samad), who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is comparable.

﴿Nor has He any protector out of weakness﴾, that is: He is not weak, so as to need a protector, a helper, or a counsellor. Rather, He, may He be exalted [[Addition from A.]], is the sole Creator of things with no partner, and the sole Determiner and Manager of them by His will, with no partner.

Mujahid said concerning His saying: ﴿Nor has He any protector out of weakness﴾: He does not form an alliance with anyone, nor does He seek the help of anyone.

﴿And magnify Him with great magnificence﴾, that is: exalt Him and glorify Him above what the wrongdoers and transgressors say, with great exaltation.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Abu Sakhr informed me, from al-Qurazi, that he used to say concerning this verse: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son…﴾ up to the end of the verse. He said: The Jews and the Christians said: Allah has taken a son. The Arabs said: [Labbayka] [[Addition from F.]] Labbayka, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You own him and what he owns. The Sabians and the Magians said: Were it not for the friends of Allah, He would be humiliated. So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with great magnificence.﴾

He also said: Bishr narrated to us, [Yazid narrated to us] [[Addition from T, F, A.]], Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ used to teach his family this verse: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with great magnificence,﴾ to the young and the old among them.

I say: It has come in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named it the verse of honour (ayat al-'izz) [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/440) from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Anas, raised to the Prophet: "The verse of honour: 'Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son…' the whole verse."]], and in some reports: that it is not recited in a house on a night when theft or calamity would befall it. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Bishr ibn Sayhan al-Basri narrated to us, Harb ibn Maymun narrated to us, Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, my hand in his hand, and he came upon a man in shabby condition, and he said: "O so-and-so, what has brought you to what I see?" He said: Sickness and harm, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Shall I not teach you words that will remove from you sickness and harm?" He said: No. He said: It would not please me to have them, even if I had been present with you at Badr or Uhud. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed and said: "Do the people of Badr and the people of Uhud attain what the poor, contented one attains?" He said: Abu Hurayrah then said: O Messenger of Allah, teach them to me. He said: "Say, O Abu Hurayrah: 'I place my trust in the Living One who does not die. Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son, and has had no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness, and magnify Him with great magnificence.'" He said: Then the Messenger of Allah came to me, and my condition had improved. He said to me: "Mah-yam?" [[In T: "Upon him be the blessing."]] I said: O Messenger of Allah, I have not ceased saying the words you taught me. [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (12/23). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/52): "It contains Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak."]]

Its chain is weak, and its text contains an unusual element. [And Allah knows best.] [[Addition from F, A. In T: "End of the tafsir of Surat al-Isra'. Praise and grace belong to Allah; with Him is success and protection. May Allah forgive its copyist, those who read it, his parents, his teachers, and all the Muslims, all of them. Amin."]]
